feature.name: Primordial Element Trait
feature.text:
At 14th level, you gain a feature from your Primordial Element.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 83 (Indie)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a feat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Fusion Master
feature.text:
Starting at 18th level, you no longer need to have cast an elemental spell before casting a fusion spell, and you don't need to keep track of the elements of the spells you cast.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a feat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Elemental Pinnacle
feature.text:
At 20th level, for the next minute after casting a spell, you become immune to a type of damage based on the last spell you cast according to the next table.

Elemental Pinnacle:
Element | Immunity
Air or Lightning | Lightning
Earth or Plant | Acid
Fire or Lava | Fire
Water or Spirit | Cold

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Primordial Element: Air Primordial Element
feature.text:
Elementalists connected to this Primordial Element are usually strongly linked to freedom, deception, mobility, and dexterity. By choosing Air as your Primordial Element you can learn Air, Water, and Fire spells, the latter two being your secondary elements, and you will know the fusion element spells of Lightning and Spirit.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Wind Wisdom (Air Primordial Element)
feature.text:
Starting at 1st level, the liberty and adaptability of the air bestow you with new skills. You gain proficiency with two skills of your choice from Acrobatics, Deception, Persuasion, and Stealth. Additionally, you gain the ability to use the Disengage and Hide actions as a bonus action, and reduce the height of any fall by 30 feet when calculating falling damage.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Swift and Graceful (Air Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 6th level, you gain proficiency in Dexterity saving throws, have advantage on initiative rolls, and your ranged spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarter cover.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Soul of the Wind (Air Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 10th level, your bond with air allows you to fly. You gain a flying speed that equals your walking speed.
	Additionally, as a bonus action, you can become invisible for a minute or until you make an attack or cast a spell. You can use this ability once, regaining its use after a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Air Body (Air Primordial Element)
feature.text:
Starting at 14th level, you can use your bonus action to channel the energy of air and become ethereal for 1 minute. This enables you to move through spaces occupied by obstructions and creatures without penalty, and move without provoking attacks of opportunity. For the duration, you also gain resistance to all non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, and immunity to the grappled condition. You cannot use this feature again until you complete a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 84 (Indie)

feature.name: Primordial Element: Earth Primordial Element
feature.text:
Elementalists who choose this Primordial Element are strongly linked to law, resolution, stability, and strength. By choosing Earth as your Primordial Element, you can learn Earth, Water, and Fire spells, with the latter two being your secondary elements, and you will know the fusion element spells of Lava and Plant.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 86 (Indie)

feature.name: Grounded Learnings (Earth Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 1st level, the endurance and stability of Earth grant you new abilities. You gain proficiency with two skills of your choice from Athletics, History, and Survival. Your hit point maximum increases by 1 at the first level, and by an additional 1 each time you gain an elementalist level. When not wearing any armor or shield, your Armor Class is determined as 10 + your Constitution modifier + your Wisdom modifier, replacing the usual Dexterity modifier.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 86 (Indie)

feature.name: Earth Sense (Earth Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 6th level, your bond with the earth allows you to sense its shapes and forms. You gain a tremorsense with a range of 30 feet. Additionally, as a bonus action, you can emit a harmless shockwave, identifying all terrains, walls, doors, passages, objects, and creatures within a 90-foot radius and pinpointing their exact locations. This ability can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus plus your Wisdom modifier, regaining all when you finish after a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 86 (Indie)

feature.name: Earth Shield (Earth Primordial Element)
feature.text:
Starting at 10th level, if you are not surprised, you can take a reaction to form a rock shield in response to an attack or a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw. This stone shield provides a bonus to your AC and saves equal to your Wisdom modifier, lasting until the start of your next turn. This ability can be used twice, regaining all uses when you finish a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 86 (Indie)

feature.name: Tomb of Invulnerability (Earth Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 14th level, when targeted or affected by an attack, spell, or any effect except divine intervention, you can use your reaction to manifest an invincible stone tomb for protection. Weighing 12,000 pounds, this tomb is impervious to all but divine intervention. Inside the tomb, you are immune to all damage and any physical, mental, or magical effects. However, you also become incapacitated, unable to perform actions, reactions, bonus actions, speak, or issue mental commands. No communication can penetrate the tomb, but you retain your tremorsense, with its range extended to 120 feet within the tomb.
	You can choose to end this effect at the start of each turn, causing the tomb to dematerialize instantly. Any effects or conditions affecting you prior to entering the tomb are suspended while inside, nullifying their effects but also halting their duration. Inside the tomb, you are unaffected by hunger, thirst, and don't need to breathe, but you continue aging normally. It is not possible to take rests within the tomb. This feature can't be used again until you complete a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 86 (Indie)

feature.name: Primordial Element: Fire Primordial Element
feature.text:
Elementalists who choose this Primordial Element are strongly linked to battles, creativity, destruction, and intelligence. By choosing Fire as your Primordial Element, you can learn Fire, Air, and Earth spells, the latter two being your secondary elements, and you will know the fusion element spells of Lava and Lightning.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Flame Brilliance (Fire Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 1st level, the creativity and cunning of fire afford you new abilities. You gain proficiency with two skills of your choice from Intimidation, Investigation, and Performance. You also gain proficiency with light armor, shields, and simple weapons. You can cast your elementalist spells even when your hands are holding weapons or shields, performing the necessary gestures to cast them.
	When wielding a weapon, your melee weapon attack rolls can use your Wisdom modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity. This modifier also applies to damage rolls from the 6th level.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Fiery Reprisal (Fire Primordial Element)
feature.text:
Starting at 6th level, when you are the target of an attack, you can take a reaction to make a melee weapon attack against an enemy within range.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Burning Inspiration (Fire Primordial Element)
feature.text:
Starting at 10th level, you can use your connection with Fire to inspire your allies. As a bonus action, you can imbue yourself and all allies within 30 feet of you with the power of flames, granting them an extra 1d6 fire damage to all unarmed, weapon, or spell attacks. This effect lasts for 1 minute. After using this ability, you can't use it again until you complete a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Second Surge (Fire Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 14th level, when using a spell slot to augment your elemental surge cantrip, you can use this cantrip again on the next turn, as an action, as if you had spent a spell slot one level lower.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Primordial Element: Water Primordial Element
feature.text:
Elementalists who choose this Primordial Element are strongly attached to peace, tradition, restoration, and wisdom. By choosing water as your Primordial Element you can learn Water, Air and Earth spells, the latter two being your secondary elements, and you will know the fusion element spells of Plant and Spirit.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Water Teachings (Water Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 1st level, the tradition and wisdom of water enable you to gain new abilities. You gain proficiency with two skills of your choice from Medicine, Nature, and Religion.
	Additionally, each time you cast an elementalist spell that heals a creature, you can also heal another creature up to 60 feet away, provided it was not healed by the original spell. The creature healed through this trait regains 1d6 hit points per level of the spell used.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Flowing Water (Water Primordial Element)
feature.text:
Starting at 6th level, your understanding of the life-sustaining flow of water allows you to adapt to adversity. While conscious and not wearing armor or wielding a shield, your Wisdom modifier is added to all saving throws you make, in addition to any other applicable modifiers.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Purifying Rain (Water Primordial Element)
feature.text:
Starting at 10th level, as a bonus action, you can call forth a 30-foot radius rainstorm at a point up to 240 feet away, lasting for 1 minute. Upon activating this ability, you and your allies within the area recover 2d8 hit points each, and any conditions, diseases, or curses affecting them are removed.
	For the duration, you and your allies in the area have advantage on all saving throws. This ability has no effect on undead and constructs. After using this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

feature.name: Healing Tide (Water Primordial Element)
feature.text:
At 14th level, you can unleash the healing powers of water in a surge of vitality. As a bonus action, you create a 60-foot emanation around you that lasts for 1 minute. During this time, you and all creatures who finish their turn within the area recover hit points equal to your elementalist level.
	Additionally, any healing spells cast on a creature within the area recover extra hit points equal to your elementalist level. This ability has no effect on undead and constructs. After using this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 87 (Indie)

trait.name: Elementalist
trait.text:
In a serene garden, a wise elementalist master prepares tea for its disciples with the utmost precision, their every movement harmoniously aligned with the elements. As the tea leaves dance in the boiling water, the disciples sense a deep connection to the elements, feeling the master's power coursing through their veins.
	When confronted by ruthless bandits, a soulborn elementalist commands the elements with a flick of their wrist, unleashing an icy beam of pure energy that encases half of the bandits in a frozen tomb while the rest flee in terror.
	Against a monstrous beast, an elf elementalist stands resolute, igniting their weapons and those of their allies with blazing magic. Confidence burns within them as they prepare for an epic battle, ready to vanquish the darkness with the raw power of the elements.
	Elementalists are versatile and wise spellcasters who serve as advisors, sages, spiritual guides, and teachers. According to prophecies, they hold the power to stop Gullog and his undead armies.
	Born from an ancestral elven tradition, elementalists stand as a distinct group of spellcasters. Their mastery diverges from conventional arcane practices, delving into the harmonization of elements, energy flow, meditation, and spiritual enlightenment. These wise practitioners dedicate their lives to attuning with one of the four elements, each of which grants distinctive abilities and purpose. Fire elementalists command martial prowess and emotional control, earth elementalists foster unwavering resilience and deep moral compass, air elementalists exhibit cunning, guile, and grace of movement, while the scarce water elementalists practice healing arts, nurturing both body and soul, and advocating temperance and non-attachment. Despite mastering one element, elementalists can manipulate the other two elements that do not directly conflict with their chosen one, enabling combinations of elements to cast spells of magma, plant, lightning, and spiritual magic, and augmenting their vast repertoire.
	The elementalist's path is a lifelong odyssey built upon the master-disciple relationship. With unwavering commitment, the disciple studies, contemplates, and serves under their master, acquiring elemental wisdom and proper conduct. Years of labor and ordinary tasks precede the true awakening to the powers of Elementalism, as masters cautiously evaluate their disciples' character before bestowing such knowledge. This bond endures for life, underpinned by duty, respect, and honor. Disciples must venerate and assist their masters throughout their lives, undertaking tasks as required and ensuring their actions never tarnish their master's name. Concurrently, masters are obligated to impart wisdom, safeguard their disciples, and foster their spiritual growth, with any abuse constituting great dishonor.
	Elementalists regard their fellow practitioners as kin, despite differing principles and views among schools devoted to various elements. They engage in fervent debates, never overstepping the bounds of theological, philosophical, and metaphysical discourse. Their relationships with other magic users are intricate, often considering wizards and sorcerers untrustworthy due to their immense powers without requisite wisdom and moral enlightenment. However, those displaying tempered conduct and good character are highly esteemed. Clerics earn respect for their devotion and moral code, but their potential fanaticism incites wariness, whereas druids are perceived as kindred spirits, embracing a more primal yet venerable approach to wisdom.
	In the world of Tanares, an ominous threat looms as the immortal kemet leader, Gullog, seeks to conquer and turn all into icy death. Elementalists are at the heart of a prophecy that may provide salvation, seeing themselves as responsible for restoring the goddess Bás to her pacifist ways and ending Gullog's tyranny. Beyond the prophecy, elementalists serve as spiritual guides, royal advisors, and guardians of elemental energies. Guided by the teachings of venerable masters and their respected schools and enclaves, elementalists confront Tanares' challenges with the perspective of ancient wisdom.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 78 (Indie)

trait.name: History of Elementalism
trait.text:
Within the time-worn tomes of Tanares, the tale of the elven kin is woven in intricate prose. Once thriving in a realm of unmatched beauty, the elves had their world shattered by the apocalyptic fury of their own goddess, Bás. Spurred by the heinous deeds of the malefic Ungods, her rage laid waste to the once-pristine elven lands. Amidst the frozen ruins, the remnants of the elves sought sanctuary in Tanares, guided by the wisdom of their remaining divine trinity.
	In their newfound haven, the divine triad endowed the elven people with the mystical knowledge of Elementalism, an art that would serve as their salvation and guide their path in the new world. Entwined within this sacred gift, a prophecy unfurled, foretelling the inexorable return of the vengeful Bás and the darkness she would bring upon Tanares.
	As the elves' prowess in Elementalism blossomed, they clung steadfastly to the hallowed teachings, safeguarding the ancestral secrets within their sanctified enclaves and revered schools. Their vigilance endured, ever-alert for the encroaching shadow of Bás's dreaded return.
	As the Evolutionist Church's hold on arcane magic intensified, their ranks infiltrated by Ungod cultists, Elementalism arose as a free and unshackled alternative. The Ungods took little notice of the elementalists, leaving them to hone their craft in peace while manipulating the persecution of wizards and sorcerers. Thus, the elves disseminated their knowledge among diverse species, nurturing a thriving community of elementalists across Tanares.
	Over the ages, water elementalism, once an esteemed elven tradition, dwindled as the winter elves forsook it in pursuit of dark prophecies that transformed them into the kemet people. The remaining elemental arts thrived, providing a substitute for arcane magic. New institutions were founded, as practitioners plumbed the depths of ancient texts, meditated, and performed rites to fortify their bonds with the elements. Their wisdom, echoing the ancient philosophies, became a coveted treasure for rulers, strategists, nobles, and merchants alike. In time, their enclaves, schools, and sects evolved into bastions of enlightenment and erudition.
	During the Kemet Invasion, the Tanares Empire's strength waned considerably. The kemets, under Gullog's command, invaded Tanares to fulfill Golgöggoth's scheme to strip mortals of their emotions, rendering them impervious to Ungod corruption. Though the combined forces of Tanares vanquished Gullog and the kemets, Bás resurfaced, reviving Gullog and forging an alliance with Golgöggoth to transform Tanares into a frozen, undead wasteland akin to the lost elven realm.
	With the ancient prophecy of Bás's return now unfolding, the elementalists must confront the trials posed by Bás and Gullog. The scarcity of water elementalists has led their enclaves to prioritize training new adepts, for it is believed that masters of all four elements are essential in facing Bás.
	As they ready themselves for the impending darkness, the timeless wisdom and deep connections of these exceptional spellweavers will forge the fate of Tanares.

trait.name: Elementalism and the Ungods
trait.text:
Elementalists, ever vigilant against the malevolent forces of the Ungods, always aware of the fate of the worlds taken by their corruption, dedicate themselves to thwarting these ancient beings and their wicked schemes. Knowing what happened to the elven world, elementalists recognize the price of failure and commit to safeguarding Tanares from a similar fate.
	Guided by the teachings of venerable masters, elementalists wield the elements to counter the myriad threats posed by the Ungods. They relentlessly confront the hidden servants who sow discord among mortals and battle the penumbral creatures that lurk in the shadows, seeking to breach into the Material Plane. Elementalists tirelessly work to prevent wars and unrest among factions, as they know that such conflicts only serve to empower the Ungods and hasten their nefarious plans.
	Air elementalists, cunning and acrobatic, infiltrate the hidden networks of the Ungods' servants. They disrupt the corrupt machinations from within, shielding the innocent from the clutches of the Cult of Shadow Wing. Earth elementalists, resolute and steadfast, stand guard over sacred places of power, preventing the Ungods from seizing these elemental energy sources. Fire elementalists, with their martial prowess, ignite the hearts of those who would defy the Ungods, inspiring them to resist the encroaching darkness. Water elementalists, rare and sagacious, offer healing and wisdom to those tainted by the Ungods' influence, cleansing them of corruption.
	To strengthen their ranks, elementalists endeavor to educate and inspire others in the ways of elementalism. Through rigorous training and the sharing of wisdom, they prepare new generations to battle the forces of the Ungods and avert the apocalyptic doom that befell their world. They instill a sense of duty, honor, and respect, nurturing lifelong bonds between master and disciple. Thus, the lineage of elemental wisdom endures, perpetually growing stronger.
	Elementalists draw upon the wisdom of their ancestral masters, forging a connection to ancient traditions and spiritual disciplines. Through long seclusions, rigorous study, and intense training, they become dignified forebears, their practices evoking a sense of time-honored tradition and spiritual commitment. They are ever vigilant against the encroachment of the Ungods' influence, striving to preserve the delicate balance of the world.

trait.name: The Return of Bás
trait.text:
The elementalists hold the Cuibhle pantheon in the highest regard, venerating the elven gods as the wisest ancestors and elemental masters. Breith, god of spring and earth; Òigridh, goddess of summer and fire; Aibidh, god of autumn and air; and Bás, once the gentle goddess of winter and death, are believed to spin the wheel of life in an eternal dance.
	Bás, though lost to wrath and vengeance, remains an ancient master of elementalists. Her heart turned cold, and her vision clouded by hatred for the Ungods, so the elementalists do not seek her destruction, but rather her redemption. They liken her to the calm and raging oceans, her actions reflecting the duality of the elemental forces.
	Her alliance with Gullog and Golgöggoth, the Augur, unveiled chilling plans for an icy wasteland free of life, making the world immune to the Ungods' corruption. Bás's goal is a twisted version of her once noble purpose, and the elementalists are integral in halting her descent. Air elementalists disrupt the freezing winds, earth elementalists stand against the encroaching frost, fire elementalists combat the cold with their passion, and water elementalists, critical to restoring balance, strive to heal and rejuvenate the land, countering Bás's icy grasp.
	Rumors suggest that the most ancient elves, direct disciples of the gods themselves, have returned from seclusion following Bás's reemergence. They purportedly carry knowledge of three divine artifacts, imbued with the essence of the gods of Summer, Autumn, and Spring, holding the key to swaying Bás and guiding her back to her pacifist ways. These enigmatic masters are believed to be seeking new apprentices to aid in the journey to stop Bás once and for all.

trait.name: The four paths of Elementalism
trait.text:
Elementalism The sacred art of Elementalism, passed down through generations of masters, manifests in four distinct paths, each reflecting the unique characteristics, tendencies, and worldviews of the elements themselves.
	Air Elementalists, known for their free-spirited and perceptive nature, embody the ephemeral essence of the wind. Their training emphasizes cunning, agility, and the art of deception. Through meditation and practice, these elementalists gain the ability to move with the swiftness of the breeze and even defy gravity. They find solace in tea-making, music, and exploration. When not in their schools, they often join merchant or adventuring groups as wandering masters, preferring to avoid conflict, but navigating challenges with cunning and quick thinking when necessary.
	Earth Elementalists, the bastions of stability and tradition, resonate with the unyielding resilience of stone. Their connection to the earth grants them an unparalleled awareness of its vibrations and mysteries. Often dedicating themselves to matters such as law, architecture, and history, they record the past and present through intricate calligraphy and poetic prose. They may find purpose in bureaucratic positions, state administration, or roles that maintain order, and while they will rarely start conflicts, they are the last to back down.
	Fire Elementalists, fueled by passion and prowess, wield both martial arts and elemental fire in a harmonious dance of destruction and creation. Their training encompasses the mastery of weapons, shields, and close combat. Many who leave their conclaves embark on the path of the soldier, mercenary, or adventurer, seeking wisdom and growth through the heat of battle. They inspire greatness in allies and are the most charismatic of all the elementalists.
	Water Elementalists, rare and nearly lost, have experienced a resurgence as the ancient art of healing and restoration is rediscovered. These wise scholars and empathetic healers possess an unparalleled understanding of life energy, allowing them to mend wounds and protect themselves from harm. They often serve as healers, physicians, counselors, and sages, sharing their wisdom and serenity with those in need. Their patience is formidable, but when pushed to the limit, their wrath is as powerful as a raging ocean.
	Each elementalist path reflects the unique teachings and focus of their respective masters, who guide their apprentices in the ways of their chosen element. Despite their elemental differences, all elementalists share a profound sense of unity and respect for one another. As the world faces the dark threat of Bás and the Forces of Darkall, the elementalists of Tanares stands united.

trait.name: Creating an Elementalist
trait.text:
When creating an elementalist, you must define how do you belong in Elementalism. What is your role? Which element represents you? Do you agree with its precepts? Are you an ally of a group or hermit elementalist? Why are you an adventurer? What do you seek in the world?
	After that, you must also define which characteristics (if any) from your element you carry in your behavior and personality. Are you a passional, fiery person, or are you stubborn like a rock? Or, even if you are connected to a certain element, is your personality more aligned to a different one? These questions define your character's goals, and how it will work to achieve them.

fields.name: Madwalker (Tanares)
fields.proficiency: Dexterity, Charisma, Acrobatics, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Perception, Stealth, Survival

trait.name: Madwalker
trait.text:
I n the Penumbral Plane, a dwarf crawls inside a nest of arachnid aberrations. Swarmed by monsters, he easily shrugs off their attacks. When he finally sees the queen, the dwarf shapeshifts into an arachne himself and handily defeats his opponent.
	While fighting in an Arena match, a gnome makes an aberrant tentacle grow from his back. Using it to cross a pit with a series of acrobatic moves, he lands right by his enemies. Grinning, he grapples his opponents with the tentacle and throws them one by one into the pit, ensuring his Team's victory.
	A human is pursued by the Ironhand. Her crime? Existing. As she is surrounded by guards, a pair of twisted wings sprout from her back. She takes flight and leaves town, knowing that on her back are not only tentacles or wings, but a target.
	Shadowy and agile guides and hunters of the Penumbral Plane who hate penumbral creatures. They wield aberrant powers, but at the cost of their sanity, walking a thin line between power and madness.
	The madwalkers, survivors of the Penumbral Plane's malevolent embrace, are individuals forever marked by their terrifying experiences with abominations spawned by the vile influence of the Ungods. Their fractured minds bear the scars of unspeakable horrors, yet they have harnessed the dark energies of the Penumbra to exact retribution upon the loathsome progeny of the Ungods. Their mastery of this mysterious force and the resilience forged in the depths of their insanity makes them formidable champions in the eternal struggle against the encroaching darkness.
	To earn the powers of a madwalker, an initiate must undergo a terrifying rite of passage, confronting and vanquishing either Watchers or arachnes, before attuning to their essence by absorbing their power. Occasionally, this transformation transpires spontaneously when individuals seeking vengeance become trapped within the Penumbral Plane, fighting for their lives and slaying aberrant creatures to survive. However, a knowledgeable mentor can shepherd the initiate through this process, enabling them to deliberately overcome their monstrous adversaries, assimilate their energy, and assume the mantle of a madwalker.
	The source of a madwalker's power determines their abilities and the path they tread. The Nightmare's Augury Trail, achieved by hunting and assimilating the essence of a servant of Golgöggoth, the Augur and master of the Watchers, grants madwalkers foresight and exceptional mental fortitude, as well as daunting defensive prowess. Conversely, the Aberrant Arachinid Trail, obtained by hunting and assimilating the essence of an arachnid servant of Bellera, the Ungods' progeny, bestows upon madwalkers unmatched hunting expertise, empowering them to orchestrate lethal ambushes and wield potent toxins against their prey.
	Ostracized by society as deranged and tainted, madwalkers dwell on the fringes of civilization. Yet their unique ability to withstand the Penumbra's insidious corruption, navigate its treacherous landscapes, and confront its dark horrors with lethal precision make them invaluable allies to mighty kingdoms and influential organizations.
	Delving into the abyss of their own madness, madwalkers manifest their innermost nightmares in corporeal form. At the zenith of their insanity, they can temporarily assume the guise of a penumbral monstrosity, granting them immense power. However, this metamorphosis demands a terrible price, leaving them enfeebled in its aftermath.
	The madwalker's journey is a precarious balancing act between their humanity and the source of their power — the insanity that threatens to consume them. They navigate a treacherous path fraught with daunting challenges as they strive to maintain their sanity while wielding the unfettered power of their nightmares. Those who master this power can unleash a force beyond the comprehension of mere mortals.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 138 (Indie)

trait.name: Madwalker History
trait.text:
In the shadowy annals of Tanares' history, the genesis of the madwalkers traces back to the Ancient Age, a bygone era where intrepid mortals dared to probe the enigmatic Penumbral Plane. These forays, aimed at combating the ceaseless menace of penumbral monstrosities, were often led by individuals fueled by vengeance against the insidious offspring of the Ungods. As they ventured into the twisted depths of this Penumbral Plane, these tormented souls were tainted and driven to the brink of insanity by confrontations with grotesque, aberrant horrors. Only a sparse few of those who endured and narrowly evaded becoming aberrations themselves were left so irrevocably warped that they were transformed into the first madwalkers.
	As the sands of time relentlessly marched forward, these enigmatic warriors fractured into two factions, each drawn to disparate sources of power. One faction pursued the malignant might of the Arachnes, malevolent minions of the Ungods, believing that mastering their adversaries' power would bring about ultimate retribution. The other faction yearned for the essence of the Watchers, fallen angels in servitude to Golgöggoth, the Augur. These tainted beings could defy the Ungods' servants, their energy morphing into a formidable weapon.
	These factions harbored disdain for one another, each unwavering in their conviction of their chosen path's dominance. Arachnid madwalkers derided the Augury faction as feeble, incapable of withstanding corruption. Conversely, Augury madwalkers loathed utilizing their enemies' power, contending that the Watchers' essence is more closely aligned with their righteous, vengeful crusade.
	Throughout the history, madwalkers were cast out as tainted pariahs, yet they persisted on the fringes of society, lurking in Tanares' penumbral recesses to hunt the abominations they swore to annihilate. For centuries, the Evolutionist Church, ensnared in the Ungods' duplicitous web, pursued the madwalkers as heretics. This persecution persisted through the dark and grim Fallen Age until the dawning of the Imperial Age.
	A recent turning tide came when several resurgent angels unveiled the gods' true intentions, unmasking the Ungods' deceit inside the Evolutionist Church. This revelation sparked the transformation of the Church into the Celestianist Church, which began to perceive madwalkers as potential allies. The Awakened, an elite monster-hunting order within the Church, incorporated numerous madwalkers, bolstering their ranks and elevating their status in the ongoing struggle against the Ungods.

trait.name: Fighting Madness with Madness
trait.text:
with Madness The madwalkers hold the ability to harness the chaotic essence of their fragmented psyche, channeling the eldritch terrors of the Penumbra as potent weapons. These tainted warriors stand unbowed in the relentless battle against the festering malignancy that lurks deep within the world's core. Bound to the Penumbra by the torment of their shattered minds, madwalkers possess an innate sense for detecting penumbral beings, portals, and rifts, allowing them to relentlessly pursue their prey through the darkest recesses of existence.
	Masterful madwalkers wield the power to conjure temporary penumbral rifts—interdimensional gateways that forge a tenuous connection between the nightmarish realm and the Material Plane. This unparalleled mastery makes them invaluable allies in the age-old struggle against the dreaded Ungods, as they can skillfully enter or exit the Penumbral Plane to confront the eldritch horrors that lie hidden within.
	However, the Penumbra's power demands a dire sacrifice. Madwalkers teeter precariously on the brink between the fragile bounds of sanity and the unfathomable abyss of madness. In moments of utmost desperation, a madwalker may choose to embrace their darkest nightmares, undergoing a horrifying transfiguration into a fearsome penumbral monstrosity. This metamorphosis allows them to assume the form of one of the many penumbral creatures, such as emoguns, Watchers, or even arachnes, depending on their source of power. In doing so, they gain immense strength and resilience, but at the perilous cost of potentially succumbing to the Penumbra's all-consuming lunacy

trait.name: The Whispers of the Penumbral Plane
trait.text:
Penumbral Plane In the uncharted depths of the cosmos, where the mortal realm's influence wanes, lies the Penumbral Plane. This eldritch and twisted dimension, born of the corruption wrought by the vile Ungods, unfurls into six distinct layers—each a haunting echo of a plane devoured by the Ungods' insatiable hunger for planar domination. This realm teems with macabre denizens, including insidious cultists, tainted penumbral dragons, and distorted emoguns—sullied souls of mortals whose dying hearts were consumed by sins and darkness.
	The Surface is cloaked in an enigmatic shroud of mists, reflecting a warped simulacrum of Tanares, and ruled by the enigmatic penumbral dragons. The mists possess a potent corruptive power, and even the most deranged madwalkers steer clear of this forsaken place. Numerous cavern entrances and pathways offer temporary refuge from the mists and the dreadful penumbral dragons that hunt the skies above.
	The Eternal Cathedral, the first layer of the Penumbra, extends infinitely as a vast, shadowy sanctuary. Once sacred, it now echoes with the whispers of the damned. Filled with crumbling altars, toppled statues, and rotting libraries, this formerly holy realm is ruled by Gideoni, the fallen High Cardinal of the Evolutionist Church, now leader of the Cult of Shadow Wing and the chosen of The Mystical One. Commanding legions of devout cultists and emoguns driven by fear and pain, Gideoni's power casts a dark pall over the cathedral.
	Delving deeper, the Caverns of the Magma Giants sprawl as a labyrinthine network of colossal tunnels and chambers, riddled with rivers and lakes of molten lava. Amidst the ruins of forgotten cities and fortresses, constructed by powerful and thriftless giants, now reside emoguns empowered by wrath and gluttony, alongside other twisted beasts spawned by the Fleshspawner himself. Ardillog, the Everspawning Chimera, watches over this fiery domain with a vigilant eye, ever prepared to be summoned to the material plane at its bestial master's behest.
	Descending further, the Crystal Forest emerges. Within its gleaming, narrow tunnels and cavernous expanses, one encounters crystalline flora that shimmer and resonate with eerie vibrations, all filled with spider webs. Bellara, mistress of this crystalline expanse, leads an army of arachnes and emoguns that feed on grudge and pride; they hide in the webs, ready to hunt the unwary.
	The Endless City, the fourth layer, sprawls across a desolate expanse the size of a continent. This once-grand world-sized metropolis now lies in ruin, its narrow streets, alleys, and decrepit buildings overtaken by shadows. Catharina, servant of the Lady of Sins, presides over this decayed realm, conspiring with Bellara as they command covens of Purple Witches and powerful hags that transform entire sections of the ancient city into swampy lands filled with sewage water, mutated rats, and emoguns spawned by lust and disgust, ensnaring invaders with illusions and enticing their curiosity to curse them with hexes.
	Treading deeper still, the Clock Level reveals itself as an endless array of bronze gears and mechanisms, its passages opening and closing with clockwork precision, creating a labyrinth of gears, levers, and shifting walls. The emoguns here rejoice on sloth and sadness, wandering this domain. Ruled by the First Queen, the ancient hive mother of the Kikoku, her swarm hides in all crevices of the endless gears that form this level, ready to attack or seize control of the many ancient bronze constructs and assail invaders in the territory of their Queen.
	At last, the Inverted Archives await. Within this enigmatic realm where gravity is inverted and ancient library rooms are connected only through one-way metallic mirrors that serve as portals, the Dark Collector, master of this domain, presides over a group of sinister hoarders who have succumbed to corruption; they command all penumbral creatures in the archives, which teem with emoguns that prey on greed and envy.
	Sparse respite can be found in this dark realm, with a few Dragon Council Towers hidden in secure places across the different levels, a handful of rare gloomfolk tribes that maintain small territories for themselves, and a few surviving collectors that have resisted corruption. These small and elusive individuals are difficult to communicate with, as they are more likely to flee than to engage in conversation or combat. However, they may offer refuge to those who are gravely weakened or visibly wounded.

trait.name: The Madwalkers and the World
trait.text:
The enigmatic madwalkers tread a path shrouded in mystery and fear, their existence once maligned by the zealous crusade of the dominant Evolutionist Church. In the wake of scandals unveiling the Ungods' corruption within the Church's core, the reformed Celestianist Church has adopted a more subtle stance, tolerating the madwalkers while withholding public support as it labors to restore its tarnished reputation.
	The madwalkers' minds, frayed by their connection to the ominous penumbral beings, inspire disquiet among the populace who tremble before their unnerving abilities and unsettling visage. Yet, it is this very instability that grants them the power to empathize with those whose sanity has been ravaged by the abominations of the Penumbral Plane, extracting invaluable knowledge where others flounder.
	Possessing a singular, twisted perspective, they devise tactics and strategies that confound even the most brilliant of minds. This uncanny ability to discern hidden patterns renders the most exceptional madwalkers highly sought after by organizations and kingdoms seeking to shatter conventional paradigms with groundbreaking insights.
	As they navigate the cities of Tanares, madwalkers are ever mindful of the need for discretion. They cloak themselves in shadows, acutely aware that common folk can sense the disturbing penumbral aura that envelops them.
	In the forsaken outskirts, where society's outcasts huddle together, madwalkers find a semblance of solace. Amidst these dark fringes, they escape the judging eyes of the people, forging a tenuous sense of belonging in a world that would otherwise cast them aside. Their shared experience of being pariahs nurtures a sense of brotherhood among them, while their similarly warped minds exchange ideas through fleeting glances and subtle gestures that only they can comprehend.
	To earn a living, many madwalkers hunt penumbral creatures, presenting their slain quarry to the Dragon Towers as evidence of their victories and claiming bounties offered by the Draconic Council. Although the pervasive fear surrounding them stifles any hope for public acclaim or positions of influence, a select few madwalkers maintain an artful facade, concealing their true nature as they excel in their chosen fields. These few can become powerful nobles, seen as eccentric by others, and are able to fund and provide protection to many aspiring madwalkers.
	Simultaneously, factions entangled in Tanares' cold war covet the singular prowess of the madwalkers, enlisting them as assassins and infiltrators in covert operations. Their actions reverberate throughout the societies they traverse, bearing far-reaching consequences.

trait.name: Creating a Madwalker
trait.text:
To create a madwalker character, start by deciding how you became a madwalker. What brought you to the plane of nightmares? How you acquired your powers, you had a mentor or you survived alone the horrors of the plane of nightmares?
Did you seek out its power, or were you pulled in by accident?
How your newfound abilities and your changed mental state affected your daily life, and what sort of relationship do you have with the people from your past?
	In addition to backstory, it's important to consider your madwalker's personality. Are they playful and mischievous, or dark and brooding? Do they revel in their powers or feel a sense of guilt and responsibility for what they can do?
	Finally, think about how your madwalker fits into the larger world. Do they have allies or enemies who know about their powers? Are they hunted by those who fear their abilities, or sought after by those who desire their power? Why are you adventuring? Vengeance against an evil being, desire for power and wealth, or for some other personal reason?

In Other Settings:
As long as there are nightmares in your setting, a madwalker can tap into its oneiric fabric and embody its creations; it is therefore not only possible, but easy, to play as a madwalker in other settings. Even though only a few minor powers of a madwalker relate to the Penumbral Plane, many other settings have similar dark or astral environments that you can treat as if they were the madwalker's penumbra, such as the Shadowfell.

feature.name: Starting Madwalker
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Madwalker, you begin play with 8 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.

	• Armor: Light armor
	• Weapons: Simple weapons, martial weapons
	• Tools: Thieves' tools
	• Saving Throws: Dexterity, Charisma
	• Skills: Choose three from Acrobatics, Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Perception, Stealth, and Survival

You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.

	• (a) a rapier or (b) a longsword
	• (a) a longbow and a quiver with 20 arrows or (b) a shortsword
	• (a) an adventurer's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
	• Two daggers and thieves' tools

If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 4d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 142 (Indie)

feature.name: Multiclass Madwalker
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose rogue as one of your classes.

Ability Score Minimum:
As a multiclass character, you must have at least the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a rogue.

	• Dexterity 13, and
	• Wisdom 13

Proficiencies Gained:
When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of your new class's starting proficiencies, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a rogue.

	• Armor: light armor
	• Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons
	• Tools: none
	• Skills: Choose 1 from Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Investigation, Perception, Stealth and Survival

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 274 (Indie)

feature.name: Multiclass Features
feature.text:
When you gain a new level in a class, you get its features for that level. You don't, however, receive the class's starting equipment, and a few features have additional rules when you're multiclassing: Channel Divinity, Extra Attack, Unarmored Defense, and Spellcasting.

Channel Divinity:
If you already have the Channel Divinity feature and gain a level in a class that also grants the feature, you gain the Channel Divinity effects granted by that class, but getting the feature again doesn't give you an additional use of it. You gain additional uses only when you reach a class level that explicitly grants them to you. For example, if you are a cleric 6/paladin 4, you can use Channel Divinity twice between rests because you are high enough level in the cleric class to have more uses. Whenever you use the feature, you can choose any of the Channel Divinity effects available to you from your two classes.

Extra Attack:
If you gain the Extra Attack class feature from more than one class, the features don't add together. You can't make more than two attacks with this feature unless it says you do (as the fighter's version of Extra Attack does).
	Similarly, the warlock's eldritch invocation Thirsting Blade doesn't give you additional attacks if you also have Extra Attack.

Unarmored Defense:
If you already have the Unarmored Defense feature, you can't gain it again from another class.

Spellcasting:
Your capacity for spellcasting depends partly on your combined levels in all your spellcasting classes and partly on your individual levels in those classes. Once you have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, use the rules below. If you multiclass but have the Spellcasting feature from only one class, you follow the rules as described in that class.

Spells Known and Prepared:
You determine what spells you know and can prepare for each class individually, as if you were a single-classed member of that class. If you are a ranger 4/wizard 3, for example, you know three 1 st-level ranger spells based on your levels in the ranger class. As a 3rd-level wizard, you know three wizard cantrips, and your spellbook contains ten wizard spells, two of which (the two you gained when you reached 3rd level as a wizard) can be 2nd-level spells. If your Intelligence is 16, you can prepare six wizard spells from your spellbook.
	Each spell you know and prepare is associated with one of your classes, and you use the spell casting ability of that class when you cast the spell. Similarly, a spellcasting focus, such as a holy symbol, can be used only for the spells from the class associated with that focus.
	If a cantrip of yours increases in power at higher levels, the increase is based on your character level, not your level in a particular class.

Spell Slots:
You determine your available spell slots by adding together all your levels in the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, and wizard classes, half your levels (rounded down) in the paladin and ranger classes, and a third of your fighter or rogue levels (rounded down) if you have the Eldritch Knight or the Arcane Trickster feature. Use this total to determine your spell slots by consulting the Multiclass Spellcaster table.
	If you have more than one spellcasting class, this table might give you spell slots of a level that is higher than the spells you know or can prepare. You can use those slots, but only to cast your lower-level spells. If a lower level spell that you cast, like burning hands, has an enhanced effect when cast using a higher-level slot, you can use the enhanced effect, even though you don't have any spells of that higher level.
	For example, if you are the aforementioned ranger 4/ wizard 3, you count as a 5th-level character when determining your spell slots: you have four 1st-level slots, three 2nd-level slots, and two 3rd-level slots. However, you don't know any 3rd-level spells, nor do you know any 2nd-level ranger spells. You can use the spell slots of those levels to cast the spells you do know-and potentially enhance their effects.

Pact Magic:
If you have both the Spellcasting class feature and the Pact Magic class feature from the warlock class, you can use the spell slots you gain from the Pact Magic feature to cast spells you know or have prepared from classes with the Spellcasting class feature, and you can use the spell slots you gain from the Spellcasting class feature to cast warlock spells you know.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 164

feature.name: Insanity Effects (Optional Rule)
feature.text:
Insanity Effects When the madwalker advances in one of the first three Insanity Steps, they must also roll a d8 to determine how their mind is being affected by madness.
	At 1st level, the madwalker can choose 1 to 3 of the following effects to not be part of the insanities they are subject to.
	When advancing an Insanity Step, the madwalker rolls a d8 and checks the Insanity Effects table. If they roll the number of one of the types of madness they chose not to be subject to, they advance each of the effects they are already suffering by one level. If they are not suffering any effect, nothing happens.
	Whenever this roll results in one of the effects they did not remove from their list, they gain a level of that madness, suffering its bonuses and penalties. If they are already suffering from that madness, they advance it to the next level, adding a new effect. If they are already at the second level of that madness, nothing happens.
	The effects of each level of madness are cumulative and end if the madwalker takes a long rest.

Insanity Effects:
D8 Result | Insanity Effects
Delirant (1) | You see and hear things that no one else does, convening hidden meanings. You have disadvantage on all Wisdom ability checks but gain advantage on all intelligence ones. The things you see and hear speak to you, inciting you to do as they say. At the start of your turn roll a die, if it's even you add 1d4 to all rolls in your turn, if it's odd you subtract 1d4 of all rolls in your turn.
Maniacal (2) | You find the world around you fun. Whenever an ally fails a saving throw or attack, you gain +1 to attack rolls and -1 to AC until the end of your next turn. The whole existence is a joke, and you laugh in the face of danger. You have -1 to your AC, but your attacks deal +1 damage and you are immune to being stunned, incapacitated and to sleep effects.
Enraged (3) | Your anger makes clear to others that they should not bother you. You automatically fail any Charisma (Persuasion) check, but you have advantage on all Charisma (Intimidation) checks. When your anger explodes, you become a crazy beast, hurting yourself and everyone in your way. All your melee weapon attacks do +2 damage, but they also cause you to take 2 damage that cannot be resisted or reduced in any way
Fearful (4) | You see the world's dangers as they truly are, making you very cautious. You have disadvantage on all initiative checks, but you cannot be surprised and you have +2 AC until the start of your first turn on each combat. You know that they are after you. You gain +1 to AC and on all saving throws, but your fear also cripples your actions. You have -1 to all attack rolls and ability checks.
Sadistic (5) | You like to see others suffering. At the start of your turn, if there is an enemy adjacent to you and you can attack it, you feel the need to harm it in some way. All attacks made to cause harm against one of such enemies have a +1 on the attack roll, and all actions that are not done to cause harm to one of them have -1 to all its rolls. You like to kill other people. On your turn, whenever a non-allied creature adjacent to you has 0 HP, you have disadvantage on all rolls on your turn that are not made with the intention to kill that creature. If you kill it, you regain hit points equal to half your level (rounded up).
Fanatic (6) | You know the powers from beyond that talk to you in your nightmares. You are one of their chosen. You immediately gain Insanity Points equal to 1 + half your madwalker level (rounded up), but your Insanity Steps don't cause penalties to your saving throws. The ancient entities feed you with unfathomable power. Your Insanity Steps penalty increases by -1, but once per turn you can add 1d6 psychic damage to an attack or aberrant mutation that causes damage.
Gloomy (7) | You feel sad, and don't really feel the need to place effort into things. You always consider that you rolled a 10 on all ability checks. Nothing really matters to you, and all is pointless. You don't apply ability modifiers on any damage roll you make. Reduce all damage caused to you by 5 (to a minimum of 1).
Narcissistic (8) | You know how great you are, but you cannot accept when others cause you to fail. When you hit an enemy you gain +1 to attack rolls until you miss an attack (the bonus doesn't stack). When you miss an attack on an enemy, you gain -1 to attack rolls until you hit an attack (it doesn't stack). Someone like you cannot be touched by lesser beings. You have +1 AC, but whenever an attack hits you, you take 1d4 extra psychic damage. This damage ignores immunities, resistances, and cannot be reduced in any way

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Aberrant Mutation
feature.text:
You can produce unimaginable temporary modifications to your body, known as Aberrant Mutations. Some of them require the target(s) to roll a saving throw to resist their effects.

	Aberrant Mutation save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Known Aberrant Mutations:
At 1st level, you know the Dark Energy 1st-level Aberrant Mutation and two other 1st-level Aberrant Mutations of your choice from the list later in this section. You may learn a new Aberrant Mutation at every odd level in the madwalker class, as shown in the madwalker table on page 139. If you wish, when you gain a madwalker level, you may choose one Aberrant Mutation that you already know and replace it with another.
	Each of your Aberrant Mutations must be of a level no higher than your madwalker level allows. For example, when you reach 5th level of the class,you can learn a new Aberrant Mutation of 1st or 2nd level, but you cannot know more than four Aberrant Mutations.
	You can use only one Aberrant Mutation per round, but you can have more than one of them active.

Insanity Points:
Madwalkers delve deeper and deeper into the realms of madness as they use their powers. After activating an Aberrant Mutation, at the end of your turn you acquire the number of Insanity Points stated in its description.
	Once you amass a specified number of Insanity Points, you receive a penalty to your AC and all attacks and saving throws, as shown in the Insanity Steps table. When you reach maximum Insanity, you transform into a Penumbral Shape. After the transformation ends, you remain at maximum Insanity and stop gaining points (keeping the penalties).
	You lose all Insanity Points after finishing a long rest.

Insanity Steps:
Total Penalty to Attacks, AC and Saves | Insanity Points (1st to 4th Levels) | Insanity Points (5th to 8th Levels) | Insanity Points (9th to 12th Levels) | Insanity Points (13th to 16th Levels) | Insanity Points (17th to 20th Levels)
-1 penalty | 3 to 5 | 6 to 11 | 9 to 17 | 12 to 23 | 15 to 29
-2 penalty | 6 to 8 | 12 to 17 | 18 to 26 | 24 to 35 | 30 to 44
-3 penalty | 9 or more | 18 or more | 27 or more | 36 or more | 45 or more
Penumbral Shape | 12 (maximum) | 24 (maximum) | 36 (maximum) | 48 (maximum) | 60 (maximum)
