Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 143 (Indie)

feature.name: Penumbral Shape
feature.text:
Starting at 1st level, when you reach the maximum number of Insanity Points indicated on the table, your shape becomes that of a penumbral creature for as many minutes as your madwalker level. You automatically revert to your normal form if you fall unconscious, drop to 0 hit points, or die.
	Each level grants you access to new Penumbral Shapes, according to the following table:

Available Penumbral Shapes:
Level | Basic (Aspect) | Aberrant Arachnid Trail | Nightmare's Augury Trail
1st | Gluttony | - | -
2nd | - | Aracne Serf | Nightmare Lurker
3rd | Envy | Aracne Scout | Nightmare Keeper
5th | Disgust | Aracne Soldier | Nightmare Guardian
7th | Sloth | Aracne Ambusher | Nightmare Warrior
9th | Pain | Aracne Hunter | Nightmare Overseer
11th | Lust | Aracne Sorcerer | Penumbral Eye
13th | Sadness | Aracne Noble | Penumbral Oppressor
15th | Pride | Aracne Commander | Penumbral Lord
17th | Greed | Aracne Overlord | Penumbral Vizir
19th | Fear | Aracne Matriarch | Penumbral Tyrant

You have access to the basic shapes and, starting at 2nd level, you also have access to the shapes from your Trail of Madness, as shown in the table. When this ability activates, choose and transform into one of the basic or trail shapes available. If there is not enough space for your chosen shape to fit, the transformation fails and you lose its use.
	While you are transformed, the following rules apply:

	• All attacks, damaging spells, and effects from your shape deal 1d4 extra damage, increasing to 2d4 at 6th level, 3d4 at 12th level, and 4d4 at 18th level.

	• Your game statistics are replaced by those of the penumbral creature, but you retain your alignment, personality, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining the creature's Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw proficiencies, and all other proficiencies it may have. If the penumbral creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block is higher than yours, use the creature's bonus instead of yours.

	• While in your Penumbral Shape, you may not activate Aberrant Mutations, cast spells, or use any of your original form's features. Any active Aberrant Mutation ends immediately. Except for your proficiencies, mental abilities, and Blades of Madness feature, you only have access to the features of your Penumbral Shape.

	• The Insanity Steps table penalties do not apply while in this form.

	• The transformation automatically interrupts your concentration in spells and features you may have already cast or activated.

	• When you transform, you assume the creature's maximum hit points and Hit Dice. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. For example, if your Penumbral Shape has 1 hit point left and you take 10 damage, you revert and your normal form takes 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked unconscious.

	• When you transform, you choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the GM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment based on the creature's shape and size. The equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.

	• You ignore Tamera's Light (that deals damage to penumbral creatures while exposed to direct daylight)

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 143 (Indie)

feature.name: Trail of Madness
feature.text:
At 2nd level, you are able to manifest one of the powerful creatures of the Penumbral Plane. Choose between the Nightmare Augury Trail or the Aberrant Arachnid Trail. Each trail offers unique Aberrant Mutations, Penumbral Shapes, and features at 2nd, 7th, 14th, and 18th levels.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 144 (Indie)

feature.name: Shadow Sense
feature.text:
At 3rd level, your mental bond with the realm of nightmares deepens, enhancing your sense of reality. You gain advantage on all Wisdom ability checks and saving throws against environmental effects in the Penumbral Plane. However, while interacting with beings from the Material Plane, excluding other madwalkers, you suffer disadvantage on all Charisma ability checks, except Intimidation.
	In addition, you are adept at locating portals and rifts leading to and from the Penumbral Plane, being aware of their distance, direction, and size within a 1-mile radius.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 144 (Indie)

feature.name: Blades of Madness
feature.text:
At 3rd level, you can materialize your nightmares and distort reality. When you use an Aberrant Mutation, you may reroll any number of damage dice until the end of your turn, using the second result. Even in your Penumbral Shape, you can apply this ability to all damage dice.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a feat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.text:
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Aberrant Mind
feature.text:
Starting at the 6th level, your proficiency bonus is doubled for saving throws against effects that manipulate your emotions, read your thoughts, cause the charmed condition, or belong to the enchantment or illusion schools. This bonus also applies to saves against spells or effects from aberration creatures or natural creatures of the Penumbral Plane.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a feat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Warped Morphology
feature.text:
Your proximity to the Penumbral Plane energies causes your physiology to become bizarre. Starting at the 10th level, when an enemy scores a critical hit on you, they must re-roll the attack. You can use this ability once, regaining its use after a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Penumbral Shift
feature.text:
Starting at 11th level, once per long rest, you can use an action to transport yourself and your allies to the Penumbral Plane or back to the Material Plane. This feature works similarly to the plane shift spell, but exclusively between the Material Plane and the Penumbral Plane.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a feat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Penumbral Portal
feature.text:
At 15th level, when using your Penumbral Shift ability, you can choose to create a portal from the Penumbral Plane to the Material Plane or vice versa. This 10-foot diameter portal remains open for 1 minute or until you close it using a bonus action. For all other purposes, it functions like the gate spell.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a feat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a feat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Waking Nightmare
feature.text:
Starting at 20th level, once per long rest, with an action, you can transform into your Penumbral Shape, regardless of how many Insanity Points you have. This transformation does not interfere with the transformation resulting from your accumulated Insanity Points.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Trail of Madness: Aberrant Arachnid Trail
feature.text:
(Arachnid Hunter's)

Madwalkers that follow this path are not only feared but also hated by the Arachnes. The gruesome ritual they undergo attunes them to the energies of Ungods and the Arachnes, harnessing their vicious powers by taking the heart of an Arachne, a price paid willingly for power.
	These madwalkers move through the shadows, sensing and manipulating the chaotic vibrations of the Penumbral Plane, blades dripping with deadly poison, and hands weaving sticky webs that ensnare prey. They feed on their victim's fear, savoring the scent of terror that fills the air before they strike with unmatched intensity and aggression.
	Their transformations are an affront to all that is natural, becoming horrid, fearsome exemplars of cunning and viciousness. The resulting humanoid-spider hybrids are chaotic deadly creatures that send shivers down the spine of even the bravest warriors, their presence alone an omen of a horrible fate. These madwalkers revel in their sinister powers, embracing their chaos and savoring the taste of their prey's terror as they move through the shadows, always aware of the price they pay for their power.
	With their senses attuned to the deep hunger of the spiders, the madwalkers that follow this path move through the Penumbral Plane as deadly predators, always on the hunt for their next victim.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Aberrant Arachnid Mutations (Aberrant Arachnid Trail)
feature.text:
As an Aberrant Arachnid Trail madwalker, you have access to various exclusive Aberrant Mutations acquired at 2nd, 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th madwalker levels. Upon gaining each of these levels, you may choose one of the available Aberrant Mutations, and it does not count toward the number of Aberrant Mutations known.

Aberrant Arachnid Mutations:
Madwalker Level | Available Aberrant Mutations
2nd | Noxious Attack, Shadow Web
5th | Venom Splash, Nauseating Spray
9th | Arachnid Legs, Venomous Saliva
13th | Allergic Spores, Pheromone Spray
17th | Web Cocoon, Exoskeleton

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 145 (Indie)

feature.name: Cunning Predator (Aberrant Arachnid Trail)
feature.text:
You embody the agility and predatory instincts of a spider.
	At 2nd level, while wearing light or no armor and without a shield, your Armor Class (AC) increases by 1. In addition, every time you engage in a melee attack against a creature with no allies within a 5-foot radius, you gain temporary hit points equal to your madwalker level. These hit points last for a minute and are granted even if the attack fails. They don't stack. Starting from the 5th level, you add your proficiency bonus to your level when obtaining these temporary hit points.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 146 (Indie)

feature.name: Arachne Penumbral Shape (Aberrant Arachnid Trail)
feature.text:
Starting at 2nd level, you have access to penumbral shapes exclusive to the Aberrant Arachnid Trail (see madwalker's penumbral shapes).

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 146 (Indie)

feature.name: Arachnid Nature (Aberrant Arachnid Trail)
feature.text:
Starting at 7th level, you gain poison immunity and a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. This allows you to traverse walls and ceilings hands-free.
	Additionally, when you suffer damage from an attack, you can react by moving up to 20 feet. If you end your movement in an area that offers total cover or is heavily obscured, you can hide as part of this reaction.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 146 (Indie)

feature.name: Black Widow's Web (Aberrant Arachnid Trail)
feature.text:
Starting at the 14th level, once per long rest, you can spend 10 minutes to weave a mystical web around you. This creates a up to 50-foot radius circular area that must be anchored between at least two solid masses as the web spell. Creatures oblivious to the web must make a Wisdom (Perception) check against your Dexterity (Stealth) check to spot it before entering its area.
	You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks within this area. Furthermore, if you're in contact with the web, you can sense all creatures that touch or move through it, thus, they can't surprise you.
	For all other creatures, the web is difficult terrain. If they move or end their turn on the web, they must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 20) once per turn. If they fail, they become restrained and stuck in the web. At the end of each turn, the restrained creature can attempt a Strength saving throw (DC 20) to break free from the web. The web lasts for 8 hours.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 146 (Indie)

feature.name: Arachnid Camouflage (Aberrant Arachnid Trail)
feature.text:
Starting at the 18th level, once per short rest, you can use an action to become invisible for a minute or until you decide to reveal yourself. Any creature trying to detect you while you're invisible in this way have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) check. This invisibility isn't interrupted by attacking. Anything you're wearing or carrying becomes invisible with you.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 146 (Indie)

feature.name: Trail of Madness: Nightmare's Augury Trail
feature.text:
(Nightmare Predator's)

Madwalkers that follow this path have delved into darkness, seeking the strength of the Watchers, natural enemies of all other penumbral creatures, so they can gain power to destroy them. By taking the heart of one of Augur's Watchers, they have unlocked the energies of the Penumbral Plane, transforming themselves into twisted beings of immense power.
	Though the Watchers regard them as mere nuisances, these madwalkers relish their newfound might.
	With their senses attuned to Augur's powers of vision and dark prophecy, these madwalkers move through the shadows with sinister intent. Their intuition predicts future events with eerie accuracy, and they can see what no other mortal can perceive.
	Their transformation is a grotesque and horrifying spectacle, turning them into floating creatures of writhing tentacles and spikes, covered in sinister scales, with a massive mouth filled with serrated teeth that feed on the pain and suffering of their victims. Their minds become even more twisted and focused in this state, consumed by thoughts of domination and control.
	Some of these madwalkers struggle against their nature, seeking to use their power for good, but others succumb to their darkest desires, using their might to oppress and dominate others. Nevertheless, many of these dark beings have turned their eyes towards heroism, using their fearsome abilities to fight against the very darkness that empowers them.
	Their very presence strikes fear in the hearts of their enemies, and their power is unmatched. They pay a terrible price for it, but they do not regret their path, as they continue to grow stronger, becoming even more powerful as they move through the penumbra with their newfound abilities.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 148 (Indie)

feature.name: Nightmarish Augurs (Nightmare's Augury Trail)
feature.text:
At the 2nd level, your terrifying dreams reveal twisted pieces of your future, enabling you to brace for impending dangers. After completing a long rest, you can select 'even' or 'odd'. Until your next long rest, whenever you receive damage from an attack and the attack roll's natural result matches your selection, you have resistance to all damage from that attack, except in case of a critical hit.
	Additionally, at 5th level, you gain the ability to foresee your potential demise. If you take damage substantial enough to drop you to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to spend any number of Hit Dice, instantly regaining hit points before the damage is applied, potentially preventing your hit points from dropping to 0.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 148 (Indie)

feature.name: Nightmare's Augury Penumbral Shape (Nightmare's Augury Trail)
feature.text:
Starting at 2nd level, you have access to penumbral shapes exclusive to the Nightmare's Augury Trail (see madwalker's penumbral shapes). Additionally, when you assume a Penumbral Shape exclusive to the Nightmare's Augury Trail, you also replace your Wisdom with the Wisdom of the Penumbral Shape.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 148 (Indie)

feature.name: Psychic Shield (Nightmare's Augury Trail)
feature.text:
At 7th level, while conscious, you can uphold a psychic protective shield. As long as this shield is active, any damage you sustain from an attack is reduced by an amount equal to your Wisdom modifier (before applying any resistances, vulnerabilities, and other effects).
	In addition, when you make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to augment the roll with your Wisdom modifier.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 148 (Indie)

feature.name: Mental Power (Nightmare's Augury Trail)
feature.text:
At the 14th level, you gain immunity to psychic damage and a flying speed equivalent to your walking speed, along with the hover property.
	In addition, you can telepathically speak to any creatures within 90 feet of you that can understand at least one language, even if you do not share a common language.
	As a bonus action, you can employ this ability to mimic the effects of the detect thoughts spell. If the creature is unwilling, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Aberrant Mutation's save DC to resist both the communication and the thought-reading ability

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 148 (Indie)

feature.name: Nightmare's Augury Mutations (Nightmare's Augury Trail)
feature.text:
As a madwalker of the Nightmare's Augury Trail, you have access to a range of Aberrant Mutations unique to this subclass, acquired at 2nd, 5th, 9th, 13rd, and 17th levels of madwalker. Upon gaining each of these levels, you may choose one of the available Aberrant Mutations, and it does not count toward the number of Aberrant Mutations known.

Nightmare's Augury Mutations:
Madwalker Level | Available Aberrant Mutations
2nd | Mind Slash, Psychic Bond
5th | Mind Drain, Psychic Weapon
9th | Telepathic Mindlink, Waves of Headache
13th | Minor Telekinesis, Penumbral Attraction
17th | Eye of Augury, Phantom of Penumbra

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 148 (Indie)

feature.name: Nocturnal Prelude (Nightmare's Augury Trail)
feature.text:
At 18th level, you can predict the near future and modify it. You can impose advantage or disadvantage on any roll you make, or that an ally or enemy in your line of sight makes, a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all uses after a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 148 (Indie)

fields.name: Mage (Tanares)
fields.proficiency: Intelligence, Wisdom, Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Religion
fields.weapons: Daggers, Darts, Slings, Staffs, Light Crossbows

trait.name: Mage
trait.text:
Mages are simplified wizards. They are ideal for new players who are looking for less complexity or to create a more straightforward character without sacrificing effectiveness during play.
	Mages are spellcasters of unparalleled talent, known for their skilled and practical approach to magic. With logical minds and sharp intellects, they focus their efforts on refining a select few incantations, honing their control until each one shines like a work of art. Their mastery of magic allows them to wield their powers with effortless precision, pursuing their individual goals with unwavering determination.
	In addition to their exceptional abilities, mages are also down-to-earth in their approach to life. They indulge in life's finer things, savoring rich cuisine and rare wines, but view the world with a utilitarian perspective, seeking success in all aspects, not just in magical prowess. They have a fondness for order and prefer tidy spaces, well-groomed attire, and everything in its proper place.
	Though not naturally charismatic, mages often play the role of hidden masterminds behind successful adventuring parties. Using their strategic thinking and practicality, they guide their companions to victory from behind the scenes, seeing themselves as the driving force behind any venture's success. They are self-assured, their confidence matched only by their exceptional abilities.
	Mages aspire to high-status positions, but prefer roles that require technical and practical work over those that involve more political or theoretical routine. With their practicality, mastery of magic, and appreciation for life's indulgences, mages are truly one-of-a-kind spellcasters, always turning their knowledge into mastery. Their logical and organized nature only adds to their unparalleled virtuosity in magic.
	You can't multiclass into Simplified Classes, or multiclass if you are a Simplified Class.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 196 (Indie)

trait.name: How to play with a Mage
trait.text:
For those players who relish commanding the battlefield with devastating spells, the mage class emerges as a compelling choice. A streamlined version of the wizard, mages wield arcane power, which they can evolve into awe-inspiring spells as they advance in levels. This arcane mastery empowers mages to turn the tides in various combat situations.
	From the first level, mages tap into their magical prowess to deal reliable damage with spells like magic missile—an attack that opponents cannot evade. They can also detect concealed magical elements in their environment using detect magic, providing valuable insights during exploration.
	Mages might not boast the sturdiest of defenses, but they flourish in a ranged combat role, dealing devastating damage from a safe distance. This class needs protection from allies, allowing mages to focus on unleashing their potent offensive capabilities. As they progress, mages unlock even more destructive spells like disintegrate and meteor swarm, continually enhancing their damage output.
	The mage's arsenal also includes protective and utility spells such as stoneskin and fly, offering resilience in combat and mobility. They can even assist their party during exploration or emergency exits with spells like teleport, making them a boon both in and out of combat scenarios.
	Mages excel in providing consistent damage in combat while simultaneously offering valuable defensive and utility abilities.
	In conclusion, the mage class is a fantastic choice for players eager to specialize in dealing damage with offensive spells. Their access to a potent spell repertoire, combined with handy utility abilities, makes them a multifaceted and indispensable asset to any adventuring party.

feature.name: Starting Mage
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Mage, you begin play with 6 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.

	• Armor: None
	• Weapons: Daggers, darts, slings, staffs, light crossbows
	• Tools: None
	• Saving Throws: Intelligence, Wisdom
	• Skills: Choose two from Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, and Religion

You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.

	• (a) a quarterstaff or (b) a dagger
	• (a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus
	• (a) a scholar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack

If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 4d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 196 (Indie)

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.text:
Due to your ability to channel arcane power, you can cast spells.

	Specific Cantrips. At 1st level, you know two cantrips: fire bolt and light. At 3rd level, you learn one more cantrip, mage hand.

	Simplified Spellcasting. Unlike more complex classes, as a mage, your spells are predetermined by your class and you can cast each of them twice per day. Follow the Mage Spells table to know which spells you know and when you will have access to them.

	Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your mage spells, since you learn your spells through study. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability.
	In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting a saving throw DC for a mage spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

	Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

	Spell Attack Modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

	Casting spells in Higher Levels. Some spells can be cast using spell slots of a higher level, making their effects more powerful.
	If you have a spell that can be cast on a higher level, you can use another spell of higher level in place of it to cast that spell on a higher level. The level of the spell you spent will determine the level the spell was effectively cast.
	Example: If you have magic missile, but want to use it as a 2nd level spell, you can choose a spell of 2nd level, such as invisibility, to use. This counts as one of your two uses of invisibility, but instead of applying the effects of invisibility, you cast the magic missile spell as a 2nd level spell adjusting its effects as described in it.

	Spellcasting Focus. You can use an arcane focus or a component pouch as a focus for your spells.

Mage Spells Table:
Level | Spells
1st | detect magic, magic missiles
3rd | invisibility, scorching ray
5th | fireball, fly
7th | dimension door, stone skin
9th | cone of cold, wall of force
11th | chain lightning, disintegrate
13th | teleport
15th | antimagic field
17th | meteor swarm

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 197 (Indie)

feature.name: Experience
feature.text:
Your experience grants you certain practical knowledge. At 2nd level, and again when you reach 10th and 18th level, you gain proficiency in a skill of your choice.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 198 (Indie)

feature.name: Arcane Protection
feature.text:

trait.name: Priest
trait.text:
Priests are simplified clerics. They are ideal for new players who are looking for less complexity or to create a more straightforward character without sacrificing effectiveness during play.

Priests are faithful servants of the gods, shining beacons of devotion who spread the word of their deity to all who will listen. Most priests serve Tamera, the radiant goddess of sun and life, while others follow Bauron, the enigmatic deity of moon and punishment. Dwarves offer their prayers to Dorsi, the god of guardianship and virtues, and among the elves, there are those who worship the Cuibhle pantheon, the gods of elements and seasons.

Acting as guides to the common people and trusted advisors to their closest allies, priests are known for their exceptional healing powers and their ability to protect those around them with sacred magic. They serve as shining lights, illuminating the path for their companions and offering hope in even the darkest of moments.

Although not trained in traditional combat, priests are equipped with the basics of armor and shield usage, allowing them to face danger with bravery. However, their true power lies in their unwavering faith and their divine magic, making them a formidable force on the battlefield and a source of inspiration to their allies. Whether ministering in small temples or venturing out into the world as adventurers, priests are a shining example of the power of the divine.

You can't multiclass into Simplified Classes, or multiclass if you are a Simplified Class.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 200 (Indie)

trait.name: How to play with a Priest
trait.text:
The priest class is a streamlined variation of the cleric. Unlike the clerics with their wide range of domains and vast spell options, priests specialize predominantly in support spells, geared towards healing and empowering their allies. From level one, priests wield spells capable of significantly influencing the course of a battle.

Priests are uniquely versatile, adept at functioning as both robust tanks and reliable support units. While they rely on their allies for protection, they possess access to armor and weapons for direct combat, providing a balanced role in the party. As they advance in levels, priests acquire even more potent spells, bolstering their supportive capabilities. Spells like revivify and greater restoration ensure that their comrades are perpetually ready for the fray, while offensive spells like spiritual weapon and fire storm offer a formidable attack repertoire.

Priests are deeply rooted in religious beliefs in Tanares. They serve as crucial intermediaries, shedding light on the intricate and profound topics that permeate the continent's discourse. This allows players to delve into the persona of the wise, scholarly priest, making this class a valuable asset in both combat and narrative scenarios.

In conclusion, priests offer the dual appeal of being potent allies in combat and insightful advisors outside of it. With their balance of support spells, tanking capabilities, and offensive magic, priests are an exceptional addition to any campaign. Whether you're enthralled by the concept of bestowing blessings or directly engaging in combat, priests cater to a broad spectrum of your preferences.

You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.

	• Weapons: Simple weapons
	• Tools: None
	• Saving Throws: Wisdom, Charisma
	• Skills: Choose two from History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion

You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.

	• (a) a mace or (b) a warhammer (if proficient)
	• (a) scale mail, (b) leather armor, or (c) chain mail (if proficient)
	• (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
	• (a) a priest's pack or (b) an explorer's pack
	• A shield and a holy symbol

If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 5d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.

feature.name: Spellcasting
feature.text:
Due to your ability to channel divine power, you can cast spells.

Specific Cantrips:
At 1st level, you know two cantrips: light and sacred flame.
At 3rd level you learn an additional cantrip, spare the dying.

Simplified Spellcasting:
Unlike more complex classes, as a priest, your spells are predetermined by your class and you can cast each of them twice per day. Follow the Priest Spells table to know which spells you know and when you will have access to them.

Spellcasting Ability:
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your priest spells. The power of your spells comes from your devotion to your deity. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability.
	In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting a saving throw DC for a priest spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

	Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

	Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Casting spells in Higher Levels:
Some spells can be cast using spell slots of a higher level, making their effects more powerful.
	If you have a spell that can be cast on a higher level, you can use another spell of higher level in place of it to cast that spell on a higher level. The level of the spell you spent will determine the level the spell was effectively cast.

Example: If you have cure wounds, but want to use it as a 2nd level spell, you can choose a spell of 2nd level, such as lesser restoration, to use. This counts as one of your two uses of lesser restoration, but instead of applying the effects of lesser restoration, you cast the cure wounds spell as a 2nd level spell adjusting its effects as described in it.

Spellcasting Focus:
You can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus for your spells.

feature.name: Multiclass Redeemer
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose redeemer as one of your classes.

Ability Score Minimum:
As a multiclass character, you must have at least the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a redeemer.

	• Charisma 13

Proficiencies Gained:
When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of your new class's starting proficiencies, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a redeemer.

	• Armor: light armor
	• Skills: one skill from the class's skill list

feature.name: Multiclass Features
feature.text:
When you gain a new level in a class, you get its features for that level. You don't, however, receive the class's starting equipment, and a few features have additional rules when you're multiclassing: Channel Divinity, Extra Attack, Unarmored Defense, and Spellcasting.

Channel Divinity:
If you already have the Channel Divinity feature and gain a level in a class that also grants the feature, you gain the Channel Divinity effects granted by that class, but getting the feature again doesn't give you an additional use of it. You gain additional uses only when you reach a class level that explicitly grants them to you. For example, if you are a cleric 6/paladin 4, you can use Channel Divinity twice between rests because you are high enough level in the cleric class to have more uses. Whenever you use the feature, you can choose any of the Channel Divinity effects available to you from your two classes.

Extra Attack:
If you gain the Extra Attack class feature from more than one class, the features don't add together. You can't make more than two attacks with this feature unless it says you do (as the fighter's version of Extra Attack does).
	Similarly, the warlock's eldritch invocation Thirsting Blade doesn't give you additional attacks if you also have Extra Attack.

Unarmored Defense:
If you already have the Unarmored Defense feature, you can't gain it again from another class.

Spellcasting:
Your capacity for spellcasting depends partly on your combined levels in all your spellcasting classes and partly on your individual levels in those classes. Once you have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, use the rules below. If you multiclass but have the Spellcasting feature from only one class, you follow the rules as described in that class.

Spells Known and Prepared:
You determine what spells you know and can prepare for each class individually, as if you were a single-classed member of that class. If you are a ranger 4/wizard 3, for example, you know three 1 st-level ranger spells based on your levels in the ranger class. As a 3rd-level wizard, you know three wizard cantrips, and your spellbook contains ten wizard spells, two of which (the two you gained when you reached 3rd level as a wizard) can be 2nd-level spells. If your Intelligence is 16, you can prepare six wizard spells from your spellbook.
	Each spell you know and prepare is associated with one of your classes, and you use the spell casting ability of that class when you cast the spell. Similarly, a spellcasting focus, such as a holy symbol, can be used only for the spells from the class associated with that focus.
	If a cantrip of yours increases in power at higher levels, the increase is based on your character level, not your level in a particular class.

Spell Slots:
You determine your available spell slots by adding together all your levels in the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, and wizard classes, half your levels (rounded down) in the paladin and ranger classes, and a third of your fighter or rogue levels (rounded down) if you have the Eldritch Knight or the Arcane Trickster feature. Use this total to determine your spell slots by consulting the Multiclass Spellcaster table.
	If you have more than one spellcasting class, this table might give you spell slots of a level that is higher than the spells you know or can prepare. You can use those slots, but only to cast your lower-level spells. If a lower level spell that you cast, like burning hands, has an enhanced effect when cast using a higher-level slot, you can use the enhanced effect, even though you don't have any spells of that higher level.
	For example, if you are the aforementioned ranger 4/ wizard 3, you count as a 5th-level character when determining your spell slots: you have four 1st-level slots, three 2nd-level slots, and two 3rd-level slots. However, you don't know any 3rd-level spells, nor do you know any 2nd-level ranger spells. You can use the spell slots of those levels to cast the spells you do know-and potentially enhance their effects.

Pact Magic:
If you have both the Spellcasting class feature and the Pact Magic class feature from the warlock class, you can use the spell slots you gain from the Pact Magic feature to cast spells you know or have prepared from classes with the Spellcasting class feature, and you can use the spell slots you gain from the Spellcasting class feature to cast warlock spells you know.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2014) p. 164

	For example, if you want to cast the 1st-level spell bless and you have one 1st-level spell slot and one 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast bless using either spell slot.

	Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher. You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the cleric spell list. The Spells Known column of the Redeemer table shows when you learn more cleric spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown on the table. For example, when you reach 3rd level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level. Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one cleric spell you know and replace it with another spell from the cleric spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

feature.text:
As a redeemer, your greatest weapons are your rays, which shoot directly from your hands. Starting at 1st level, you can fire a Positive or Negative ray using your action, as long as you have at least one free hand. Your rays have a range of 60 feet and must target a single creature.

	The temporary hit points granted by the ray change to 2d4 at 5th level in this class, 3d4 at 11th level, and 4d4 at 17th level.

	Negative Ray. Make a ranged spell attack against the target creature, dealing 1d6 necrotic damage on a hit. This damage ignores any immunity or resistance the creature has if it's an unnatural creature. In Tanares, unnatural creatures are those not created by Tamera and/or Bauron, such as penumbral creatures, Ungods, undead, and aberrations. If you're playing in another setting, talk to your GM to decide what types of creatures fit this definition.

feature.name: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

If your DM allows the use of feats, you may instead take a feat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 185

feature.name: Balance of Life
feature.text:
Starting at 20th level, using your action, you can call upon the Balance of Life. You and all creatures within 30 feet of you either get healed or take damage, such that each is left with half their maximum hit points. You can only re-use this ability after a long rest. Creatures that would lose hit points due to this ability can resist its effect by making a Constitution saving throw (DC 20).

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 185

feature.name: Spiritual Vocation: Doomspeaker
feature.text:
Chosen by Bauron in their dreams, even if not aware of it, redeemers of the Doomspeaker vocation strive to ready mortals for the inevitable armageddon. Tasked with fortifying society against the Ungods' invasion, they establish institutions, build armies, and manipulate the masses for the ultimate battle in the Penumbral Plane. Exceptional strategists and businessmen, Doomspeakers amass resources and wealth to construct a resilient society able to withstand the Ungods' onslaught. Often found in influential positions, such as traders, politicians, or religious leaders, their primary goal is to consolidate power and resources, ensuring the world stands prepared for the impending threat.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 187

feature.name: Businessman (Doomspeaker)
feature.text:
At 2nd level, you gain one of the following benefits: proficiency in vehicles (land) and cartographer's tools, or proficiency in vehicles (water) and navigator's tools. Additionally, you have advantage on ability checks associated with gathering information and connecting with influential people in the politics and economy.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 188

feature.name: Doom Magic (Doomspeaker)
feature.text:
Starting at 2nd level, whenever you use Magic in Rays and hit an enemy, you can choose to apply one of the extra effects on the table below.

Doom Magic:
Name | Effect
Decay | The target takes only half of all damage caused by the ray and the spell, but becomes cursed by your magic for 1 minute. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it takes half the damage again, then it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw to end this effect.
Despair | You instill the fear of the world-end on the creature. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1d4 rounds.
Omen | Before the target creature makes a saving throw against your spell, choose two numbers between 2 and 20. If the creature's roll equals either of the chosen numbers, it automatically fails the saving throw. If the creature has advantage on the saving throw, use the highest of its two rolls. If the creature has disadvantage on the saving throw, use the lowest of its two rolls.
Apocalypse | All other creatures within 10 feet of the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they are affected by the spell (but not your ray) as if they were the original target. You must make any necessary attack rolls, saving throws, or decisions for each affected creature, as if casting the spell against that target.

After using Apocalypse, you must take a short rest before you can use this option again.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 188

feature.name: Ray of Damnation (Doomspeaker)
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, your negative ray imposes disadvantage on saves made by non-natural creatures (penumbral creatures, Ungods' servants, undeads, and aberrations, or as determined by your GM in other settings) targeted by the ray until the beginning of your next turn (including saves against spells cast by Magic in Ray during the same ray).
	Starting at 9th level, whenever you use your negative ray using the Magic in Ray ability, in addition to other effects, you also deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage to the target on a successful hit. This extra damage ignores any immunity or resistance the creature might have if it is a unnatural creature.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 188

feature.name: Doombringer Extra Spells (Doomspeaker)
feature.text:
At 3rd, 7th, 10th, 13th and 16th levels, following the table below, you learn a new spell, which counts as a cleric spell for you and doesn't count against your number of spells known

Doombringer Spell List:
Level | Extra Spell
3rd | Tasha's hideous laughter
7th | vampiric touch
10th | dream
13th | finger of death
16th | dominate monster

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 188

feature.name: Doombringer (Doomspeaker)
feature.text:
Starting at 6th level, when you unleash your Negative Ray, you inflict additional necrotic damage equivalent to your Proficiency Bonus.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 188

feature.name: King of Treasures (Doomspeaker)
feature.text:
Your business acumen offers you distinctive abilities to appraise items, as well as to count treasures. Starting at 10th level, you have advantage on any Intelligence checks related to trading goods, conducting mathematical calculations, economics, or investing in a business. Additionally, you can verify the authenticity of a work of art, coin, gem, jewelry, document, or magic item and determine its price by examining it for at least 1 minute.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 188

feature.name: Charming (Doomspeaker)
feature.text:
Starting at 15th level, when you succeed on a Charisma ability check to interact with a non-hostile creature, it becomes charmed by you. The creature becomes friendly to you until you commit an act harmful to it, or say or do something against its deep-rooted beliefs. The creature can resist this effect with a successful Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. The effect lasts for 7 days and is not considered magical, but merely the result of your extraordinary persuasive power. A creature that succeeds on the save becomes immune to this ability for the next 24 hours.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 188

feature.name: New Perspective (Doomspeaker)
feature.text:
At 18th level, you can alter a creature's viewpoint by engaging it in conversation for at least 10 minutes. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On failure, you can modify the creature's opinion on a subject or individual, provided it does not contradict its core beliefs. This ability can only be used on the same creature once every 7 days. This effect is not magical but results from your great power of persuasion, and creatures influenced by this ability will feel convinced rather than charmed or manipulated. At the GM's discretion, a creature exposed to this ability multiple times over months or years may even change its alignment, personality traits, ideals, and flaws, if the change aligns with the creature's circumstances.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 188

feature.name: Spiritual Vocation: Shepherd
feature.text:
Redeemers who follow the Shepherd vocation are those whose mission given by Tamera in their dreams, even if they are not aware of it, is to bring balance and soothe the masses so that their emotions do not generate penumbral creatures. In addition, controlling the emotions of the masses ensures that wars are less likely to happen. Shepherds are excellent leaders of crowds, often religious leaders, prophets, and healers.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 186

feature.name: Preacher (Shepherd)
feature.text:
At 2nd level, you gain proficiency in Religion. If you are already proficient, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability checks you make that uses this skill.
	In addition, you have advantage on Charisma checks related to gathering groups, crowds, or audiences to listen to you.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 186

feature.name: Cycle of Redemption (Shepherd)
feature.text:
At 2nd level, you receive a special marking on your character sheet called the Cycle of Redemption. The position to which you move the marker on the Cycle, when you use one of your rays, will guarantee you a unique benefit, which will last until the beginning of your next turn.
	After taking a long rest, you determine your starting position on the Cycle and then place a marker on your character sheet in the chosen position. You move this marker every time you declare firing one of your Rays. The position you will be in at the end of this move will determine the benefit you will receive until the beginning of your next turn. You do not receive any benefits if you did not use your action to perform a ray in your turn.
	The movement happens before the ray is shot, so all benefits to moving in a new position are applied before the ray is used. This movement still happens if you are using Magic in Rays, and is also applied before the spell is cast.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 186

feature.name: Movement On The Cycle (Shepherd)
feature.text:
Positive Ray:
If you declare that you will fire your Positive Ray, you must make a move with your marker following the arrow present on the circumference of the circle (yellow arrow - Order Track - one movement clockwise)

Negative Rays:
If you declare that you will fire your Negative Ray, you must make a move with your marker following the arrow passing through the middle of the circle (purple arrow - Chaos Track - two movements counterclockwise)

Positions and Effects:
A - When unleashing a ray, you can shoot an extra ray of the same type towards a separate target. Starting at 10th level, you can release two additional rays towards two distinct targets, excluding your original target.

B - Prior to firing your ray, you can instantly move 20 feet. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks and occurs before the ray is discharged. From the 10th level, this movement increases to 30 feet.

C - Until your next turn starts, all your saving throws receive a bonus equivalent to your Charisma modifier. From the 10th level, gain your Charisma modifier plus 2 as the bonus.

D - The temporary hit points granted by your Positive Ray increase by 2d4, and the damage inflicted by your Negative Ray increases by 2d6. From the 10th level, this extra bonus rises to 3d4 and 3d6, respectively.

E - Your rays' magical attack rolls receive a +3 bonus and can bypass half cover and three-quarter cover. From the 10th level, this bonus increases to +5.

F - Until your next turn starts, creatures suffer disadvantage when executing ranged attacks against you. From the 10th level, you also gain +2 AC against all ranged attacks aimed at you.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 186

feature.name: Further The Cycle (Shepherd)
feature.text:
Starting at 2nd level, when making a move in your Cycle of Redemption, you can choose to move twice instead of just once. You can only use this ability again after a short or long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 187

feature.name: Saved By Ray (Shepherd)
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, your positive ray grants your target advantage on all saves imposed by unnatural creatures (penumbral creatures, Ungods, undead, aberrations, or as determined by your GM in other settings) until your next turn starts. At 9th level, each time you employ your positive ray using the Magic in Ray ability, you also heal 1d8 hit points of your target in addition to other effects.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 187

feature.name: Shepherd Extra Spells (Shepherd)
feature.text:
At 3rd, 7th, 10th, 13th and 16th levels, following the table below, you learn a new spell, which counts as a cleric spell for you and doesn't count against your number of spells known.

Extra Spells:
Level | Extra Spell
3rd | goodberry
7th | hypnotic pattern
10th | dream
13th | magnificent mansion
16th | sunburst

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 187

feature.name: Empowered Rays (Shepherd)
feature.text:
Starting at 6th level, when you release one of your rays, add your Charisma modifier to the damage dealt or the temporary hit points provided by your ray

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 187

feature.name: Reform Argument (Shepherd)
feature.text:
At 10th level, if you fail a Charisma ability check when addressing a crowd or group, you can swiftly rephrase your argument, enabling you to reroll the check and take the new result. You can use this ability a number of times equivalent to your Charisma modifier. You regain all uses after a long rest.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 187

feature.name: Crowd Leader (Shepherd)
feature.text:
Starting at 15th level, your role as a Shepherd provides you with exceptional skills in engaging with crowds and building trust with individual members. When making a Charisma (Performance) check to interact with a non-hostile group of at least three creatures, you can add your proficiency bonus in Deception or Persuasion to the check in addition to your proficiency in Performance. If the check succeeds, you capture the absolute attention of the creatures, instilling trust in them during the interaction, and they have a disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks for anything besides you during this period.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 187

feature.name: Mob Mentality (Shepherd)
feature.text:
At 18th level, you can once per day influence a group of creatures by bending their will to your commands. Any individual who can hear and comprehend your speech for 1 minute must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature that fails will pursue the course of action you described as if affected by the suggestion spell, behaving this way until the order is completed or 7 days have passed. The course of action must be expressed in one or two sentences, and follows the same restrictions and limitations as the suggestion spell.
	This effect isn't considered magical but is instead the result of your powerful persuasiveness, so affected creatures will feel persuaded rather than enchanted or manipulated. Affected creatures have advantage on saving throws against any effect that would compel them to act against your suggestion.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 187

trait.name: Redeemer
trait.text:
Amidst the bustling city, a tiefling preacher stands on a crate, captivating the faithful with honeyed words that evoke adulation. The crowd showers him with trinkets and coins, and he catches them with a sly smile, claiming the treasures in the name of the gods. But the faithful can't help but wonder if his motives are pure, and if their requests will come true.
	As the sun sets, a cirrus enters the home of an ailing child, unnoticed by all. The parents offer everything they have, believing in the wanderer's saintly aura. With a gentle touch, the cirrus fills the room with hope, and the child is miraculously cured. The guardian angel fades into the night, never seeking payment or recognition. A silent and selfless savior.
	In a murky alleyway, an elf waits for bandits and their stolen gold. When they appear, he unleashes an inky burst of energy, sending one of the thieves flying. The others falter, and the elf claims the coins as a reward for justice. Many question his methods, and if his desire for retribution goes too far. The elf justifies his actions as the means to a righteous end.
	Redeemers are divine spellcasters chosen by the gods, using energy rays to heal or harm. Guided by prophetic dreams, they possess unique charisma and influence to inspire others. They purify negative emotions, bestow blessings and are embodiments of Tamera and Bauron's duality.
	Across the vast eons of Tanares, redeemers have served as divine emissaries of the celestial deities Tamera and Bauron, bestowed with divine magic and exceptional charisma. Endowed with a natural ability to move mortal hearts, they develop a plethora of skills, individually guided by their prophetic dreams and visions of destiny. Bound by their divine calling, redeemers tread a unique path, interpreting and sharing their revelations of the gods' will, which grants them profound insights into the world.
	Amidst the spreading darkness of the Ungods' corruption, redeemers emerge as spiritual beacons, wielding their divine gifts to cleanse objects tainted by mortal sins and malevolent desires. In doing so, they turn these once-corrupted items into wellsprings of sacred power, banishing the influence of the Ungods and gaining power to give their blessings upon those in need.
	As visionaries of unrivaled allure, redeemers shepherd their followers, inspiring unwavering faith in their divine guidance. Skilled in the arts of negotiation, trade, and leadership, they serve as revered advisors and orators, their celestial blessings from both Tamera and Baron granting them a harmonious perspective on the world and the wisdom to find balance between extremes.
	Though their convictions may diverge from established doctrines and from each other, most redeemers remain united by their divine purpose. Their liberty of belief extends even to those who renounce the gods, embracing twisted philosophies to justify their actions. Yet, their divine powers remain undiminished, stirring fervent discourse within the halls of the Celestianist Church regarding their sacred nature.
	As prophets and visionaries, redeemers effortlessly draw adherents to their cause, forming tight-knit circles of devout believers. With their vast array of divine spells and their innate ability to perceive the emotions of others, they become sought after by those yearning for spiritual guidance and divine intervention.

Source:	Player's Guide to Tanares p. 178 (Indie)

trait.name: Redeemer History
trait.text:
In the nascent days of Tanares, when the divine permeated the land, an extraordinary caste of individuals arose. Consecrated by the deities Tamera and Bauron, they came to be known as the redeemers. At first, these divine envoys were scarce and enigmatic, yet their influence would reverberate across the ages, shaping the world in ways both profound and nuanced.
	Among these celestial emissaries were the cirrus Windspeakers, who partook of the gods' words through the angels that forged them. They were but the vanguard of the redeemers who would traverse Tanares' realms, guided by prophetic dreams and visions heralding the world's pivotal moments.
	Throughout the epochs, redeemers have stirred cult followings with their singular interpretations of divine will. Yet their distinctive wisdom and divine endowments have incurred the wrath of the Evolutionist Church, which sought to suppress them in its quest for spiritual hegemony.
	As the Evolutionist Church ascended to prominence, wielding unparalleled might and sway, it came to regard redeemers and the cirrus people with contempt. The redeemers' distinctive interpretations of sacred texts and their god-given powers were perceived as a threat to the Church's dominion. This tension ultimately culminated in a campaign of persecution, with the Church hunting redeemers and driving the cirrus species to the brink of extinction.
	In contemporary times, the Evolutionist Church has undergone a metamorphosis. With the return of a few angels to the mortal plane, the Church has been compelled to confront the corruption within its echelons and the manipulation of its sacred texts by the insidious Ungods' agents entrenched in the Church's ecclesiastical hierarchy. In response, the Church has rebranded itself as the Celestianist Church, embarking on sweeping reforms to expunge the Cult of Shadow Wing from its midst.
	In this era, redeemers took even greater prevalence. Their divine gifts and prophetic insights, once spurned by the Evolutionist Church, are now embraced by many within the reformed Celestianist Church. Nevertheless, some redeemers harbor mistrust towards the Church's past transgressions and choose to maintain their autonomy, cultivating their own followings and interpreting the gods' will as they deem appropriate.
	The redeemers' tenacity and adaptability have enabled them to endure millennia of persecution and transformation. Today, their divine powers and unyielding convictions remain as potent as ever. As charismatic leaders, spiritual guides, great prophets, and potent spellcasters, the redeemers stand as pivotal figures in the politics and power struggles among the diverse factions and kingdoms seeking to sway the common people to advance their agendas.

trait.name: Purging the Corruption
trait.text:
Unfettered by dogma or doctrine, most of these consecrated beings follow their personal convictions, channeling their divine-bestowed powers to purify Tanares and battle the sinister Ungods.
	Gifted with an unparalleled aptitude for discerning and extracting malevolent energies from precious objects, redeemers transmute these dark forces into sanctified blessings. They personify the restorative radiance of Tamera and the annihilating fury of Bauron, embodying a duality that empowers them to expunge Tanares of the corruption spawned by the nefarious Ungods.
	In their call against the forces of darkness, redeemers are guided by cryptic dreams and prophetic visions bestowed by Tamera and Bauron. This divine foresight enables them to undermine their adversaries and tilt the balance in the protracted, ages-old struggle that has determined the destiny of Tanares.
	All too aware of the redeemers' formidable abilities, the Ungods contrive insidious stratagems to thwart their celestial foes. They desecrate temples, infiltrate religious institutions, manipulate governing bodies against rising redeemers, and foment dissension among believers in a bid to sabotage the redeemers' influence and obstruct their divine mission.
	Yet, redeemers possess a steadfast conviction that remains unshaken, employing their versatile talents to surmount the challenges of their sacred vocation. Through their divine revelations, redeemers frequently find themselves in the path of the Ungods' schemes, either consciously or inadvertently wielding their extraordinary powers to shield Tanares from the darkness that seeks to engulf it.
	In a realm plagued by corruption, redeemers stand as instruments of the gods, their divine endowments a testament to the might of Tamera and Bauron, and their conferred gifts a beacon of hope in the battle to purify Tanares from the malevolence that imperils it.

trait.name: Religious Conflicts in Tanares
trait.text:
Tanares, a land steeped in diverse and tumultuous religious traditions, has long been a crucible for conflicting ideologies. Redeemers have historically stood amidst this strife, their unique insights into the divine will often clashing with prevailing dogmas of established institutions. Despite these variations, redeemers have consistently demonstrated an ability to wield divine powers, often leading to the formation of devoted followings. This only served to fuel further conflict, providing ample opportunities for the sinister Ungods and their minions to sow discord and manipulate opposing factions, ultimately corrupting the souls of the fallen.
	The Celestianist Church, formerly known as the Evolutionist Church, venerates the celestial deities Tamera and Bauron and remains the dominant religious institution in Tanares. Despite recent major reforms, spurred by angelic revelations regarding the true nature of the gods and the corruption of sacred scriptures by the Cult of Shadow Wing, the Church maintains its power and structure in the land.
	Ranged against the Celestianists are various factions, including the insidious Cult of Shadow Wing, which favors the four Ungods seeking to engulf Tanares in corruption. The fallen elven goddess Bás, while also opposed to the Ungods, is an enemy of the Church too, due to her apocalyptic solution that defends a world of ice and the undead.
	While the Ba-Ka faith, worshiping the Spirit God of Magic, had historically clashed with the Evolutionist Church due to the Evolutionists aversion to arcane magic, the Celestianist reform has eased tensions between them, albeit with lingering distrust. The Cuibhle Pantheon, an elven religion venerating elemental deities, has forged an alliance with the Celestianist Church against Bás and the Cult of Shadow Wing.
	Other faiths, such as Luminism, Fumetsu Eido, Fruitlism, and Dorsianism, occupy unique positions in Tanares. Lumina, the Goddess of Wisdom, has formed a new alliance with the Celestianist Church, while Fumetsu Tenshikin, a dragon claiming godhood through angelic artifacts, has transitioned from a tolerated enemy to an uneasy ally. Fruitful, a halfling deity, and Dorsi, the Guardian God of dwarves, both enjoy strong relationships with the reformed Church.
	However, it is the Windspeaker religion of the cirrus people that best exemplifies the religious turmoil that has historically plagued Tanares. The cirrus, once a thriving civilization, were nearly eradicated by the Evolutionist Church's inquisition, which condemned the Windspeaker faith as heresy due to its divergent interpretations of sacred scriptures. The reformed Celestianists, despite theological differences, now seek to mend relations with the surviving cirrus and Windspeakers.
These religious divisions and alliances, complex in nature, share a common theme: the interplay of divine power and mortal interpretation. Redeemers, with their unique divinely inspired dreams, have only further fueled these conflicts, as their singular visions rarely align with the religious interpretations of others.
	With recent revelations concerning the gods' true nature and the corrupted sacred scriptures, the religious landscape in Tanares teeters on the precipice of a new era. While some redeemers have joined the reformed Celestianist Church to help cleanse it of corruption, others remain cautious of the institution's past and continue to pursue their divine callings independently.
	The religious strife in Tanares, shaped by the interplay of divine gifts and mortal interpretation, continues to mold the destiny of this multifaceted realm. As new alliances form and old adversaries reemerge, the redeemers find themselves both catalysts and agents of change in this ever-evolving tapestry of faiths and religions.

trait.name: Preachers, Merchants and Community Leaders
trait.text:
and Community Leaders The redeemers, as heavenly conduits of the divine twins Tamera and Bauron, navigate the intricacies of Tanares with their celestial gifts, which manifest as both transcendent oratory and preternatural sagacity. These divine emissaries, with their captivating presence, serve as harbingers of the gods' wisdom and custodians of sacred relics.
	By day, most redeemers traverse the social tapestry, pursuing their celestial mandates while tending to their communities, confronting the Ungods' corruption, and bestowing their blessings upon the deserving. As influential orators, they amass devout adherents who heed their inspiring exegeses of sacred texts and dreams, forging new communities and sanctuaries that espouse their doctrines.
	Understanding the significance of wealth in furthering their divine mission, redeemers often embrace roles as prosperous merchants or astute investors. However, they perceive riches as a means to an end—a vessel through which to channel their blessings and advance their cause—rather than an object of materialistic desire.
	The redeemers' ethical compass transcends the confines of earthly institutions, often placing them at odds with established religious orders such as the Celestianist Church. Despite these tensions, some redeemers ally with the Church to amplify their influence, while others retain their independence, disseminating their personal interpretations of scripture and gathering followers as prophetic visionaries.

trait.name: Prophetic Dreams
trait.text:
The dreams of the redeemers are steeped in mystique, woven from ethereal reveries and enigmatic signs gifted by their celestial patrons, Tamera and Bauron. Unlike the unwavering conduits of the divine, who draw upon celestial energies through steadfast devotion, the redeemers first awaken their spellcasting prowess amidst visions of resplendent grandeur, infused with the very essence of divinity.

The recent resurgence of the angels saw them confirmed the divine origins of the redeemers' dreams and visions, emphasizing the need for discerning interpretation. Yet, the myriad conclaves of the redeemers are far from immune to internal strife. A great number of beliefs unfurl, as some advocate for collective endeavors to decipher the cryptic symbols embedded within the revelations, asserting that the wisdom of the most exalted should guide the interpretations. In stark contrast, others extol the merits of individual sovereignty, resolute in their belief that each redeemer must divine the meaning of their own visions, as the gods intended solely for the chosen recipient and no other.

This divergence of convictions gives birth to factions within the hallowed halls of the redeemers' temples, underscoring the unique nature of each redeemer's visions as they embark upon their sacred missions. Despite the turbulence, an atmosphere of mutual respect prevails, with the majority acknowledging the divine gifts of their brethren, united by their shared vocation to shepherd and uplift the denizens of Tanares and their unyielding bond with Tamera and Bauron.

trait.name: Redeemer Dreams
trait.text:
The redeemers possess a rare gift, one that allows them to receive prophetic dreams and visions from the gods. These dreams are not only meant to inspire and guide the redeemers themselves, but to aid and motivate others as well. The Dream Table outlines the different styles of these dreams in vivid detail, from the Empowering and Enlightening to the Lucid and Nightmarish. Each style is accompanied by a short description, a common use in campaigns, including an explanation of why the gods might choose to send such a dream, and an example of what one might look like.

These dreams can be a powerful tool in the hands of a skilled GM, one who can use them to weave a rich tapestry of story and character development. But they should not be viewed as a shortcut or a means of bypassing important plot elements. Instead, they should be employed to help players deal with unsolved challenging puzzles or overlooked plot hooks. The gods should always be on the side of the redeemers, guiding them towards success, but never at the expense of overall enjoyment of all players.

Style of Dream | Description | Use | Example
Empowering:
The redeemer has complete mastery over their powers and abilities in a dream, and utilizes them to achieve great victories, exploring their full potential.
	Allows the redeemer to see where they are failing to best utilize their skills and how to implement better strategies. The gods use this method to empower the redeemer and help them grow in power and skill.
	The redeemer failed in a recent encounter because they didn't know how to use their powers effectively. In an Empowering dream, they are shown how to better utilize their abilities, waking with newfound confidence.

Enlightening:
The redeemer experiences a profound moment of insight or clarity, allowing them to understand a previously unknown truth.
	Provides the redeemer with information that they did not have previously, allowing them to solve a puzzle, understand a situation, or make an important decision. The gods use this method to reveal hidden knowledge and provide the redeemer with greater understanding.
	The redeemer has been trying to uncover the secret of a puzzling letter, but neither they nor their friends can solve it. In a dream, the gods show a clue that helps them connect the dots and identify the solution.

Lucid:
The redeemer realizes that they are dreaming and can control their actions in the dream, as if they were awake.
	Allows the redeemer to explore new scenarios, try out new abilities, or have a fun diversion from the campaign. The gods use this method to allow the redeemer to have a personal experience with them or other servants of the gods, in a place separate from the events of the physical world.
	The redeemer has been feeling stressed out and burned out from the amount of combat and traps they are facing in a dungeon. In a dream, they have a relaxing vacation in a tropical paradise, where they interact with different people that may provide new information or quests.

Nightmarish:
The redeemer is plagued by terrible visions of death, destruction, or loss.
	Creates tension, provides a warning, or sets up future events. The gods use this method to instill a sense of urgency or fear in the redeemer, motivating them to act.
	The redeemer has been feeling uneasy about a recent peace treaty signed with a neighboring nation. In a dream, they see a terrible vision of the treaty falling apart as one of the diplomats dies.

Past Life:
The redeemer experiences a dream that seems to be from a past life or the life of an ancestor, providing them with insight into past history or about their own origins.
	Provides the redeemer with information about their character's past or provides them with insight into their own personal history. The gods use this method to provide the redeemer with information they lack about their own roots or to help them understand an important aspect of their character's backstory.
	The redeemer has a dream where they see themselves as a priestess in a long-ago battle and learn that the death knight that is now their enemy was once her beloved husband, who fell by the blades of its own traitorous comrades he swore to protect.

Prophetic:
The redeemer has a cryptic dream about a future event filled with symbolism and prophetic messages that are all connected to a critical situation they are in or will be in.
	This dream is useful for challenging the redeemer's ability to interpret signs and connect information, creating puzzles, and communicating a specific message or warning about the future. The gods use this method to ensure their intervention does not supersede mortal free will and agency.
	The redeemer dreams of a looming invasion of their home city and sees symbols and flashes of specific scenes, such as a golden glass filled with wine, a crown with 7 rubies, and a light pointing south. These symbols may mean that the culprit is one of the 7 lords of the south, the one known for its vineyard, leading the redeemer to investigate and interpret the signs to prevent the invasion.

Prophetic Warning:
The redeemer experiences a clear and direct vision that warns them of an impending disaster or danger, providing a clear goal, path, and call to action.
	This dream is useful for giving the redeemer a warning they can act upon and providing a clear command to intercede on a specific situation. The gods use this method to guide mortals in preventing disasters or preparing for upcoming events.
	The redeemer dreams of a dragon attacking a town at dawn, giving them the chance to return and prevent the disaster they missed due to not noticing the clues previously.

Recurring:
The redeemer has the same dream multiple times, with minor differences each time, providing a major long-term goal and small bits of help as they advance towards it.
	This dream is useful for providing the redeemer with a sense of direction and culminating in a big climax for their story. The gods use this method to guide mortals on long journeys.
	The redeemer dreams of standing in front of a mysterious locked door with a different symbol on it each time, gaining new information to interpret the symbol and ultimately unlocking the door to reveal its secret.

trait.name: Creating a Redeemer
trait.text:
The first step to creating your redeemer is to define their personal beliefs. While their power originates from the gods, it's important to consider what they believe the gods want from them and any prophetic dreams they may have had. Not all redeemers know precisely where their powers come from; they simply know that they are fueled by gold and other emotion-infused material goods. By defining your redeemer's beliefs, you can map out the discourse they will adopt—one of divine salvation or personal fulfillment, for example.

Once you have established your redeemer's beliefs, consider what they do with the gold they receive. Do they use their powers to help people in the best way possible, fulfilling their desires? Or do they move from town to town, collecting gold from the desperate and becoming rich? Do they view other redeemers as competitors or potential allies who can help them solve people's problems?

Finally, it's important to define what led your character into the life of adventure. Were they seeking an easier way to obtain gold and artifacts? Did they have a divine dream that drove them to adventure? Are they looking for protection by being part of a team, or do they want to gather an army to prepare for the Armageddon? Perhaps they seek to spread the word of the gods to as many people as possible. Whatever the case, understanding your redeemer's motivations and beliefs will help you create a rich and engaging character for your campaign.
