Roll the Bardic Inspiration die and refer to the Spirits from Beyond table to determine the spirit you channel, then choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself as the spirit's target. The spirit immediately takes effect; if a spirit's effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals your Bard spell save DC.

Spirits from Beyond:
Bardic Insp. Die | Spirit
1 | Beloved. The target regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Charisma modifier.
2 | Sharpshooter. The target takes Force damage equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Charisma modifier.
3 | Avenger. Until the end of your next turn, any creature that hits the target with a melee attack roll takes Force combined into a single feature, Channeler. This new damage equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die.
4 | Renegade. The target can immediately take a Reaction to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
5 | Fortune Teller. The target has Advantage on D20 Tests until the start of your next turn.
6 | Wayfarer. The target gains Temporary Hit Points equal to a roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Bard level. While it has these Temporary Hit Points, the target's Speed increases by 10 feet.
7 | Trickster. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes Psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die and has the Charmed condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.
8 | Shade. The target gains the Invisible condition until the end of its next turn or until the target makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell. When the invisibility ends, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take Necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die.
9 | Arsonist. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking Fire damage equal to four rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.
10 | Coward. The target and each creature of your choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the start of your next turn. While Frightened, a creature's Speed is halved, and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action, not both.
11 | Brute. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Thunder damage equal to three rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die and has the Prone condition. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.
12 | Controlled Channeling. You determine the spirit's effect by choosing one of the other rows in this table.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 3

feature.name: Level 6: Empowered Channeling (College of Spirits (UA))
feature.text:
Your ability to channel spirits improves. You gain the following benefits.

	Power from Beyond. Once per turn, when you cast a Bard spell that deals damage or restores Hit Points, roll a d6. You gain a bonus to one of the spell's damage rolls or to the total Hit Points the spell restores equal to the number rolled.

	Spiritual Manifestation. You always have the Spirit Guardians spell prepared. You can cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest.

Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so the spirits also guard against worldly threats. When cast in this way, you and allies within the spell's Emanation have Half Cover. Once you modify the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 4

feature.name: Level 14: Mystical Connection (College of Spirits (UA))
feature.text:
You gain mastery over the spirits you call forth. Whenever you roll on the Spirits from Beyond table, you can roll the die twice and choose which of the two effects to bestow.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 4

feature.name: Bard Subclass: College of Dolce Stil Novo (HB)
feature.text:
Weave magic through their poetic language and transcendent visions

E io a lui: «I' mi son un che, quando
Amor mi spira, noto, e a quel modo
ch'e' ditta dentro vo significando».
«O frate, issa vegg'io», diss'elli, «il nodo
che 'l Notaro e Guittone e me ritenne
di qua dal dolce stil novo ch'i' odo!
— Divine Comedy, Purgatory XXIV, vv. 52-57

Theme: This subclass connects directly to the Dolce Stil Novo's ideals of love and divine beauty as transcendent forces. Each feature reflects the poets' ability to inspire and captivate both allies and adversaries.

The name ('sweet new style') comes from a dialogue in Dante's Purgatorio (xxiv. 57). This style is marked mainly by praise of the beloved in religious terms as an embodiment of divine grace, an attitude seemingly influenced by troubadour poetry and the codes of courtly love.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 11 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Poetic Transcendence (College of Dolce Stil Novo (HB))
feature.text:
You channel your bardic magic through refined and metaphysical poetry, inspiring profound thoughts and feelings.

	Inspiration of Love. When a creature uses your Bardic Inspiration die, it regains hit points equal to the number rolled + your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).

	Stanza of Enlightenment. As a Bonus Action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to recite a mystical stanza targeting one creature that can hear you within 30 feet of you. Choose one effect:

	• Hearts Opened. The target has Advantage on Charisma Tests until the end of your next turn.

	• Veil Lifted. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Disadvantage on its next Test.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 11 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Voice of the Muse (College of Dolce Stil Novo (HB))
feature.text:
Your connection to divine inspiration sharpens your eloquence and insight. You gain proficiency in Insight or Performance, and one additional language of your choice. You gain Expertise in one of these skills if you are already proficient in both.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 11 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Visionary Verse (College of Dolce Stil Novo (HB))
feature.text:
Your poetry channels visions of divine beauty and metaphysical truth that inspire or bewilder your audience.
	As a Magic Action, you can weave a Visionary Verse. Choose up to three creatures within 60 feet of you that can hear you:

	• Your Allies gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Bard level and have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened and Charmed conditions for 1 minute.

	• Creatures Hostile to you make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Blinded condition until the end of their next turn.

Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 11 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Divine Illumination (College of Dolce Stil Novo (HB))
feature.text:
Channeling the power of pure beauty and divine inspiration, as a Magic Action you invoke the highest ideals of the Dolce Stil Novo poets, that take the form of a 15-foot Emanation around you:

	Aura of Inspiration. While in the Emanation, your Allies are Immune to Psychic Damage and gain a bonus to their saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier. When the Emanation enters an Hostile creature's space and whenever that creature enters the Emanation for the first time in a turn, or starts its turn there, that creature makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Disadvantage on any Tests until the end of its next turn.

	Final Canticle. As a Magic Action, you can recite a canticle of divine love, ending the Emanation. Choose up to six creatures within 60 feet that can hear you. Your Allies regain Hit Points equal to 5d10 + your Bard level up to their maximum, and end one Condition affecting them. Hostile creatures make a DC Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: 6d10 Psychic damage and the Blinded condition until the end of their next turn. Success: half as much damage and no other ill effects on a successful save.

Once you use this feature, you can't use them again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 11 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Bard Subclass: College of Skalds (HB)
feature.text:
Drawing power from epic tales

Theme: Norse warrior-poets who inspire allies with tales of heroism and channel primal rage and magic.

Playstyle: Martial and supportive. Combines combat prowess with powerful rallying abilities for a battlefield leader role.

Skalds, or skálds (meaning "poet" in Old Norse), were poets who composed skaldic poetry, one of the two kinds of Old Norse poetry in alliterative verse, the other being Eddic poetry. Skaldic poems were traditionally composed to honor kings, but were sometimes ex tempore. They include both extended works and single verses.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 9 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Skald's Inspiration (College of Skalds (HB))
feature.text:
When you join the College of the Skald at 3rd level, your Bardic Inspiration takes on a martial edge. You gain the following benefits:

	Battle Chant. When a creature uses your Bardic Inspiration die, they can choose to deal extra damage equal to the die roll on a weapon attack or gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the roll.

	Tales of the Ancestors. You learn one additional spell from the Bard Spell List. This spell must be of a level you can cast, and it doesn't count against your spells known.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 9 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Words of Fury (College of Skalds (HB))
feature.text:
You can stir the hearts of your Allies into a battle frenzy. As a Bonus Action, you can use your Bardic Inspiration to target up to five creatures that you can see within 30 feet of you.
	These creatures gain one of the following benefits of your choice until the start of your next turn:

	• Advantage on attack rolls.
	• A +2 bonus to their AC

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 9 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Saga of Heroes (College of Skalds (HB))
feature.text:
You invoke the tales of legendary Norse warriors to inspire greatness in your allies. You have the following 

	Saga's Guidance. As a Magic Action, you can choose up to 3 creatures within 60 feet of you. Each creature gains Temporary Hit points equal to twice your Bard level and can add your Charisma modifier to one Test of their choice within the next minute.

	Warding Runes. When a creature that is Allied to you that you can see within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can use your Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d10 + your Charisma modifier.

You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 9 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Valkyries' Call (College of Skalds (HB))
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, You call upon the Valkyries, the legendary spirits of battle, that flit around you in a 30-foot Emanation that lasts for 1 minute. While in the Emanation:

	• Your Allies have advantage on Death Saving Throws and saving throws against the Frightened condition.

	• When your Allies take damage, they can use their Reaction to move up to 15 feet and make a single weapon attack.

	• Hostile Creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 9 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Bard Subclass: College of the Cabaret (HB)
feature.text:
Extravagant master performer

Theme: Flamboyant and provocative performers who beguile and dazzle through sharp wit and charm.

Playstyle: Battlefield control and charm. Uses subversive magic to hinder enemies while uplifting allies.

Referencing the period between 1871 to 1914, La Belle Époque literally means "the beautiful era" in French. In more ways than one, La Belle Époque has been regarded as Europe's golden age, a remarkable time that significantly altered the history of the continent and beyond. The Cabaret is a form of theatrical entertainment featuring music, song, dance, recitation, or drama. The performance venue might be a pub, a casino, a hotel, a restaurant, or a nightclub with a stage for performances. The audience, often dining or drinking, does not typically dance but usually sits at tables.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 16 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Dazzling Presence (College of the Cabaret (HB))
feature.text:
Your performances captivate and confuse onlookers.

	Flamboyant Wit. When you cast a spell that targets a creature, you can use your Bonus Action to distract another creature that can see you within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Disadvantage on its Tests until the end of your next turn.

	Performance Expertise. You gain Expertise in Performance, and you can use Charisma (Performance) checks in place of Dexterity (Stealth) when attempting to blend into a crowd.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 16 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Revelry's Charm (College of the Cabaret (HB))
feature.text:
Your revelry bolsters allies and disorients foes. As a Bonus Action, you can affect up to 6 creatures that can hear or see you within 60 feet of you.

	• For 1 minute, your Allies gain temporary hit points equal to your Bardic Inspiration die at the start of each of their turns.

	• For 1 minute, at the start of each of their turns, creatures Hostile to you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Disadvantage on any attack roll until the end of their turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a 3+ level spell slot (no action required).

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 16 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Grand Finale (College of the Cabaret (HB))
feature.text:
Your ultimate performance leaves audiences awestruck. As a Magic Action, you unleash a performance that affects all creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you that can hear or see you:

	• Your Allies gain 5d10 temporary hit points, can immediately make a weapon attack as a Reaction, and have Advantage on all saving throws for 1 minute.

	• Creatures Hostile to you must make a Wisdom against your spell save DC. Failure: Stunned condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its next turns, an affected creature can make another Wisdom saving throw, ending the condition on itself on a success.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 16 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Bard Subclass: College of the Elizabethan Theatre (HB)
feature.text:
Enhance acting with magic

Theme: Every feature draws from the spirit of Elizabethan theatre, blending the emotions of tragedy and comedy with the grandeur of live performance.

Playstyle: Versatile performer. Its playstyle is a balance of social manipulation, adaptability, and combat trickery.

Elizabethan theatre, sometimes called English Renaissance theatre, refers to that style of performance plays which blossomed during the reign of Elizabeth I of England and which continued under her Stuart successors.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 13 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Theatrical Persona (College of the Elizabethan Theatre (HB))
feature.text:
You adopt the larger-than-life personas of the stage to captivate and inspire.

	Masks of the Stage. As a Bonus action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to assume a theatrical persona, such as the Tragic Hero, the Comedic Fool, or the Noble Monarch, granting you the following benefits for 1 minute:

	Tragic Hero. When you or a creature Allied to you that you can see within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can use your Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d6 + your Charisma modifier.

	Comedic Fool. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Disadvantage on their next Test.

	Noble Monarch. You and your Allies within 10 feet of you gain Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened and Charmed condition.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 13 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Wordsmith's Wit (College of the Elizabethan Theatre (HB))
feature.text:
Your mastery of dialogue and soliloquy sharpens your ability to manipulate social situations.

	• You gain Proficiency in Deception or Persuasion. You gain Expertise in one of these skills if you are already proficient in both.

	• When you cast a level 1+ spell from the Enchantment Scholl that forces a creature to make a saving throw, you can use your Reaction to give that creature Disadvantage on the roll. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 13 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Playwright's Performance (College of the Elizabethan Theatre (HB))
feature.text:
You bring the power of the stage to life, crafting moments of triumph or despair. As a Magic Action, you create a magical performance that affects up to a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1) within 30 feet. Choose one effect:

	Tragedy. Creatures of your choice that can see or hear you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: 3d8 Psychic damage and Frightened condition until the end of your next turn. Success: Half damage.

	Comedy. Creatures of your choice that can hear or see you regain hit points equal to 2d8 + your Charisma modifier and gain temporary hit points equal to your Bard level.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a 3+ level spell slot (no action required).

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 13 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Stage of Destiny (College of the Elizabethan Theatre (HB))
feature.text:
You create an ethereal magical stage that manifests around you in a 15-foot Emanation that symbolizes themes of Elizabethan theatre to inspire or terrify those who witness it. The Emanation lasts for 1 minute.

	Grand Performance. Within:

	• Your Allies that can see the Emanation have Advantage on their Tests.
	• Creatures Hostile to you the Emanation have Disadvantage on their Tests.

	Dramatic Finale. Once during this feature's duration, you can deliver a climactic soliloquy as a Magic Action. Choose one of the following effects:

	• The Triumph: Your Allies within the Emanation regain 6d10 Hit Points and can immediately use their Reaction to move up to their speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

	• The Fall: Creatures Hostile to you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: 6d10 Psychic damage and Stunned condition until the end of your next turn. Success: Half damage.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 14 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Bard Subclass: College of the Minnesingers (HB)
feature.text:
Make extraordinary endeavors through love and magic

Theme: Romantic and spiritual devotion, uplifting allies through love and reverence.

Playstyle: Protective and defensive. Focuses on emotional bonds and resilience, heavily leaning into themes of chivalric love and faith.

Minnesingers flourished in the Middle-High German period (XII to XIV century). The name derives from Minne, the Middle High German word for love, as that was Minnesang's main subject. People who wrote and performed Minnesang were known as Minnesänger. and a single song was called a Minnelied. The Minnesänger are comparable to the Occitan troubadours and northern French trouvères, but they are "an original German contribution to courtly lyric."

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 15 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Devotion's Blessing (College of the Minnesingers (HB))
feature.text:
Your words of love and reverence inspire resilience and determination.

	Aura of Inspiration. When you confer a Bardic Inspiration die to a creature, that creature also gains temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).

	Song of Reverence. As a Bonus Action, you can perform a hymn of devotion. Choose one creature that can hear you within 30 feet of you. That creature gains advantage on its next attack until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 15 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Eternal Love (College of the Minnesingers (HB))
feature.text:
Your devotion creates an unbreakable bond. When a creature Allied to you that you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your Reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your Bardic Inspiration die + your Charisma modifier.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 15 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Minne's Transcendence (College of the Minnesingers (HB))
feature.text:
Your love and reverence transcend the material, uplifting allies and overwhelming foes.As Bonus action, you can sing a divine ode of love. Each creature of your choice that can hear you within 30 feet of you has the following effects:

	• Your Allies have Advantage on saving throws and gain a bonus to attack rolls equal to your Charisma modifier for 1 minute.

	• Hostile creatures must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Incapacitated condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its next turns, an affected creature can make another Charisma saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 15 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Bard Subclass: College of the Troubadour (HB)
feature.text:
Dashing poet-musician in noble courts

Theme: Romantic poet-musicians of medieval France, weaving love and beauty into magic, embodying the spirit of medieval France's traveling poet-musicians, celebrated for their romantic ballads, satirical wit, and courtly presence.

Playstyle: Supportive and enchanting. Focuses on emotional connection and protective magic, with a hint of summoning.

Troubadours were composers and performesr of Old Occitan lyric poetry during the High Middle Ages (1100-1350 AD). The troubadour school or tradition began in the late 11th century in Occitania, but it subsequently spread to the Italian and Iberian Peninsulas. Under the influence of the troubadours, related movements sprang up throughout Europe. After the "classical" period around the turn of the 13th century and a mid-century resurgence, the art of the troubadours declined in the 14th century and around the time of the Black Death (1348) and since died out. The texts of troubadour songs deal mainly with themes of chivalry and courtly love. Most were metaphysical, intellectual, and formulaic. Many were humorous or vulgar satires.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 10 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Ballad of Inspiration (College of the Troubadour (HB))
feature.text:
Your Bardic Inspiration becomes deeply emotional, evoking feelings of love, valor, or wit. You gain the following traits:

	Chivalric Flai. When a creature uses your Bardic Inspiration die, it gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). Additionally, the creature can move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

	Poet's Wit. When you use Bardic Inspiration, you can also target a Hostile creature within 30 feet of you. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Disadvantage on its next attack roll or saving throw before the start of your next turn.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 10 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Courtly Grace (College of the Troubadour (HB))
feature.text:
Your training in etiquette and charm allows you to manipulate social interactions.
	You gain Proficiency in Persuasion or Performance Skill. If you are already proficient, you gain Expertise in that skill.
	As a Reaction, when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll or saving throw, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration to roll the die and either add it to the roll or subtract it.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 10 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Troubadour's Serenade (College of the Troubadour (HB))
feature.text:
You can entrance others with your music and poetry.
	As a Magic Action, you can perform a magical serenade that affects up to a number of creatures that can hear you equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1) within 30 feet of you. Each creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Failure: Charmed condition for 1 minute or until it takes damage. A Charmed creature has also the Incapacitated condition, enraptured by your performance. At the end of each of its next turn, a Charmed creature can make another Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 10 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Hymn of Devotion (College of the Troubadour (HB))
feature.text:
Your songs and poetry channel a powerful magic that inspires loyalty and passion.
	As a Bonus Action, you can affect each creature of your choice other than you within 30 feet of you that can hear you. Target creatures are Immune to the Frightened and Charmed condition for 1 minute and gain 30 Temporary Hit Points at the start of each of their next turns for 1 minute.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 10 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Cleric [5.5e]
fields.proficiency: Wisdom, Charisma, History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, Religion

trait.name: Cleric
trait.text:
Clerics draw power from the realms of the gods and harness it to work miracles. Blessed by a deity, a pantheon, or another immortal entity, a Cleric can reach out to the divine magic of the Outer Planes—where gods dwell—and channel it to bolster people and battle foes.
	Because their power is a divine gift, Clerics typically associate themselves with temples dedicated to the deity or other immortal force that unlocked their magic. Harnessing divine magic doesn't rely on specific training, yet Clerics might learn prayers and rites that help them draw on power from the Outer Planes.
	Not every member of a temple or shrine is a Cleric. Some priests are called to a simple life of temple service, carrying out their devotion through prayer and rituals, not through magic. Many mortals claim to speak for the gods, but few can marshal the power of those gods the way a Cleric can.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 69

feature.name: Becoming A Cleric As A Level 1 Character
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Cleric, you begin play with 8 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

Core Cleric Traits:
	• Primary Ability: Wisdom
	• Hit Point Die: D8 per Cleric level
	• Saving Throw Proficiencies: Wisdom and Charisma
	• Skill Proficiencies: Choose 2: History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, or Religion
	• Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons
	• Armor Training: Light and Medium armor and Shields

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background (choose A or B):
	• (A) Chain Shirt, Shield, Mace, Holy Symbol, Priest's Pack, and 7 GP
	• (B) 110 GP

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 69

feature.name: Becoming A Cleric As A Multiclass Character
feature.text:
Core Cleric Traits:
	• Primary Ability: Wisdom
	• Hit Point Die: D8 per Cleric level
	• Armor Training: Light and Medium armor and Shields

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 69

feature.name: Level 1: Spellcasting
feature.text:
You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Cleric spells, which appear on the Cleric spell list later in the class's description.

	Cantrips. You know three cantrips of your choice from the Cleric spell list. Guidance, Sacred Flame, and Thaumaturgy are recommended.
	Whenever you gain a Cleric level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Cleric spell list.
	When you reach Cleric levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Cleric spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Cleric Features table.

	Spell Slots. The Cleric Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

	Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Cleric spell list. Bless, Cure Wounds, Guiding Bolt, and Shield of Faith are recommended.
	The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Cleric levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Cleric Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Cleric spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Cleric, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels. 1 and 2 in any combination.
	If another Cleric feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Cleric spells for you.

	Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Cleric spells for which you have spell slots.

	Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Cleric spells.

	Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Holy Symbol as a Spellcasting Focus for your Cleric spells.

feature.name: Level 1: Divine Order: Thaumaturge
feature.text:
You know one extra cantrip from the Cleric spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to the divine gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 70

feature.name: Level 2: Channel Divinity
feature.text:
You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Divine Spark and Turn Undead, each of which is described below. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, choose which Channel Divinity effect from this class to create. You gain additional effect options at higher Cleric levels.
	You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You gain additional uses when you reach certain Cleric levels, as shown in the Channel Divinity column of the Cleric Features table.
	If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 70

feature.name: Level 2: Channel Divinity: Divine Spark
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you point your Holy Symbol at another creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself and focus divine energy at it. Roll 1d8 and add your Wisdom modifier. You either restore Hit Points to the creature equal to that total or force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to that total. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage (round down).
	You roll an additional d8 when you reach Cleric levels 7 (2d8), 13 (3d8), and 18 (4d8).

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 70

feature.name: Level 2: Channel Divinity: Turn Undead
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and censure Undead creatures. Each Undead of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its save, it has the Frightened and Incapacitated conditions for 1 minute. For that duration, it tries to move as far from you as it can on its turns. Th is effect ends early on the creature if it takes any damage, if you have the Incapacitated condition, or if you die.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 70

feature.name: Level 3: Cleric Subclass
feature.text:
You gain a Cleric subclass of your choice. The Life Domain, Light Domain, Trickery Domain, and War Domain subclasses are detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Cleric levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Cleric level or lower.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 5: Sear Undead
feature.text:
Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8) and add the rolls together. Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll's total. This damage doesn't end the turn effect.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 7: Blessed Strikes
feature.text:
Divine power infuses you in battle. You gain one of the following options of your choice (if you get either option from a Cleric subclass in an older book, use only the option you choose for this feature).

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 7: Blessed Strikes: Divine Strike
feature.text:
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can cause the target to take an extra 1d8 Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 7: Blessed Strikes: Potent Spellcasting
feature.text:
Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 8: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 10: Divine Intervention
feature.text:
You can call on your deity or pantheon to intervene on your behalf. As a Magic action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a Reaction to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. You can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 12: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 14: Improved Blessed Strikes
feature.text:
The option you chose for Blessed Strikes grows more powerful.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 14: Improved Blessed Strikes: Divine Strike
feature.text:
The extra damage of your Divine Strike increases to 2d8.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 14: Improved Blessed Strikes: Potent Spellcasting
feature.text:
When you cast a Cleric cantrip and deal damage to a creature with it, you can give vitality to yourself or another creature within 60 feet of yourself, granting a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 16: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 19: Epic Boon
feature.text:
You gain an Epic Boon feat (see chapter 5) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Level 20: Greater Divine Intervention
feature.text:
You can call on even more powerful divine intervention. When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose Wish when you select a spell. If you do so, you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish 2d4 Long Rests.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 71

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Life Domain
feature.text:
Soothe the Hurts of the World

The Life Domain focuses on the positive energy that helps sustain all life in the multiverse. Clerics who tap into this domain are masters of healing, using that life force to cure many hurts.
	Existence itself relies on the positive energy associated with this domain, so a Cleric of almost any religious tradition might choose it. This domain is particularly associated with agricultural deities. gods of healing or endurance. and gods of home and community. Religious orders of healing also seek the magic of this domain.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 73

feature.name: Level 3: Life Domain Spells (Life Domain)
feature.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Life Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Life Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Prepared Spells
3 | Aid, Bless, Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration
5 | Mass Healing Word, Revivify
7 | Aura of Life, Death Ward
9 | Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 73

feature.name: Level 3: Disciple of Life (Life Domain)
feature.text:
When a spell you cast with a spell slot restores Hit Points to a creature, that creature regains additional Hit Points on the turn you cast the spell. The additional Hit Points equal 2 plus the spell slot's level.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 73

feature.name: Level 3: Preserve Life (Life Domain)
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to evoke healing energy that can restore a number of Hit Points equal to five times your Cleric level. Choose Bloodied creatures within 30 feet of yourself (which can include you), and divide those Hit Points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half its Hit Point maximum.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 73

feature.name: Level 6: Blessed Healer (Life Domain)
feature.text:
The healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. Immediately after you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points to one or more creatures other than yourself, you regain Hit Points equal to 2 plus the spell slot's level.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 74

feature.name: Level 17: Supreme Healing (Life Domain)
feature.text:
When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore Hit Points to a creature with a spell or Channel Divinity, don't roll those dice for the healing; instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 Hit Points to a creature with a spell, you restore 12.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 74

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Light Domain
feature.text:
Bring Light to Banish Darkness

The Light Domain emphasizes the divine power to bring about blazing fire and revelation. Clerics who wield this power are enlightened souls infused with radiance and the power of their deities' discerning vision, charged with chasing away lies and burning away darkness.
	The Light Domain is associated with gods of truth, vigilance, beauty, insight, and renewal. Some of these gods are identified with the sun or as charioteers who guide the sun across the sky. Others are sentinels who pierce deception. Some are deities of beauty and artistry who teach that art is a vehicle for the soul's improvement.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 74

feature.name: Level 3: Light Domain Spells (Light Domain)
feature.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Light Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Light Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Prepared Spells
3 | Burning Hands, Faerie Fire, Scorching Ray, See Invisibility
5 | Daylight, Fireball
7 | Arcane Eye, Wall of Fire
9 | Flame Strike, Scrying

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 74

feature.name: Level 3: Radiance of the Dawn (Light Domain)
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to emit a flash of light in a 30-foot Emanation originating from yourself. Any magical Darkness-such as that created by the Darkness spell-in that area is dispelled. Additionally, each creature of your choice in that area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking Radiant damage equal to 2d10 plus your Cleric level on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 74

feature.name: Level 3: Warding Flare (Light Domain)
feature.text:
When a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself makes an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before it hits or misses.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 74

feature.name: Level 6: Improved Warding Flare (Light Domain)
feature.text:
You regain all expended uses of your Warding Flare when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
	In addition, whenever you use Warding Flare, you can give the target of the triggering attack a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to 2d6 plus your Wisdom modifier.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 75

feature.name: Level 17: Corona of Light (Light Domain)
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you cause yourself to emit an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it (no action required). You emit Bright Light in a 60-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet. Your enemies in the Bright Light have Disadvantage on saving throws against your Radiance of the Dawn and any spell that deals Fire or Radiant damage.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 75

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Trickery Domain
feature.text:
Make Mischief and Challenge Authority

The Trickery Domain offers magic of deception, illusion, and stealth. Clerics who wield this magic are a disruptive force in the world, puncturing pride, mocking tyrants, freeing captives, and flouting hollow traditions. They prefer subterfuge and pranks to direct confrontation.
	Gods of trickery are mischief-makers and instigators who stand as a constant challenge to the accepted order among both gods and mortals. They embody the forces of change and social upheaval, and they're patrons of thieves, scoundrels, gamblers, rebels, and liberators. Religious orders that operate in secret, especially those that seek to undermine oppressive governments or hierarchies, also draw on the power of the Trickery Domain.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 75

feature.name: Level 3: Trickery Domain Spells (Trickery Domain)
feature.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Trickery Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Trickery Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Prepared Spells
3 | Charm Person, Disguise Self, Invisibility, Pass without Trace
5 | Hypnotic Pattern, Nondetection
7 | Confusion, Dimension Door
9 | Dominate Person, Modify Memory

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 76

feature.name: Level 3: Blessing of the Trickster (Trickery Domain)
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you can choose yourself or a willing creature within 30 feet of yourself to have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. This blessing lasts until you finish a Long Rest or you use this feature again.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 75

feature.name: Level 3: Invoke Duplicity (Trickery Domain)
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to create a perfect visual illusion of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The illusion is intangible and doesn't occupy its space. It lasts for 1 minute, but it ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or have the Incapacitated condition. The illusion is animated and mimics your expressions and gestures. While it persists, you gain the following benefits.

	Cast Spells. You can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, but you must use your own senses.

	Distract. When both you and your illusion are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have Advantage on attack rolls against that creature, given how distracting the illusion is to the target.

	Move. As a Bonus Action, you can move the illusion up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is within 120 feet of yourself.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 75

feature.name: Level 6: Trickster's Transposition (Trickery Domain)
feature.text:
Whenever you take the Bonus Action to create or move the illusion of your Invoke Duplicity, you can teleport, swapping places with the illusion.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 76

feature.name: Level 17: Improved Duplicity (Trickery Domain)
feature.text:
The illusion of your Invoke Duplicity has grown more powerful in the following ways.

	Shared Distraction. When you and your allies make attack rolls against a creature within 5 feet of the illusion, the attack rolls have Advantage.

	Healing Illusion. When the illusion ends, you or a creature of your choice within 5 feet of it regains a number of Hit Points equal to your Cleric level.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 76

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: War Domain
feature.text:
Inspire Valor and Smite Foes

	War has many manifestations. It can make heroes of ordinary people. It can be desperate and horrific, with acts of cruelty and cowardice eclipsing instances of excellence and courage. Clerics who tap into the magic of the War Domain excel in battle, inspiring others to fight the good fight or offering acts of violence as prayers.
	Gods of the War Domain watch over warriors and reward them for their great deeds. They include champions of honor and chivalry as well as gods of destruction and pillage. Other war gods take a more neutral stance, promoting war in all its manifestations and supporting warriors in any circumstance.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 76

feature.name: Level 3: War Domain Spells (War Domain)
feature.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the War Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

War Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Prepared Spells
3 | Guiding Bolt, Magic Weapon, Shield of Faith, Spiritual Weapon
5 | Crusader's Mantle, Spirit Guardians
7 | Fire Shield, Freedom of Movement
9 | Hold Monster, Steel Wind Strike

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 77

feature.name: Level 3: Guided Strike (War Domain)
feature.text:
When you or a creature within 30 feet of you misses with an attack roll, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and give that roll a +10 bonus, potentially causing it to hit. When you use this feature to benefit another creature's attack roll, you must take a Reaction to do so.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 77

feature.name: Level 3: War Priest (War Domain)
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can make one attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 77

feature.name: Level 6: War God's Blessing (War Domain)
feature.text:
You can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to cast Shield of Faith or Spiritual Weapon rather than expending a spell slot. When you cast either spell in this way, the spell doesn't require Concentration. Instead the spell lasts for 1 minute, but it ends early if you cast that spell again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 77

feature.name: Level 17: Avatar of Battle (War Domain)
feature.text:
You gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 77

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Knowledge Domain
feature.text:
Unearth Secrets and Master the Mind

The Knowledge Domain values learning and understanding above all. Clerics who tap into this domain study esoteric lore, collect old tomes, delve into secret places, and examine the processes of the mind. To them, knowledge is more valuable than material wealth, and learning is an act of worship. Libraries, universities, and other educational institutions also draw on the power of the Knowledge Domain.
	Gods of knowledge vary from masters of arcane magic to patrons of craft and invention. In Faerûn, Clerics of the Knowledge Domain worship deities of learning and ingenuity such as Oghma and Gond, among many others.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 18

feature.name: Level 3: Blessings of Knowledge (Knowledge Domain)
feature.text:
You gain proficiency with one type of Artisan's Tools of your choice and in two of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. You have Expertise in those two skills.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 18

feature.name: Level 3: Knowledge Domain Spells (Knowledge Domain)
feature.text:
When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Knowledge Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Knowledge Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Spells
3 | Command, Comprehend Languages*, Detect Magic*, Detect Thoughts*, Identify*, Mind Spike*
5 | Dispel Magic, Nondetection, Tongues*
7 | Arcane Eye*, Banishment, Confusion
9 | Legend Lore*, Scrying*, Synaptic Static

*Spell of the Divination school

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 18

feature.name: Level 3: Mind Magic (Knowledge Domain)
feature.text:
As a Magic action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to manifest your magical knowledge. Choose one spell from the Divination school on the Knowledge Domain Spells table that you have prepared. As part of that action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 18

feature.name: Level 6: Unfettered Mind (Knowledge Domain)
feature.text:
You gain telepathy out to 60 feet. When you use this telepathy, you can simultaneously contact a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one).
	Additionally, you gain proficiency in Intelligence saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain saving throw proficiency with one ability in which you lack it.

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 18

feature.name: Level 17: Divine Foreknowledge (Knowledge Domain)
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you magically expand your mind to the future. For 1 hour, you have Advantage on D20 Tests. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of this feature by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

Source:	Forgotten Realms: Heroes of Faerûn [5.5e] p. 19

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Grave Domain
feature.text:
Embody Deific Forces of Death

The Grave Domain concerns itself with the boundary between life and death. To those who tap into this domain's power, death is a natural and inevitable part of the multiverse. Such Clerics seek to destroy undead and shepherd spirits.
	The magic of this domain also allows these Clerics to stave off death for a time. But this is merely a delay of death, not a denial of it, for the grave will always claim its due.

Source:	Ravenloft: The Horrors Within

feature.name: Level 3: Grave Domain Spells (Grave Domain)
feature.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Grave Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Grave Domain Spells:
Cleric Level | Spells
3 | Detect Evil and Good, False Life, Gentle Repose, Ray of Enfeeblement, Spare the Dying
5 | Revivify, Vampiric Touch
7 | Blight, Death Ward
9 | Dispel Evil and Good, Raise Dead

Source:	Ravenloft: The Horrors Within

feature.name: Level 3: Circle of Mortality (Grave Domain)
feature.text:
You can manipulate the balance between life and death, granting you the following benefits.

	Pull of Death. Once per turn, when you deal damage to a creature that's missing any Hit Points by casting a spell or by hitting with an attack roll, that creature takes an extra 1d4 Necrotic damage. This extra damage increases to 1d6 when you reach Cleric level 11.

	Return to Life. You can cast Spare the Dying as a Bonus Action.
	Additionally, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore Hit Points to a creature at 0 Hit Points with a spell or Channel Divinity, don't roll those dice for the healing; instead, use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d4 Hit Points to a creature at 0 Hit Points with a spell, you restore 8.

Source:	Ravenloft: The Horrors Within

feature.name: Level 3: Path to the Grave (Grave Domain)
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of Channel Divinity to curse one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself until the start of your next turn. While cursed, the creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws.
	When you or an ally you can see hits the cursed target with an attack roll, you can end the curse early (no action required) to make the attack deal extra Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to your Cleric level.

Source:	Ravenloft: The Horrors Within

feature.name: Level 6: Sentinel at Death's Door (Grave Domain)
feature.text:
When you or a Bloodied creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself is hit with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve that attack's damage (round down). If the triggering attack roll was a Critical Hit, any effects triggered by a Critical Hit are canceled.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Ravenloft: The Horrors Within

feature.name: Level 17: Divine Reaper (Grave Domain)
feature.text:
Your deep connection to this domain renders you a hallowed harbinger of death, granting you the following benefits.

	Enhanced Necromancy. When you cast a spell of level 5 or lower from the Necromancy school that targets one creature, or when you cast a spell from the Grave Domain Spells table, you can expend a use of Channel Divinity to target a second creature within the spell's range. If the spell requires costly or consumed Material components, you must provide Material components for each target.

	Keeper of Souls. When an enemy dies within 60 feet of you, you or one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself regains Hit Points equal to twice your Cleric level. You can't use this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest, unless you expend a level 6+ spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

Source:	Ravenloft: The Horrors Within

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Knowledge Domain (UA)
feature.text:
Unearth Secrets and Master the Mind

The Knowledge Domain values learning and understanding above all. Clerics who tap into this domain study esoteric lore, collect old tomes, delve into the secret places of the earth, and examine the process of the mind itself.

Gods of knowledge vary from masters of arcane magic to patrons of craft and invention. To them, knowledge is more valuable than material wealth, and the desire to learn is an act of worship. Libraries, universities, and other institutions dedicated to education also draw on the power of the Knowledge Domain.

On Faerûn, Clerics of the Knowledge Domain worship deities of learning and ingenuity like Oghma and Gond. Other powerful deities—such as Asmodeus, Mystra, Savras, and Jergal—also count Clerics of the Knowledge Domain among their devotees, as do less-common divinities like Deneir, the Scribe of Oghma, and Azuth, servant of Mystra.

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 2

feature.text:
You gain proficiency with one type of Artisan's Tools of your choice and in two of the following skills of your choice: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. You have Expertise in those two skills.

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 2

feature.text:

feature.text:

feature.text:

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of this feature by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

Source:	Unearthed Arcana: Forgotten Realms Subclasses p. 3

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Grave Domain (UA)
feature.text:
Embody Deific Forces of Death

The Grave Domain concerns itself with the boundary between life and death. To those who tap into this domain's power, death is a foundational, natural, and inevitable part of the multiverse. Such Clerics seek to destroy Undead and strive to shepherd spirits to the afterlife (whether those spirits want to go or not).
	The magic of this domain also allows these Clerics to stave off death for a time, particularly for those who still have some great work to accomplish in the world. But this is merely a delay of death, not a denial of it, for the grave will always claim its due.

Design Note: Grave Domain Updates
Here are the main updates in this subclass since its appearance in Xanathar's Guide to Everything:

	• Circle of Mortality now also grants you a small damage boost against Bloodied creatures.

	• Grave Domain Spells has been updated to include more versatility and combat-relevant spells.

	• Path to the Grave now produces an ongoing curse effect in addition to boosting the damage of an attack.

	• Sentinel at Death's Door now can trigger on any attack, not just Critical Hits.

	• Divine Reaper is a new feature that absorbs the previous benefits of Keeper of Souls and provides a boost to the Cleric's Necromancy spells.

Source:	UA2024-Horror Subclasses p. 4

feature.name: Level 3: Circle of Mortality (Grave Domain (UA))
feature.text:

Your game statistics remain the same, apart from the following changes:

	Condition Immunities. You have Immunity to the Grappled, Paralyzed, Prone, and Restrained conditions.

A creature also takes this damage when it enters your space or ends its turn there. A creature takes this damage only once per turn.

You revert to your true form after 10 minutes, if you choose to end the transformation (no action required), if you have the Incapacitated condition, or if you die.

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Black Death Domain (HB)
feature.text:
Spread and retain disease at your will

"To cure or to cull, to heal or to harm—faith and pestilence are two hands of the same god."

Theme: Masters of life and death, these clerics wield plague magic to heal and harm in equal measure.

Playstyle: Poison-based abilities, battlefield control, and resilience.

The Black Death was a devastating global epidemic of bubonic plague that struck Europe and Asia in the mid1300s. The plague arrived in Europe in October 1347, when 12 ships from the Black Sea docked at the Sicilian port of Messina. People gathered on the docks were met with a horrifying surprise: Most sailors aboard the ships were dead, and those still alive were gravely ill and covered in black boils that oozed blood and pus. Sicilian authorities hastily ordered the fleet of "death ships" out of the harbor, but it was too late: Over the next five years, the Black Death would kill more than 20 million people in Europe—almost one-third of the continent's population.

"Stone endures longer than empires—let faith rise as high as the spires above."

Playstyle: Radiant damage, auras, and support.

The building of monumental cathedrals in the middle ages was a reflection of faith and the channel for much of the creative energy of medieval European society. Although cathedral building was driven by religious figures or institutions, it was often a community effort. The Cathedral was a place of Catholic worship and the seat of the Bishop of the diocese, but it was also a symbol of Paradise. In Medieval times, it was the centerpiece of the community, representing hope and refuge. Refuge from the struggles and difficulties of human life; hope of the promise of Heaven while in the presence of God. Its very structure should make men yearn for Heaven. Cathedrals were built to evoke that feeling through their structure and art, both rich in symbolism.

"Where the fire burns, so too does hope. My faith is not in walls or gods—it is in the warmth that binds us together."

Hearth was a common topic and icon in many ancient European religions. The hearth also served as a communal and ritualistic space, where stories were told, and bonds strengthened. This reverence for the hearth can be seen in burial practices and household rituals, with fire representing life and death cycles. Even in folklore, the hearth was immensely symbolic.

"The truth is not written in stone, but in the whispers of the doubters, the fire of the condemned, and the revelations of those who dare to question."

Theme: Inspired by the real-world heresies of medieval Europe (such as the Cathars, Hussites, and Lollards), this domain represents faith as rebellion.

The gods may grant power, but the Heretic dares to question their authority.

Playstyle: Blend divine magic with cunning defiance, gaining powers that fuel rebellion, protect outcasts, and challenge the authority of the gods themselves.

Heresy was an opinion about the teaching of the Catholic church, which was condemned by the church as inconsistent with it. First heretics groups started in XI century and lasted until XVI century. Heretics were religious groups whose beliefs did not wholly conform with the medieval Church's doctrines. While the groups themselves ranged in beliefs, their commonality was their rejection of and persecution by the Church. Many of the groups still thought of themselves as Christians despite the Church's rejection. Some felt that the Church had changed too much and that it, in fact, was heretical. In this way, heretics were both within and outside the Church. It is often hard to determine whose beliefs were truly heretical.

Playstyle: Specialized in investigation, coercion, and relentless pursuit of those who defy their faith. They control battlefields through fear and suppression, limiting enemy options while bolstering allies with unwavering certainty.

The Inquisition was a powerful office set up within the Catholic Church to root out and punish heresy throughout Europe and the Americas. Beginning in the 12th century and continuing for hundreds of years, the Inquisition is infamous for the severity of its tortures and its persecution of Jews and Muslims. Its worst manifestation was in Spain, where the Spanish Inquisition was a dominant force for more than 200 years, resulting in some 32,000 executions.

feature.name: Cleric Subclass: Mysteries Domain (HB)
feature.text:
Keeper of hidden truths and powerful divine magic

"The divine is not to be known, but to be sought. Every question is a prayer, every answer another veil to be lifted."

Theme: Keepers of divine secrets, clerics of Mysteries serves the hidden gods, the cryptic prophecies, and the sacred rites known only to the initiated. They speak in riddles, guard lost truths, and wield magic that veils, reveals, or warps reality itself. They uncover hidden truths and wield arcane power through their divine insight.

Playstyle: Supportive, through divination, arcane magic, and knowledge.

The Eleusinian Mysteries (Greek: Ἐλευσίνια Μυστήρια, romanized: Eleusínia Mystḗria) were initiations held every year for the cult of Demeter and Persephone based at the Panhellenic Sanctuary of Eleusis in ancient Greece. They are considered the "most famous of the secret religious rites of ancient Greece". Their basis was a Bronze Age agrarian cult, and there is some evidence that they were derived from the religious practices of the Mycenean period. The Mysteries represented the myth of the abduction of Persephone from her mother Demeter by the king of the underworld Hades. The rites, ceremonies, and beliefs were kept secret and consistently preserved from antiquity.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 21 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Oracle's Insight (Mysteries Domain (HB))
feature.text:
You start to understand the true secrets of the world. You gain the following benefits:

	• You are Proficient in Arcana. If you are already proficient, you gain Expertise.

	• You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects of the illusion and enchantment schools.

	• You learn the Minor Illusion cantrip. This cantrip is on top the number of cantrips you can normally learn, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability to cast it.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 21 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Revelation (Mysteries Domain (HB))
feature.text:
As a Magic Action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to reveal hidden truths within a 30-foot radius. Invisible creatures and objects are revealed for 1 minute, and each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you gains Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects of illusion and enchantment schools.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 21 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Mysteries Domain Spells (Mysteries Domain (HB))
feature.text:

feature.name: Level 6: Veil of Mystery (Mysteries Domain (HB))
feature.text:
As a Reaction, when an enemy targets you with an attack, you can impose Disadvantage on the roll and teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 21 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 17: Oracle's Sight (Mysteries Domain (HB))
feature.text:
You gain Truesight 120 feet. Additionally, you are Immune to Blinded condition and can't be surprised.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Druid [5.5e]
fields.proficiency: Intelligence, Wisdom, Arcana, Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion, Survival

trait.name: Druid
trait.text:
Druids belong to ancient orders that call on the forces of nature. Harnessing the magic of animals, plants, and the four elements, Druids heal, transform into animals, and wield elemental destruction.
	Revering nature above all, individual Druids gain their magic from nature, a nature deity, or both, and they typically unite with other Druids to perform rites that mark the passage of the seasons and other natural cycles.
	Druids are concerned with the delicate ecological balance that sustains plant and animal life and with the need for people to live in harmony with nature. Druids often guard sacred sites or watch over regions of unspoiled nature, but when a significant danger arises, Druids take a more active role as adventurers who combat the threat.

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 79

feature.name: Becoming A Druid As A Level 1 Character
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Druid, you begin play with 8 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

Core Druid Traits:
	• Primary Ability: Wisdom
	• Hit Point Die: D8 per Druid level
	• Saving Throw Proficiencies: Intelligence and Wisdom
	• Skill Proficiencies: Choose 2: Arcana, Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion, or Survival
	• Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons
	• Tool Proficiencies: Herbalism Kit
	• Armor Training: Light armor and Shields

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background (choose A or B):
	• (A) Leather Armor, Shield, Sickle, Druidic Focus (Quarterstaff), Explorer's Pack, Herbalism Kit, and 9 GP
	• (B) 50 GP

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 79

feature.name: Becoming A Druid As A Multiclass Character
feature.text:
Core Druid Traits:
	• Primary Ability: Wisdom
	• Hit Point Die: D8 per Druid level
	• Armor Training: Light armor and Shields

Source:	Player's Handbook (2024) p. 79

feature.name: Level 1: Spellcasting
feature.text:
You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Druid spells, which appear on the Druid spell list later in the class's description.

	Cantrips. You know two cantrips of your choice from the Druid spell list. Druidcraft and Produce Flame are recommended.
	Whenever you gain a Druid level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list.
	When you reach Druid levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Druid Features table.

	Spell Slots. The Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1• spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

	Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Druid spell list. Animal Friendship, Cure Wounds, Faerie Fire, and Thunderwave are recommended.
	The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Druid levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Druid Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Druid spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Druid, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
	If another Druid feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Druid spells for you.

	Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells with other Druid spells for which you have spell slots.

	Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Druid spells.

	Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Druid spells.
