feature.text:
Command the Powers of Death and Undeath

You explore the cosmic forces of life, death, and undeath. As a Necromancer, you learn to manipulate the energy that animates all creatures. As you progress, you learn to use magic to drain the life force from a creature and transform its vital energy into magical power. Many see Necromancers as menacing or villainous, though not all Necromancers are evil. Nevertheless, the manipulation of life and death is considered taboo in many societies.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 7

feature.name: Level 3: Necromancy Savant (Necromancer v2 (UA))
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Necromancy school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Necromancy school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 7

feature.name: Level 3: Necromancy Spellbook (Necromancer v2 (UA))
feature.text:
The necromantic secrets in your spellbook grant you additional powers. You gain the following benefits.

	Necrotic Resistance. You have Resistance to Necrotic damage.

	Grim Harvest. When you cast a Necromancy spell using a spell slot, you can choose an Undead creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to regain a number of Hit Points equal to the level of the spell slot expended plus your Wizard level.

	Undead Familiar. The Find Familiar spell appears in your spellbook. When you cast the spell, you choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: Skeleton or Zombie (see appendix B of the Player's Handbook for the familiar's stat block).

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 6: Grave Power (Necromancer v2 (UA))
feature.text:
You have discovered more necromantic insights and inscribed them in your spellbook. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

	Grave Resilience. When you use Arcane Recovery, your Exhaustion level, if any, decreases by 1.

	Overwhelming Necrosis. Damage from your Wizard spells and Wizard features ignores Resistance to Necrotic damage.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 6: Undead Thralls (Necromancer v2 (UA))
feature.text:
You always have Animate Dead prepared and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that the spell's effective level is increased by 1.
	In addition, whenever you cast a Necromancy spell using a spell slot that creates or summons an Undead, the Undead gains the benefits below.

	Undead Fortitude. The Undead's Hit Point maximum and current Hit points increase by a number equal to the level of the spell slot used plus your Intelligence modifier for the duration of the spell.

	Withering Strike. Whenever the Undead hits a creature with an attack roll, the Undead deals extra Necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 Necrotic damage).

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 10: Harvest Undead (Necromancer v2 (UA))
feature.text:
You have learned more secrets about the nuances of life and death. Immediately after you become Bloodied but aren't killed outright from taking damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce an Undead creature under your control that you can see to 0 Hit Points. You then immediately regain a number of Hit Points equal to your Wizard level.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 14: Death's Master (Necromancer v2 (UA))
feature.text:
Abstruse rituals within your spellbook allow you mastery over forces of death. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

	Bolster Undead. As a Bonus Action, choose any number of Undead you have created or summoned with a Necromancy spell that are within 60 feet of you. Those Undead each gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wizard level. Once an Undead gains Temporary Hit Points from this feature, it can't gain them in this way again for the next 24 hours.

	Extinguish Undead. When an Undead creature you can see is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can cause it to explode with necrotic energy. Roll a number of d6s equal to half the creature's unexpended Hit Dice (round up, minimum of 1d6) and add them together. Each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the Undead makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled and can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only. When you use this feature to explode an Undead creature you don't control, you must take a Reaction and expend a level 5+ spell slot to do SO.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Transmuter v2 (UA)
feature.text:
Transform Energy and Matter

You study spells that modify energy and matter. To you, the world is not a fixed thing, but eminently mutable. Your magic gives you the tools to become a smith at reality's forge.
	Some Transmuters are tinkerers and pranksters. Others pursue their magical studies with deadly seriousness, seeking the power make and destroy worlds.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 3: Transmutation Savant (Transmuter v2 (UA))
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Transmutation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Transmutation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 3: Transmuter's Stone (Transmuter v2 (UA))
feature.text:
When you finish a Long Rest, you can create a magic stone that lasts until you use this feature again. The stone is a Tiny object, and you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.
	A creature with the stone in its possession gains proficiency in Constitution saving throws and one of the following benefits, which you choose when you create the stone. You can change the stone's benefit when you cast a Transmutation spell using a spell slot.

	Darkvision. The bearer gains Darkvision with a range of 60 feet or increases the range of its Darkvision by 60 feet.

	Speed. The bearer's Speed increases by 10 feet.

	Resistance. The bearer gains Resistance to Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage (your choice each time you choose this benefit).

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 3: Wondrous Alteration (Transmuter v2 (UA))
feature.text:
You always have the Alter Self spell prepared and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest.
	While under the effects of Alter Self, you gain an additional benefit for each of its options.

	Aquatic Adaptation. While underwater, you can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action.

	Change Appearance. You have Advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks.

	Natural Weapons. The damage of your new growth increases to 2d6 damage of the type associated with the growth. You also have Advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 6: Empowered Transmutation (Transmuter v2 (UA))
feature.text:
When you cast a Transmutation spell that doesn't deal damage, such as Fly or Magical Weapon, using a spell slot, you can treat the spell as if it were cast using a spell slot 1 level above the slot expended.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 10: Potent Stone (Transmuter v2 (UA))
feature.text:
Your Transmuter's Stone is more versatile. When you create your Transmuter's Stone, you can choose up to two benefits. You can choose each option other than Resistance only once. If you choose Resistance twice, you must choose different damage types. You can change either or both benefits when you cast a Transmutation spell using a spell slot.
	In addition, the following are now among your benefit options for Transmuter's Stone.

	Mighty Build. The bearer has Advantage on Strength saving throws. The bearer also counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity.

	Tremorsense. The bearer gains Tremorsense with a range of 30 feet.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 10: Shapechanger (Transmuter v2 (UA))
feature.text:
You always have the Polymorph spell prepared and can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest.
	In addition, when you target yourself with the spell, you can modify the spell to gain the benefits below. Once you modify the spell using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

	Game Statistics. You retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak. You also retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores;
class features; languages; and feats.

	Transmute Spells. You can cast Transmutation spells while shape-shifted, except for any spell with a Material component that has a cost specified or is consumed by the spell.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 11

feature.name: Level 14: Master Transmuter (Transmuter v2 (UA))
feature.text:
While you carry your Transmuter's Stone, you can take a Magic action to consume the reserve of transmutation magic stored inside and choose one of the following benefits. After you use your Transmuter's Stone in this way, the stone crumbles to dust. You can prevent the stone from crumbling by expending a level 5+ spell slot as part of the Magic action you take using this feature.

	Major Transformation. You can transmute one nonmagical object—no larger than a 10-foot Cube or eight connected 5-foot Cubes-into another nonmagical object of similar size and mass and of equal or lesser value. You must spend 10 minutes handling the object to transform it.

	Panacea. You touch a creature as part of this Magic action, and the target regains a number of Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum (round down). The target is cured of all magical contagions, and any curses affecting the target are lifted, including the target's Attunement to a cursed item. If the target has the Poisoned or Petrified conditions, those conditions end.

	Restore Life. You cast the Raise Dead spell without expending a spell slot, using the stone in place of the required Material components.

	Restore Youth. You touch one willing creature as part of this Magic action, and the target's Exhaustion level, if any, decreases to 0 and it permanently appears 3d10 years younger, to a minimum of young adulthood.

Source:	UA25-ArcaneSubclassesUpdate p. 10

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: School of Circean Enchantment (HB)
feature.text:
Enthrall the others with charming magic

"And I will tell you of all the wicked witchcraft that Circe will try to practice upon you. She will mix a mess for you to drink, and she will drug the meal with which she makes it"
— Homer, Odyssey X

Theme: Inspired by the sorceress Circe from The Odyssey, this subclass focuses on enchanting, transforming, and manipulating others, blending charm and transmutation magic.

Playstyle: Circean Enchanters are masters of control, turning enemies into allies and reshaping their forms.

Circe is known for her role in Homer's Odyssey when Odysseus visits her island of Aeaea on the way back from the Trojan War. Circe had a vast knowledge of potions and herbs. Through the use of these and a magic wand or staff, she transformed her enemies, or those who offended her, into animals.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Enchanting Voice (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
You learn the Charm Person spell and you can cast it without expending a spell slot once per Long Rest. When you cast the Charm Person spell, you can target an additional creature.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Will of the Sorceress (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
When you cast a spell of the enchantment school that targets a creature, you can force that creature to have Disadvantage on the saving throw.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Transmutation's Touch (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
You learn the Polymorph spell, but it doesn't count against your spells prepared.
	You can cast it once without expending a spell slot once per Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Beguile and Transform (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
Your spells ignore Immunity to the Charmed condition. Your spells can also change the shape of creatures whose form is usually immutable, such as Constructs.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Circe's Dominion (School of Circean Enchantment (HB))
feature.text:
As a Magic Action, you target a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature is transformed into a harmless beast (CR 0) for to 1 minute. The creature retains its alignment and personality but is unable to act against you.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 67 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: School of Illuminism (HB)
feature.text:
Bring the light of knowledge in the darkness

"Education is bitter, but its fruit is sweet"

Theme: Inspired by the Enlightenment, this subclass reflects a pursuit of knowledge, logic, and understanding of the natural world, using magic to illuminate both metaphorically and literally.

Playstyle: Illuminists excel at uncovering secrets, countering lies, and shedding light on mysteries. They have abilities that disrupt illusions, reveal hidden truths, and empower their allies with clarity.

The Enlightenment was an intellectual and philosophical movement taking place in Europe from the late 17th century to the early 19th century. The central doctrines of the Enlightenment were individual liberty, representative government, the rule of law, and religious freedom, in contrast to an absolute monarchy or single party state and the religious persecution of faiths other than those formally established and often controlled outright by the State.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Light of Truth (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
You learn the Detect Magic and Identify spells, which don't count against your spells prepared. You can cast each of these once without expending a spell slot, regaining the feature when you finish a Short or Long rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Dispel the Shadows (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
When you cast a spell that creates light (such as Light or Daylight), the radius of the light is doubled.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Unveiling Insight (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
You gain Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Insight) checks. Additionally, as a Magic Action, you can focus your mind to gain Truesight up to 30 feet for 1 minute.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Illuminated Mind (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
Your mind resists magical manipulation. You are Immune to the Charmed condition.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Brilliant Revelation (School of Illuminism (HB))
feature.text:
As a Magic Action, you emit a burst of magical light in a 30-foot radius. Creatures of your choice within the radius must make a Constitution saving throw against a spell save DC. Failure: Blinded condition for 1 minute. While Blinded, can't have the Invisible condition. An affected creature can make another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its next turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 68 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: School of the Alchemist (HB)
feature.text:
Master of Transformation and Elixirs

"Every element holds a secret, every reaction a revelation. To seek the philosopher's stone is to seek the divine"

Theme: Rooted in medieval alchemical traditions, this subclass focuses on transmutation, creation, and the pursuit of perfection.

Playstyle: Alchemists are versatile, able to create potions, transmute materials, and alter the battlefield.

The School of Alchemy is a discipline of arcane science, blending mystical knowledge with chemistry, metallurgy, and the natural philosophy of medieval and Renaissance Europe. These wizards embody the historical alchemists who sought the Philosopher's Stone, dabbled in transmutation, and believed that magic and science were two sides of the same coin. Rooted in the traditions of figures like Paracelsus, Albertus Magnus, and Nicolas Flamel, this school explores the alchemical mysteries of matter, energy, and spiritual transformation.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Transmutation Magic (School of the Alchemist (HB))
feature.text:
You learn the Alter Self spell, which doesn't count against your spells prepared. You can cast it once without expending a spell slot, once per Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Alchemical Recipes (School of the Alchemist (HB))
feature.text:
During a Long Rest, you can create a potion. Choose from the following: healing, resistance (to one damage type), or speed (increases movement by 10 feet for 1 hour). The DM has the statistics for the potions.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Magnum Opus (School of the Alchemist (HB))
feature.text:
You advance in your studies of alchemical transmutation, allowing you to tap into deeper arcane formulas.
	You can create a special elixir that mimics the effects of a lesser restoration spell. The drinker can remove one disease, condition (Blinded, Deafened, Poisoned, Paralyzed), or regain lost ability score points. Once used, you cannot create this elixir again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Great Work of the Alchemist (School of the Alchemist (HB))
feature.text:
Your knowledge of mystical chemistry allows you to manipulate the very structure of magic and matter.
	When you cast a spell that deals Acid, Fire, Poison, or Necrotic damage, you can change its damage type to Force or Radiant, representing the purified essence of alchemy.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Elixir of Immortality (School of the Alchemist (HB))
feature.text:
You have uncovered the secrets of longevity and perfected the final stages of the Magnum Opus.
	During a Long Rest action, you can create a perfected alchemical elixir. When you drink it as a Bonus Action, it alters your form for 1 minute. Choose one of the following effects:

	• Adamantine Flesh. You gain Resistance to all damage except Psychic.

	• Liquid Essence. You can move through small openings, difficult terrain does not slow you, and you gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

	• Purified Form. You are immune to Poison damage and the Frightened, Charmed and Poisoned conditions.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 66 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: School of the Renaissance (HB)
feature.text:
Mix magic with the power of art and invention

"Knowledge is not inherited, nor granted by gods—it is created. Let the old world tremble before new ideas"

Theme: Drawing from the creativity and ingenuity of the Italian Renaissance, this subclass combines art and invention, creating magical constructs and enhancing spells with artistic flair.

Playstyle: Renaissance Wizards are versatile, with abilities to summon magical objects, enhance their spell effects with artistry, and create magical blueprints.

Renaissance' means 're-birth' and during this time Europe left behind the fixed ideas of the Middle Ages and created the beginnings of the modern world as we know it. The civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome were rediscovered, inspiring an interest in Classical learning which challenged medieval beliefs and ideas.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 69 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Magical Craftsmanship (School of the Renaissance (HB))
feature.text:
You can cast the Unseen Servant spell without expending a spell slot, regaining the feature when you finish a Long Rest.
	You also learn the Mending and Prestidigitation cantrips, which don't count against your known cantrips.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 69 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Artistic Infusion (School of the Renaissance (HB))
feature.text:
When you cast a spell, you can flavor it with artistic elements, such as radiant paintings or bursts of music. When a creature succeeds a saving throw against a spell you cast, you can impose Disadvantage on its next Test before the end of your next turn.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 69 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Inspired Creation (School of the Renaissance (HB))
feature.text:
During a Long Rest, you can create a magical construct using your spellbook. Choose one of the following effects:

	• A tiny modron floating around a creature of your choice granting a +2 to its AC.

	• A hovering platform that can carry up to 500 pounds and moves 30 feet per round as a Bonus Action action.

These constructs last until you finish a Long Rest or dismiss them.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 69 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Artful Enhancement (School of the Renaissance (HB))
feature.text:
When you cast a spell, you can grant a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wizard level.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 69 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Masterpiece (School of the Renaissance (HB))
feature.text:
As a Magic Action, you create a magical masterpiece, such as an intricate sculpture or mural. Choose one of the following effects:

	Mural of Glory. All your Allies within 30 feet of you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wizard level + Intelligence modifier and have Advantage on a Test of their choice within 1 minute.

	Sculpture of Binding. A creature within 30 feet must make on a Dexterity saving throw Failure: Restrained condition for 1 minute. Success: Restrained condition until the end of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Old World's Might - Subclasses from Old Europe p. 69 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Death Mage (HB)
feature.text:
Treat Life as a Resource, and Death as an Opportunity

Some mages deem it unwise to dabble in Necromancy, but you know better. To you, the so-called "barrier" between life and death is merely a gentle hill, and nothing builds your appetite like a nice brisk walk...

Source:	Death Mage by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Necromancy Savant (Death Mage (HB))
feature.text:
Choose two spells from the Necromancy school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one spell from the Necromancy school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
	Necromancy spells do not need to be on the Wizard spell list for you to add them with this feature.

Source:	Death Mage by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Life Siphon (Death Mage (HB))
feature.text:
Once per turn, when you damage a creature with a Necromancy spell, you can choose one die result from the damage roll and gain that many Temporary Hit Points. If you choose a die that rolled its maximum value, and the spell is a leveled spell, you can receive any of that die's Temporary Hit Points as Hit Points.
	The number of damage dice you can apply this feature to increases to two, then three, then four at Wizard Levels 5, 11, and 17 respectively.

Source:	Death Mage by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Necrotic Conduit (Death Mage (HB))
feature.text:
Undead creatures controlled by your Necromancy spells gain a +2 bonus to their attack rolls and add your Intelligence modifier to their saving throws. In addition, when you use your Life Siphon feature, you can redirect any Hit Points and Temporary Hit Points received to any of these creatures (no action required).

Source:	Death Mage by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Blood Magic (Death Mage (HB))
feature.text:
You can bolster your ability to sustain spells by sacrificing some of your vitality when you cast them. Each time you cast a spell that requires Concentration, you may chose to lose 5 Hit Points for each level of the spell or spell slot (whichever is higher) and reduce your Hit Point maximum by the same amount for the spell's duration. If the spell is a cantrip, you lose 5 Hit Points only.
	Until the spell ends, you do not make Concentration saving throws, your Concentration on the spell does not end due to you having the Incapacitated condition, and you have Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws.

Source:	Death Mage by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Maestro of Undeath (Death Mage (HB))
feature.text:
When Undead creatures controlled by your Necromancy spells deal damage with a feature in their stat blocks, this counts as damage from your leveled Necromancy spells for the purposes of your Life Siphon feature.

Source:	Death Mage by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Convoker (HB)
feature.text:
Summon Aid and Scatter Enemies

As a Convoker you specialize in the Conjuration school of magic, summoning extraplanar spirits to your side and teleporting great distances in the blink of an eye. Convokers are as valued for their practical abilities as they are feared for their control of battlefields.

Source:	Convoker by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Conjuration Savant (Convoker (HB))
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Conjuration school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Conjuration school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
	Finally, while a spellbook of yours exists and contains at least one of your spells, you can summon it to your hand at any time as a Magic Action. If the spellbook is torn into multiple pieces, you summon the largest piece.

Source:	Convoker by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Consummate Convoker (Convoker (HB))
feature.text:
Focused study has improved your command of summoning and teleportation magic, granting you the following benefits:

	Convoker's Companion. You always have the Find Familiar spell prepared. When you cast Find Familiar you choose from the normal forms, the form of an Homunculus, or the form of any type of Mephit. When your familiar forces a creature to make a saving throw, you use your spell save DC. In addition, when your familiar is about to take damage, you can take a Reaction and expend a level 1+ Wizard spell slot to dismiss the familiar instead.

	Convoker's Jaunt. You always have the Misty Step spell prepared, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You regain your use of this feature when you finish a Short or Long Rest, or when you expend a level 2+ Wizard spell slot to recharge it (no action required).

Source:	Convoker by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Misty Fling (Convoker (HB))
feature.text:
When you cast Misty Step, you can change its range to Touch and target one creature other than yourself that is Large size or smaller. A willing target is teleported up to the spell's maximum distance to a space you can see.
	An unwilling target must succeed a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC to resist being teleported.

Source:	Convoker by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Extraplanar Bond (Convoker (HB))
feature.text:
When you summon a creature with a Conjuration spell that requires Concentration, taking damage can't break your Concentration on this spell, and you can apply the Find Familiar spell's 'Telepathic Connection' benefit to the summoned creature as if it were your familiar.

Source:	Convoker by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Dimensional Mastery (Convoker (HB))
feature.text:
Misty Fling now increases Misty Step's range to 30 feet, its maximum teleport distance to 60 feet, and enables the spell to teleport Huge or Gargantuan creatures other than yourself if cast with a spell slot of level 4+.

Source:	Convoker by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Compeller (HB)
feature.text:
Charm the Scales Off a Snake

As a Compeller you specialize in Enchantment magic, a school focused on spells that captivate and control.

"If a Compeller is distrusted," it is often said, "they must not be very good at it!" Then the Compeller smiles, and everyone laughs and lowers their weapons.

Source:	Compeller by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Enchantment Savant (Compeller (HB))
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Enchantment school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Enchantment school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
	Lastly, any non-Enchantment Wizard spell can be treated as an Enchantment spell for you if it imposes a Wisdom saving throw on a creature when cast.

Source:	Compeller by Niall Keegan by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Dazzle (Compeller (HB))
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you flick a tangled thread of Enchantment magic at one creature you can see within 60 feet, briefly muddling its instincts. The target subtracts 1d4 from the result of the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn; or it subtracts 1d6 if that saving throw is made to resist the effects of an Enchantment spell. A creature can only be affected by one use of Dazzle at a time.
	You can use this feature a number of times per day equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you complete a Long Rest.

Source:	Compeller by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Slip of the Mind (Compeller (HB))
feature.text:
When your Concentration on a spell ends, you can take a Reaction to force creatures Charmed by that spell to each make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature does not remember that you cast the spell; on a success, the spell ends normally for them.

Source:	Compeller by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Mental Barricade (Compeller (HB))
feature.text:
Whenever you make a Wisdom saving throw, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the result.

Source:	Compeller by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Compelling Weave (Compeller (HB))
feature.text:
When a creature makes an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw at the end of its turn to end an ongoing effect of one of your spells, it makes the roll with Disadvantage.

Source:	Compeller by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: All-Charmer (Compeller (HB))
feature.text:
Your spells ignore creatures' Immunity to the Charmed condition; instead, creatures with Immunity to the Charmed condition have Advantage on saving throws against being Charmed by your spells.

Source:	Compeller by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Wizard Subclass: Alterant (HB)
feature.text:
Be the Change You Want to See

As an Alterant, you embrace the powerful yet mercurial school of Transmutation magic. Alterants most excel at spells that strengthen and enhance, but in battle they never hesitate to turn their problems into solutions.

Source:	Alterant by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Transmutation Savant (Alterant (HB))
feature.text:
Choose two Wizard spells from the Transmutation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.
	In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Transmutation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
	Lastly, as a Magic Action you can transmute your spellbook into any simple object weighing 1 to 3 pounds. The spellbook remains transmuted until someone touches it and takes a Magic Action to change it back, or until the object takes any damage.

Source:	Alterant by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Spell Morpher (Alterant (HB))
feature.text:
When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot targeting only yourself and your allies, before the spell ends you can change it into a different Transmutation spell you have prepared without expending another spell slot.
The rules for doing so are as follows:

	Normal Casting. You cast the new spell as normal.

	Timing. The old spell ends the instant the new spell is cast. The new spell lasts its normal duration, or the remainder of the old spell's duration, whichever is less.

	Target Limit. The targets of the new spell must be chosen from among the targets of the old spell.

	Effect Limit. The new spell is not considered to be cast with a spell slot. It is cast at the same level the old spell was, treating a level 6+ spell slot as if it were level 5, and it cannot grant Temporary Hit Points.

Source:	Alterant by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Divided Mind (Alterant (HB))
feature.text:
You have transmuted your own brain to protect the parts most important for spellcasting. When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can choose to succeed the saving throw and take Psychic damage instead (no action required).
	The amount of Psychic damage you take equals the DC for the saving throw minus your saving throw result. This damage cannot be reduced in any way and does not provoke a Concentration saving throw of its own.

Source:	Alterant by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Quick Change (Alterant (HB))
feature.text:
You always have the Polymorph spell prepared, and you can cast it as a Bonus Action. You can cast Polymorph once without expending a spell slot, and you regain your ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Alterant by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Grasp of the Alterant (Alterant (HB))
feature.text:
By reusing wasted energy from your spells you can sculpt matter to bind and hinder your foes.
	When one or more creatures you can see succeed a saving throw to be unaffected by one of your spells, you can take a Reaction to force those creatures to make Dexterity saving throws against your spell save DC. Each creature that fails gains one of the following conditions as transmuted matter binds it: Blinded, Deafened, or Restrained (you choose for each creature).
	This feature's effect on a creature ends when the transmuted matter changes back at the start of your next turn, or when an affected creature ends it early by taking an Action on its turn to free itself.
	Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a Long Rest, or until you expend a level 4+ spell slot to regain your use of it.

Source:	Alterant by Niall Keegan p. 2 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Artificer [5.5e]
fields.proficiency: Constitution, Intelligence, Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Sleight of Hand
fields.tools: Thieves' Tools, Tinker's Tools, one type of Artisan's Tools of your choice

trait.name: Artificer
trait.text:
Masters of invention, Artificers use ingenuity and magic to unlock extraordinary capabilities in objects. They see magic as a complex system waiting to be decoded and then harnessed in their spells and inventions.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer

feature.name: Becoming An Artificer As A Level 1 Character
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Artificer, you begin play with 8 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

Core Artificer Traits:
	• Primary Ability: Intelligence
	• Hit Point Die: D8 per Artificer level
	• Saving Throw Proficiencies: Constitution, Intelligence
	• Skill Proficiencies: Choose 2: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Sleight of Hand
	• Armor Training: Light Armor, Medium Armor, Shields
	• Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons
	• Tool Proficiencies: Thieves' Tools, Tinker's Tools, Artisan's Tools of your choice

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background (choose A or B):
	• (A) Studded Leather Armor, Dagger, Thieves' Tools, Tinker's Tools, Dungeoneer's Pack, and 16 GP
	• (B) 150 GP

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 7

feature.name: Becoming An Artificer As A Multiclass Character
feature.text:
Core Artificer Traits:
	• Hit Point Die: D8 per Artificer level
	• Skill Proficiencies: Choose 1: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Sleight of Hand
	• Armor Training: Light Armor, Medium Armor, Shields
	• Tool Proficiencies: Tinker's Tools

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 7

feature.name: Level 1: Spellcasting
feature.text:
You have learned how to channel magical energy through objects.

	Tools Required. You produce your Artificer spells through tools. You can use Thieves' Tools, Tinker's Tools, or another kind of Artisan's Tools with which you have proficiency as a Spellcasting Focus, and you must have one of those focuses in hand when you cast an Artificer spell (meaning the spell has an "M" component when you cast it).

	Cantrips. You know two Artificer cantrips of your choice. Acid Splash and Shocking Grasp are recommended.
	Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Artificer cantrip of your choice.
	When you reach Artificer levels 10 and 14, you learn another Artificer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Artificer Features table.

	Spell Slots. The Artificer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

	Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Artificer spells. Cure Wounds and Grease are recommended.
	The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Artificer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column below. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Artificer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Artificer, your list of prepared spells can include six Artificer spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
	If another Artificer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Artificer spells for you.

	Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Artificer spells for which you have spell slots.

	Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Artificer spells.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 7

feature.name: Level 1: Tinker's Magic
feature.text:
You know the Mending cantrip.
	As a Magic action while holding Tinker's Tools, you can create one item in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of yourself, choosing the item from the following list:

	• Ball Bearings
	• Basket
	• Bedroll
	• Bell
	• Blanket
	• Block and Tackle
	• Bottle, Glass
	• Bucket
	• Caltrops
	• Candle
	• Crowbar
	• Flask
	• Grappling Hook
	• Hunting Trap
	• Jug
	• Lamp
	• Manacles
	• Net
	• Oil
	• Paper
	• Parchment
	• Pole
	• Pouch
	• Rope
	• Sack
	• Shovel
	• Spikes, Iron
	• String
	• Tinderbox
	• Torch
	• Vial

The item lasts until you finish a Long Rest, at which point it vanishes.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 8

feature.name: Level 2: Replicate Magic Item
feature.text:
You have learned arcane plans that you use to make magic items.

	Plans Known. When you gain this feature, choose four plans to learn from the Magic Item Plans (Artificer Level 2+) table. Alchemy Jug, Cap of Water Breathing, Rope of Climbing, and Sending Stones are recommended. Whenever you gain an Artificer level, you can replace one of the plans you know with a new plan for which you qualify.
	You learn another plan of your choice when you reach certain Artificer levels (6th, 10th, 14th, 18th). When you choose a plan to learn, you choose it from any Magic Item Plans table for which you qualify; your qualification is based on your Artificer level.

	Creating an Item. When you finish a Long Rest, you can create one or two different magic items if you have Tinker's Tools in hand. Each item is based on one of the plans you know for this feature.
	If a created item requires Attunement, you can attune yourself to it the instant you create it. If you decide to attune to the item later, you must do so using the normal process for Attunement.
	When you reach certain Artificer levels (6th, 10th, 14th, 18th), the number of magic items you can create at the end of a Long Rest increases. Each item you create must be based on a different plan you know.
	You can't have more magic items from this feature than the number shown in the Magic Items column of the Artificer Features table for your level. If you try to exceed your maximum number of magic items for this feature, the oldest item vanishes, and then the new item appears.

	Duration. A magic item created by this feature functions exactly like the normal magic item, except its magic isn't permanent. When you die, the magic item vanishes after 1d4 days. If you replace a plan you know with a new plan, any magic item created with the replaced plan immediately vanishes.
	If an item that you created with this feature is a container, such as a Bag of Holding, and it vanishes, its contents harmlessly appear in and around its space.

	Spellcasting Focus. You can use any Wand or Weapon created by this feature as a Spellcasting Focus in lieu of using a set of Artisan's Tools.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 8

feature.name: Level 3: Artificer Subclass
feature.text:
You gain an Artificer subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Artificer levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Artificer level or lower.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Artificer levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 6: Magic Item Tinker
feature.text:
Your Replicate Magic Item feature gains the following options.

	Charge Magic Item. As a Bonus Action, you can touch a magic item within 5 feet of yourself that you created with Replicate Magic Item and that uses charges. You expend a level 1+ spell slot and recharge the item. The number of charges the item regains is equal to the level of spell slot expended.

	Drain Magic Item. As a Bonus Action, you can touch a magic item within 5 feet of yourself that you created with Replicate Magic Item and cause the item to vanish, converting its magical energy into a spell slot. The slot is level 1 if the item is Common or level 2 if the item is Uncommon or Rare. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.

	Transmute Magic Item. As a Magic action, you can touch one magic item within 5 feet of yourself that you created with Replicate Magic Item and transform it into a different magic item. The resulting item must be based on a magic item plan you know. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

	Expanded Replication. When you learn a plan for your Replicate Magic Item feature, you can now also choose from the Magic Item Plans (Artificer Level 6+) table.

feature.name: Level 7: Flash of Genius
feature.text:
When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails an ability check or a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to add a bonus to the roll, potentially causing it to succeed. The bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).
	You can take this Reaction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 8: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 10: Magic Item Adept
feature.text:
You've achieved a profound understanding of how to use and make magic items, granting you the following benefits.

	Additional Attunement. You can attune to up to four magic items at once rather than three.

	Expanded Replication. When you learn a plan for your Replicate Magic Item feature, you can now also choose from the Magic Item Plans (Artificer Level 10+) table.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 11: Spell-Storing Item
feature.text:
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can touch one Simple or Martial weapon or one item that you can use as a Spellcasting Focus, and you store a spell in it, choosing a level 1, 2, or 3 Artificer spell that has a casting time of an action and doesn't require a Material component with a gold cost that is consumed by the spell (you needn't have the spell prepared).
	While holding the object, a creature can take a Magic action to produce the spell's effect from it, using your spellcasting ability modifier. If the spell requires Concentration, the creature must concentrate. Once a creature has used the object to produce the spell's effect, the object can't be used this way again until the start of the creature's next turn.
	The spell stays in the object until it's been used a number of times equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of twice) or until you use this feature again to store a spell in an object.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 12: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 14: Advanced Artifice
feature.text:
Your skill with magic items deepens, granting you the following benefits.

	Magic Item Savant. You can attune to up to five magic items at once rather than three.

	Refreshed Genius. When you finish a Short Rest, you regain one expended use of your Flash of Genius feature.

	Expanded Replication. When you learn a plan for your Replicate Magic Item feature, you can now also choose from the Magic Item Plans (Artificer Level 14+) table.

Magic Item Plans (Artificer Level 14+):

Ring of the Ram | Yes
Rare Wondrous Item that isn't cursed* | Varies

* You can learn this option multiple times and must select a different item each time; each item selected counts as a different plan

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 16: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 18: Magic Item Master
feature.text:
You can now attune to up to six magic items at once rather than three.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 19: Epic Boon
feature.text:
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Energy Resistance is recommended.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 20: Soul of Artifice
feature.text:
You have developed a mystical connection to your magic items, which you can draw on for aid. You gain the following benefits.

	Cheat Death. If you're reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can disintegrate any number of Uncommon or Rare magic items created by your Replicate Magic Item feature. If you do so, your Hit Points instead change to a number equal to 20 times the number of magic items disintegrated.

	Magical Guidance. When you finish a Short Rest, you regain all expended uses of your Flash of Genius if you have Attunement to at least one magic item.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Artificer Subclass: Alchemist
feature.text:
Craft Magic Elixirs and Potions

An Alchemist is an expert at combining reagents to produce magical effects. Alchemists use their creations to give life and to leech it away.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 12

feature.name: Level 3: Tools of the Trade (Alchemist)
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

	Tool Proficiency. You gain proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies and the Herbalism Kit. If you already have one of these proficiencies, you gain proficiency with one other type of Artisan's Tools of your choice (or with two other types if you have both).

	Potion Crafting. When you brew a potion using the crafting rules, the amount of time required to craft it is halved.

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 12

feature.name: Level 3: Alchemist Spells (Alchemist)
feature.text:
When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Alchemist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Alchemist Spells:
Level | Spells

5 | Flaming Sphere, Melf's Acid Arrow
9 | Gaseous Form, Mass Healing Word
13 | Death Ward, Vitriolic Sphere
17 | Cloudkill, Raise Dead

Source:	Eberron: Forge of the Artificer p. 13

feature.name: Level 3: Experimental Elixir (Alchemist)
feature.text:
Whenever you finish a Long Rest while holding Alchemist's Supplies, you can use that tool to magically produce two elixirs. For each elixir, roll on the Elixir list below for the elixir's effect, which is triggered when someone drinks the elixir. The elixir appears in a vial, and the vial vanishes when the elixir is drunk or poured out. If any elixir remains when you finish a Long Rest, the elixir and its vial vanish.

	Drinking an Elixir. As a Bonus Action, a creature can drink the elixir or administer it to another creature within 5 feet of itself.

	Creating Additional Elixirs. As a Magic action while holding Alchemist's Supplies, you can expend one spell slot to create another elixir. When you do so, you choose its effect from the Elixir list below rather than rolling.
	When you reach certain Artificer levels, you can make an additional elixir at the end of each Long Rest: a total of three at level 5, four at level 9, and five at level 15.

Experimental Elixers:

2 | Swiftness. The drinker's Speed increases by 10 feet for 1 hour. This bonus increases when you reach Artificer levels 9 (15 feet) and 15 (20 feet).
3 | Resilience. The drinker gains a +1 bonus to AC for 10 minutes. The duration increases when you reach Artificer levels 9 (1 hour) and 15 (8 hours).
4 | Boldness. The drinker can roll 1d4 and add the number rolled to every attack roll and saving throw they make for the next minute. The duration increases when you reach Artificer levels 9 (10 minutes) and 15 (1 hour).
5 | Flight. The drinker gains a Fly Speed of 10 feet for 10 minutes. The Fly Speed increases when you reach Artificer levels 9 (20 feet) and 15 (30 feet).
