3 | Magic Missile, Thunderwave
5 | Mirror Image, Shatter
9 | Hypnotic Pattern, Lightning Bolt
13 | Fire Shield, Greater Invisibility
17 | Passwall, Wall of Force

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 8

feature.name: Level 3: Arcane Armor (Armorer)
feature.text:
As a Magic action while you have Smith's Tools in hand, you can turn a suit of armor you are wearing into Arcane Armor. The armor continues to be Arcane Armor until you don another suit of armor or you die.

You gain the following benefits while wearing your Arcane Armor:

No Strength Requirement:
If the armor normally has a Strength requirement, the Arcane Armor lacks this requirement for you.

Quick Don and Doff:
You can don or doff the armor as a Utilize action.

Second Skin:
The armor attaches to you and can't be removed against your will. It also expands to cover your entire body, although you can retract or deploy the helmet as a Bonus Action. The armor replaces missing limbs, functioning identically to a limb it replaces.

Spellcasting Focus:
You can use the Arcane Armor as a Spellcasting Focus for your Artificer spells.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 8

feature.name: Level 3: Armor Model (Armorer)
feature.text:
You can customize your Arcane Armor. When you do so, choose one of the following armor models: Dreadnaught, Guardian, or Infiltrator. The model you choose gives you special benefits while you wear it.

Each model includes a special weapon. When you attack with that weapon, you can add your Intelligence modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity modifier, to the attack and damage rolls.

You can change the armor's model whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest if you have Smith's Tools in hand.

Dreadnaught:
You design your armor to become a towering juggernaut in battle. It has the following features:

Armor Flail:
An iron ball on a chain appears on one of your armor's gauntlets and has the following traits:

Weapon Category: Simple Melee
Damage on a Hit: 1d10 Bludgeoning plus the ability modifier used for the attack roll Properties: Reach

Giant Stature:
As a Bonus Action, you transform and enlarge your armor for 1 minute. For the duration, your reach increases by 5 feet, and if you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing. If there isn't enough room for you to increase your size, your size doesn't change. You can use this Bonus Action a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Wrecking Ball:
If you hit a creature that is at least one size smaller than you with the flail, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself or pull the creature up to 10 feet toward yourself. Guardian. You design your armor to be in the front line of conflict. It has the following features:

Thunder Gauntlets:
Each of the armor's gauntlets has the following traits:

Weapon Category: Simple Melee
Damage on a Hit: 1d8 Thunder plus the ability modifier used for the attack roll

Distracting Pulse:
A creature hit by the gauntlet has Disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn.

Defensive Field:
While you are Bloodied, you can take a Bonus Action to gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Artificer level. You lose these Temporary Hit Points if you doff the armor.

Infiltrator:
You customize your armor for subtle undertakings. It has the following features:

Lightning Launcher:
A gemlike node appears on one of the armor's gauntlets or on the armor's chest (your choice). It has the following traits:

Weapon Category: Simple Ranged
Damage on a Hit: 1d6 Lightning plus the ability modifier used for the attack roll
Properties: Thrown (Range 90/300 feet)

Lightning Jolt:
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your Lightning Launcher, you can deal an extra 1d6 Lightning damage to that target.

Powered Steps:
Your Speed increases by 5 feet.

Dampening Field:
You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. If the armor normally imposes Disadvantage on such checks, the Advantage and Disadvantage cancel each other, as normal.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 8

feature.name: Level 5: Extra Attack (Armorer)
feature.text:
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 9

feature.name: Level 9: Armor Replication (Armorer)
feature.text:
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 9

feature.name: Level 15: Perfected Armor (Armorer)
feature.text:
Your Arcane Armor gains additional benefits based on its model, as detailed below.

Dreadnaught:
The damage die of your Armor Flail increases to 2d6 Bludgeoning damage.

In addition, when you use your Giant Stature, your reach increases by 10 feet, your size can increase to Large or Huge (your choice), and you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

Guardian:
The damage die of your Thunder Gauntlets increases to 1d10 Thunder damage.

In addition, when a Huge or smaller creature you can see ends its turn within 30 feet of you, you can take a Reaction to magically force that creature to make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you pull the creature up to 25 feet directly to an unoccupied space. If you pull the target to a space within 5 feet of yourself, you can make a melee weapon attack against it as part of this Reaction.

You can take this Reaction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Infiltrator:
The damage die of your Lightning Launcher increases to 2d6. Any creature that takes Lightning damage from your Lightning Launcher glimmers with magical light until the start of your next turn. The glimmering creature sheds Dim Light in a 5-foot radius, and it has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you, as the light jolts it if it attacks you.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 9

feature.name: Artificer Subclass: Artillerist
feature.text:
Wield Destructive Power from Afar

An Artillerist specializes in using magic to hurl energy, projectiles, and explosions on a battlefield.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 3: Tool Proficiency (Artillerist)
feature.text:
You gain proficiency with Woodcarver's Tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of Artisan's Tools of your choice.

In addition, when you craft a magic Wand, the amount of time required to craft it is halved.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 3: Artillerist Spells (Artillerist)
feature.text:
When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Artillerist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Artillerist Spells:
Artificer Level | Spells
3 | Shield, Thunderwave
5 | Scorching Ray, Shatter
9 | Fireball, Wind Wall
13 | Ice Storm, Wall of Fire
17 | Cone of Cold, Wall of Force

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 3: Eldritch Cannon (Artillerist)
feature.text:
Using Woodcarver's Tools or Smith's Tools, you can take a Magic action to create a Small or Tiny Eldritch Cannon in an unoccupied space on a horizontal surface within 5 feet of yourself. The cannon's game statistics appear below. You determine its appearance, which includes your choice of legs or wheels. It disappears if it is reduced to 0 Hit Points or after 1 hour. You can dismiss it early as a Magic action.

Once you create a cannon, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest or expend a spell slot to create one. You can have only one cannon at a time and can't create one while your cannon is present.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 5: Arcane Firearm (Artillerist)
feature.text:
When you finish a Long Rest, you can use Woodcarver's Tools to carve special sigils into a Rod, Staff, or Wand and thereby turn it into your arcane firearm. The sigils disappear from the object if you later carve them on a different item. The sigils otherwise last indefinitely.

You can use your arcane firearm as a Spellcasting Focus for your Artificer spells. When you cast an Artificer spell through the firearm, roll 1d8, and you gain a bonus to one of the spell's damage rolls equal to the number rolled.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 10

feature.name: Level 9: Explosive Cannon (Artillerist)
feature.text:
Every Eldritch Cannon you create is now more destructive. You gain the following benefits:

Detonate:
When your cannon is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to command the cannon to detonate if you are within 60 feet of it. Doing so destroys the cannon and forces each creature within 20 feet of it to make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 3d10 Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Firepower:
The cannon's damage rolls increase by 1d8.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 15: Fortified Position (Artillerist)
feature.text:
You're a master at forming well-defended emplacements using your Eldritch Cannon. You gain the following benefits:

Double Firepower:
You can now have two cannons at the same time. You can create two with the same Magic action (but not with the same spell slot), and you can activate both of them with the same Bonus Action, ordering them to use the same activation option or different ones. You can't create a third cannon while you have two.

Shimmering Field Projection:
You and your allies have Half Cover while within 10 feet of your Eldritch Cannon.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Artificer Subclass: Battle Smith
feature.text:
Command a Construct Guardian

A Battle Smith is a combination of protector and medic, an expert at defending others and repairing both materiel and personnel. To aid in their work, Battle Smiths are accompanied by a Steel Defender, a protective companion of their own creation.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 3: Tool Proficiency (Battle Smith)
feature.text:
You gain proficiency with Smith's Tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of Artisan's Tools of your choice.

In addition, when you craft an ordinary or magic weapon, the amount of time required to craft it is halved.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 3: Battle Smith Spells (Battle Smith)
feature.text:
When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Battle Smith Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Battle Smith Spells:
Artificer Level | Spells
3 | Heroism, Shield
5 | Shining Smite, Warding Bond
9 | Aura of Vitality, Conjure Barrage
13 | Aura of Purity, Fire Shield
17 | Banishing Smite, Mass Cure Wounds

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 3: Battle Ready (Battle Smith)
feature.text:
Your combat training and your experiments with magic have paid off in two ways:

Arcane Empowerment:
When you attack with a magic weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity modifier, for the attack and damage rolls.

Weapon Knowledge:
You gain proficiency with Martial weapons.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 3: Steel Defender (Battle Smith)
feature.text:
Your tinkering has borne you a companion, a Steel Defender (see the stat block). You determine the defender's appearance and whether it has two legs or four; your choices don't affect the defender's game statistics.

The Steel Defender is Friendly to you and your allies and obeys you. It vanishes if you die.

The Defender in Combat:
In combat, the defender acts during your turn. It can move and take its Reaction on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action to command it to take an action. If you have the Incapacitated condition, the defender acts on its own and isn't limited to the Dodge action.

Restoring or Replacing the Defender:
If the defender has died within the last hour, you can take a Magic action to touch it and expend a spell slot. The defender returns to life after 1 minute with all its Hit Points restored.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can create a new Steel Defender if you have Smith's Tools in hand. If you already have a defender from this feature, the first one vanishes.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 11

feature.name: Level 5: Extra Attack (Battle Smith)
feature.text:
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 12

feature.name: Level 9: Arcane Jolt (Battle Smith)
feature.text:
When either you hit a target with an attack roll using a magic weapon or your Steel Defender hits a target, you can channel magical energy through the strike to create one of the following effects:

Destructive Energy:
The target takes an extra 2d6 Force damage.

Restorative Energy:
Choose one creature or object you can see within 30 feet of the target. Healing energy flows into the chosen recipient, restoring 2d6 Hit Points to it.

You can use this energy a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), but you can do so no more than once a turn. You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 12

feature.name: Level 15: Improved Defender (Battle Smith)
feature.text:
Your Arcane Jolt and Steel Defender have become more powerful, granting these benefits:

Improved Jolt:
The extra damage and healing of your Arcane Jolt both increase to 4d6. Fortified Defender. Your Steel Defender gains a +2 bonus to Armor Class.

Improved Deflection:
Whenever your Steel Defender uses its Deflect Attack, the attacker takes Force damage equal to 1d4 plus your Intelligence modifier.

Source:	UA2024-Artificer p. 12

feature.name: Artificer Subclass: Cartographer
feature.text:
Chart Advantageous Courses through Turmoil

Cartographers are the premier navigators and reconnaissance agents. Using their creations, Cartographers can highlight threats, safeguard their allies, and carve portals to distant locations.

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 6

feature.name: Level 3: Tool Proficiencies (Cartographer)
feature.text:
You gain proficiency with Calligrapher's Supplies and Cartographer's Tools. If you already have one of these proficiencies, you gain proficiency with one other type of Artisan's Tools of your choice.
	In addition, when you scribe a Spell Scroll using the crafting rules in the Player's Handbook, the amount of time required to craft it is halved.

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 6

feature.name: Level 3: Cartographer Spells (Cartographer)
feature.text:
When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Cartographer Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Cartographer Spells:
Artificer Level | Spells
3 | Faerie Fire, Guiding Bolt, Healing Word
5 | Locate Object, Mind Spike
9 | Clairvoyance, Haste
13 | Freedom of Movement, Locate Creature
17 | Scrying, Teleportation Circle

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 6

feature.name: Level 3: Adventurer's Atlas (Cartographer)
feature.text:
Whenever you finish a Long Rest while holding Cartographer's Tools, you can use that tool to create a set of magical maps by touching at least two creatures (one of whom can be yourself), up to a maximum number of creatures equal to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum of two creatures).
	Each target receives a magical map, which is illegible to all others. The maps last until you die or until you use this feature again, at which point any existing maps created by this feature immediately vanish.
	While carrying the map, a target gains the following benefits.

Awareness: The target adds 1d4 to its Initiative rolls.

Positioning: The target knows the location of all other map holders that are on the same plane of existence as itself. When casting a spell or creating an effect that requires being able to see the target, a map holder can target another map holder regardless of sight, so long as the other map holder is still within the spell or effect's range.

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 7

feature.name: Level 3: Scouting Gadgets (Cartographer)
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

Boost: On your turn, you can expend half your movement to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of yourself. You can't use this benefit if your Speed is 0.

Radar: You can cast Faerie Fire without expending a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 7

feature.name: Level 5: Portal Jump (Cartographer)
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
	You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once).
	You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
	You can also use this ability without expending a use if the destination space is within 5 feet of a creature carrying a map created with your Adventurer's Atlas. Doing so destroys the map that creature carries.

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 7

feature.name: Level 9: Ingenious Movement (Cartographer)
feature.text:
When you use your Flash of Genius, you or a willing creature of your choice you can see within 30 feet of yourself can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see as part of that same Reaction.

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 7

feature.name: Level 15: Superior Atlas (Cartographer)
feature.text:
Your Adventurer's Atlas improves, gaining the following benefits.

Safe Haven: When a map holder is reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, that creature can destroy its map. The creature is then teleported to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you or another map holder of its choice and is Stable.

Unerring Path: If you are one of the map holders for your Adventurer's Atlas, you can cast Find the Path without expending a spell slot, without preparing the spell, and without needing spell components. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Unshakeable Mind: While at least one map created with your Adventurer's Atlas still exists, taking damage can't cause you to lose Concentration on your Artificer spells.

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 7

trait.name: Artificer
trait.text:
A Magical Crafter and an Inventor of Wonders

Masters of invention, Artificers use ingenuity and magic to unlock extraordinary capabilities in objects. They see magic as a complex system waiting to be decoded and then harnessed in their spells and inventions. You can find everything you need to play

Source:	UA2024-Eberron Updates p. 1

fields.name: Psion (UA) [5.5e]
fields.proficiency: Intelligence, Wisdom, Arcana, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Perception, Persuasion

feature.name: Becoming A Psion As A Level 1 Character
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Psion, you begin play with 6 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

Core Artificer Traits:
	• Primary Ability: Intelligence
	• Hit Point Die: D6 per Psion level
	• Saving Throw Proficiencies: Intelligence and Wisdom
	• Skill Proficiencies: Choose 2: Arcana, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Perception, Persuasion
	• Weapon Proficiencies: Simple weapons
	• Armor Training: None

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background (choose A or B):
	• (A) Spear, 2 Daggers, Light Crossbow, 20 Bolts, Case, Dungeoneer's Pack, and 6 GP
	• (B) 50 GP

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 1

feature.name: Becoming A Psion As A Multiclass Character
feature.text:
Core Artificer Traits:
	• Hit Point Die: D6 per Psion level

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 1

feature.name: Level 1: Psionic Power
feature.text:
You harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. This energy is represented by your Psionic Energy Dice. Your Psion level determines the die size and number of Psionic Energy Dice you have, as shown in the Energy Dice column of the Psion Features table.
	Your Psionic Energy Dice are used to enhance or fuel certain Psion features. You start with two such features: Telekinetic Propel and Telepathic Connection, each of which is detailed below. Some of your powers expend the Psionic Energy Dice, as specified in a power's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when all your Psionic Energy Dice are expended
	You regain one expended Psionic Energy Die when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all of them when you finish a Long Rest.
	Some features that use Psionic Energy Dice require your target to make a saving throw. The save DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

	Telekinetic Propel. As a Bonus Action, choose one Large or smaller creature other than you that you can see within 30 feet of yourself. When you do so, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be moved 5 feet straight toward you or straight away from you. Alternatively, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die when you take this Bonus Action, and the distance moved is equal to 5 times the number rolled. The die is expended only if the target fails the saving throw.

	Telepathic Connection. You have telepathy with a range of 30 feet. As a Bonus Action, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die. For the next hour, the range of your telepathy increases by a number of feet equal to 10 times the number rolled. The first time you use this Bonus Action after each Long Rest, you don't expend the Psionic Energy Die. All other times you use this feature, you expend the die.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 2

feature.name: Level 1: Spellcasting
feature.text:
You have learned how to channel magical energy using the power of your mind. See the Player's Handbook for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Psion spells, which appear in the Psion spell list later in the class's description.

	Cantrips. You know two Psion cantrips of your choice. Minor Illusion and Telekinetic Fling are recommended.
	Whenever you gain a Psion level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Psion cantrip of your choice.
	When you reach Psion levels 4 and 10, you learn another Psion cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Psion Features table.

	Spell Slots. The Psion Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

	Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 Psion spells. Charm Person, Command, Dissonant Whispers, and Mage Armor are recommended.
	The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Psion levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Psion Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Psion spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Psion, your list of prepared spells can include six Psion spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.
	If another Psion feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Psion spells for you.

	Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Psion level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Psion spell of an eligible level.

	Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Psion spells.

	Psionic Spellcasting. When you cast a Psion spell, that spell doesn't require a Verbal or Material component, even if the spell includes "V" or "M" in its "Components" entry, except Material components that are consumed by the spell or have a cost specified in the spell.

Spells Prepared:
Level | Prepared Spells
1 | 4
2 | 5
3 | 6
4 | 7
5 | 9
6 | 10
7 | 11
8 | 12
9 | 14
10 | 15
11 | 16
12 | 16
13 | 17
14 | 17
15 | 18
16 | 18
17 | 19
18 | 20
19 | 21
20 | 22

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 3

feature.name: Level 1: Subtle Telekinesis
feature.text:
You know the Mage Hand cantrip. You can cast it without Somatic components, and you can make the spectral hand Invisible when you cast it.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 3

feature.name: Level 2: Psionic Discipline
feature.text:
You learn further psionic techniques that are fueled by your Psionic Energy Dice. You gain two disciplines of your choice, such as Expanded Awareness and Id Insinuation. Disciplines are described in the "Psion (UA) [5.5e]: Psionic Discipline Options" spell list.
	You can use only one Discipline each turn and only once per turn unless otherwise noted in one of those options.
	Whenever you gain a Psion level, you can replace one of your Psionic Discipline options with one you don't know. You gain one additional option at Psion levels 5, 10, 13, and 17.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 3

feature.name: Level 3: Psion Subclass
feature.text:
You gain a Psion subclass of your choice. The Metamorph, Psykinetic, and Telepath subclasses are detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Psion levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Psion level or lower.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Psion levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 5: Psionic Discipline Improvement (1)
feature.text:
You gain one additional Psionic Discipline at Psion level 5.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 3

feature.name: Level 5: Psionic Restoration
feature.text:
You can perform a meditation that focuses the mind for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Psionic Energy Dice. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 7: Psionic Surge
feature.text:
You can push your psionic powers using your life force. After you roll one or more Psionic Energy Dice, you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice and treat any roll of 1, 2, or 3 on those Psionic Energy Dice as a 4.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 8: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 10: Psionic Discipline Improvement (2)
feature.text:
You gain one additional Psionic Discipline at Psion level 10.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 3

feature.name: Level 12: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 13: Psionic Discipline Improvement (3)
feature.text:
You gain one additional Psionic Discipline at Psion level 13.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 3

feature.name: Level 16: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 17: Psionic Discipline Improvement (4)
feature.text:
You gain one additional Psionic Discipline at Psion level 17.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 3

feature.name: Level 18: Psionic Reserves
feature.text:
When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Psionic Energy Dice until you have four if you have fewer than that.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 19: Epic Boon
feature.text:
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Energy Resistance is recommended.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Level 20: Enkindled Lifeforce
feature.text:
You burn your life force to achieve greater psionics. Once per turn, when you roll one or more Psionic Energy Dice for a Psion feature or Psionic Discipline, you can expend one or two of your Hit Point Dice. For each Hit Point Die expended, roll an additional Psionic Energy Die and add the numbers rolled to the total. This roll does not expend the Psionic Energy Die.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 4

feature.name: Psion Subclass: Metamorph
feature.text:
Psychically Sculpt Life and Flesh

Your mastery of psionic powers turns inward. Your own flesh becomes like clay to you, and you mold it into the perfect vessel for your psionic powers. Experience in manipulating your life energy also enables you to adjust the life force of friends and foes.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 7

feature.name: Level 3: Metamorph Spells (Metamorph)
feature.text:
When you reach a Psion level specified in the Metamorph Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared

Metamorph Spells:
Psion Level | Spells
3 | Alter Self, Cure Wounds, Inflict Wounds, Lesser Restoration
5 | Aura of Vitality, Haste
7 | Polymorph, Stoneskin
9 | Contagion, Mass Cure Wounds

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 7

feature.name: Level 3: Mutable Form (Metamorph)
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can expend one Psionic Energy Die to psionically stretch your limbs for 1 minute. Roll the expended Psionic Energy Die and gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 Temporary Hit Point). In addition, you gain the following benefits while this feature is active.

	• Reach. Your reach increases by 5 feet.

	• Speed. Your Speed increases by 5 feet.

	• Touch. When you cast a spell that has a range of Touch and a casting time of an action, you can make the spell's range 10 feet.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 7

feature.name: Level 3: Organic Weapons (Metamorph)
feature.text:
You can shape your limbs into weapons. As a Magic action, you can reform your free hand into one of the following organic weapons: Bone Blade, Flesh Maul, or Viscera Launcher. When you take the Attack action, you can use this feature before you make the attack roll. Your limb retains the form of the organic weapon until you take a Magic action to change it into another organic weapon, you have the Unconscious condition, or you return the limb to its previous form (no action required).
	Whenever you attack with the weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 3: Organic Weapons: Bone Blade (Metamorph)
feature.text:
A blade made of bone springs from your forearm or extends from your hand. The blade counts as a Simple Melee weapon with the Finesse property, and it deals 1d8 Piercing damage on a hit. You have Advantage on the attack roll you make with the blade if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 3: Organic Weapons: Flesh Maul (Metamorph)
feature.text:
Your fist and forearm coalesce into a hardened mass of flesh and bone. The maul counts as a Simple Melee weapon and deals 1d10 Bludgeoning damage on a hit. A creature hit by the maul has Disadvantage on the next Strength or Constitution saving throw it makes before the start of its next turn.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 3: Organic Weapons: Viscera Launcher (Metamorph)
feature.text:
Viscera Launcher. Your hand and forearm transform into a crossbow made of muscle and sinew that fires bolts of bile. The launcher counts as a Simple Ranged weapon with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 90 feet, and it deals 1d6 Acid damage on a hit. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using the launcher, you can deal an extra 1d6 Acid damage to the target.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 3: Extend Limbs (Metamorph)
feature.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can expend one Psionic Energy Die. For the next minute, you gain the following benefits.

	Reach. Your reach increases by 5 feet.

	Speed. Your Speed increases by 5 feet.

	Touch. When you cast a spell that has a range of Touch and a casting time of an action, you can make the spell's range 10 feet.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 6: Extra Attack (Metamorph)
feature.text:
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
	In addition, you can cast one of your Psion cantrips that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 6: Flesh Weaver (Metamorph)
feature.text:
When you use Mutable Form, you can expend an additional Psionic Energy Die to gain the following benefits while the feature is active.

	Organic Defense. You gain a +2 bonus to AC.

	Empowered Healing. When you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points to one or more creatures, you can expend one Psionic Energy Die, roll it, and add the number rolled to the number of Hit Points regained.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 10: Improved Mutable Form (Metamorph)
feature.text:
When you use Mutable Form, the duration increases to 10 minutes and you gain one of the following benefits of your choice, the effects of which last until Mutable Form ends.

	Stony Epidermis. You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration. In addition, choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Poison, Slashing, or Thunder. You gain Resistance to the chosen damage type.

	Superior Stride. While you aren't wearing armor, you can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action, and you have a Climb Speed and Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

	Unnatural Flexibility. You gain a +1 bonus to AC, and your body—along with any equipment you're wearing or carrying—becomes pliable. You can move through any space as narrow as 1 inch, and you can spend 5 feet of movement to escape from nonmagical restraints or end the Grappled condition.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Level 14: Life-bending Weapons (Metamorph)
feature.text:
Your weapon becomes wreathed in negative energy, and you radiate lite-mending psionic energy. When you hit a target with an attack roll using your Organic Weapon, roll one Psionic Energy Die. The target takes extra Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled. This roll doesn't expend the die.
	Alternatively, when you hit a creature with your Organic Weapon, you can instead expend one Psionic Energy Die and roll it. The target takes extra Necrotic damage equal to the roll, and each creature of your choice in a 30-foot Emanation originating from you regains Hit Points equal the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 8

feature.name: Psion Subclass: Psykinetic
feature.text:
Mold Psionic Force for Creation and Destruction

A Psykinetic controls their psionic powers like a malleable force. They bend their telekinetic energies into sturdy barriers and strike with the force of a battering ram.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 3: Psykinetic Spells (Psykinetic)
feature.text:
When you reach a Psion level specified in the Psykinetic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Psykinetic Spells:
Psion Level | Spells
3 | Cloud of Daggers, Levitate, Shield, Thunderwave
5 | Slow, Telekinetic Crush
7 | Otiluke's Resilient Sphere, Stone Shape
9 | Telekinesis, Wall of Force

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 3: Stronger Telekinesis (Psykinetic)
feature.text:
When you cast Mage Hand, its range increases by 30 feet when you cast it, and the hand can carry up to 20 pounds.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 3: Telekinetic Techniques (Psykinetic)
feature.text:
When you use Telekinetic Propel, you can roll 1d4 and use the number rolled instead of expending a Psionic Energy Die.
	In addition, when a target fails the saving throw against your Telekinetic Propel, you can impose one of the following effects on that target.

	Boost. The target's Speed increases by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

	Disorient. The target can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn.

	Telekinetic Bolt. The target takes Force damage equal to the number rolled on the Psionic Energy Die.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 6: Destructive Trance (Psykinetic)
feature.text:
At the start of your turn, you can expend one Psionic Energy Die to enter a destructive state. For the next 10 minutes, you gain a Fly Speed of 20 feet and can hover, and when you cast a Psion spell that expends a spell slot, you can roll your Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to one damage roll of that spell. This roll doesn't expend the Psionic Energy Die.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 6: Rebounding Field (Psykinetic)
feature.text:
When you cast Shield in response to being hit by an attack roll and cause the triggering attack to miss, you can expend one Psionic Energy Die to launch the force back at the attacker. The attacker makes a Dexterity saving throw. Roll one Psionic Energy Die. On a failed save, the attacker takes Force damage equal to the amount rolled plus your Intelligence modifier. On a successful save, the attacker takes half as much damage only. Whether the target fails or succeeds on the saving throw, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the amount of damage dealt.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 10: Enhanced Telekinetic Crush (Psykinetic)
feature.text:
When you cast Telekinetic Crush, you can expend one Psionic Energy Die to modify the spell so that whether a creature fails or succeeds on the saving throw against the spell, its Speed is halved until the start of your next turn. In addition, you can roll the expended Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to one damage roll of the spell.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Level 14: Heightened Telekinesis (Psykinetic)
feature.text:
You can cast Telekinesis without expending a spell slot by instead expending four Psionic Energy Dice. When you cast Telekinesis without expending a spell slot using this feature, you can modify the spell so that it doesn't require Concentration. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting, and you can target Gargantuan creatures and objects.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 9

feature.name: Psion Subclass: Telepath
feature.text:
Master Tactics in the Landscape of the Mind

Telepaths are masters of mind magic. They use their psionic powers for all matters of the mind, whether they bolster the mental defenses of allies or probe the thoughts of others undetected. A telepath can be a bastion of psionic aid or a crafty manipulator.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 10

feature.name: Level 3: Mind Infiltrator (Telepath)
feature.text:
When you cast Detect Thoughts, you can expend one Psionic Energy Die to modify the spell so that the spell doesn't require spell components or Concentration. In addition, when you use the Read Thoughts effect of the spell, the target doesn't know you're probing its mind if it fails the Wisdom saving throw.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 10

feature.name: Level 3: Telepath Spells (Telepath)
feature.text:
When you reach a Psion level specified in the Telepath Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Telepath Spells:
Psion Level | Spells
3 | Bane, Command, Detect Thoughts, Mind Spike
5 | Counterspell, Slow
7 | Compulsion, Confusion
9 | Modify Memory, Yolande's Regal Presence

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 10

feature.name: Level 3: Telepathic Distraction (Telepath)
feature.text:
When a creature you can see within range of your telepathy hits with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to roll one Psionic Energy Die and subtract the number rolled from attack roll, potentially causing the attack to miss. The die is expended only if the target misses the attack.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 10

feature.name: Level 6: Bulwark Mind (Telepath)
feature.text:
At the start of your turn, you can expend one Psionic Energy Die to strengthen your mind and enter a fortified state. For the next 10 minutes, you have Resistance to Psychic damage; and whenever you make an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you add a roll of your Psionic Energy Die to the save. Rolling the Psionic Energy Die doesn't expend it. You can't use this benefit if you have the Incapacitated condition.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 10

feature.name: Level 6: Potent Thoughts (Telepath)
feature.text:
You have telepathy with a range of 60 feet. In addition, you add your Intelligence modifier to the damage you deal with any Psion cantrip.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 10

feature.name: Level 10: Telepatic Bolstering (Telepath)
feature.text:
When you or a creature you can see within range of your telepathy fails an ability check or misses with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend one Psionic Energy Die. Roll the die and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning a failed check into a success or a miss into a hit. The Psionic Energy Die is expended only if the check succeeds or the attack hits.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 10

feature.name: Level 14: Scramble Minds (Telepath)
feature.text:
You can cast Confusion without expending a spell slot by instead expending four Psionic Energy Dice. When you cast Confusion without a spell slot using this feature, you can modify the spell so that the radius of the spell's Sphere becomes 30 feet and you can choose one creature you can see in the spell's area to automatically succeed on their saving throw against the spell.
	In addition, when a creature under the effect of the spell starts its turn, you choose their behavior from the table for the turn instead of the creature rolling to determine its behavior.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 10

trait.name: Psion
trait.text:
A Master of Psionic Power

Psions wield magic and extraordinary powers through the power of thought. They develop their minds as fonts of power that manifest spells and grow stronger over the course of their adventuring careers. You can find everything you need to play one of these psionic powerhouses in the next few sections.

Source:	UA2025-PsionUpdate p. 1

trait.name: What Is a Psion?
trait.text:
Psions are spellcasters who use innate mental powers to gain extraordinary abilities and unleash the magic of their minds. Psions and their magic (sometimes called "psionics") can trace their history back to the appendix of the first edition Player's Handbook, and a psionicsusing class first appeared in The Complete Psionics Handbook in 1991. Psionics have taken numerous forms in D&D, from alternative magic systems to options that dovetail with other D&D rules. In the fifth edition, psychic power is synonymous with magic, and the magic of the mind flavors numerous spells, monsters, and subclasses-like the Psi Warrior Fighter and the Aberrant Sorcery Sorcerer in the Player's Handbook. In this edition, the Psion is a spellcaster who interfaces with magic and spellcasting similarly to other classes in the game.
	This UA provides the Psion with unique twists to spellcasting using Psionic Energy Dice and the Psionic Spellcasting feature, carving out a space to make the Psion stand out from its spellcasting peers.

fields.name: Alchemist (HB) [5.5e]
fields.proficiency: Constitution, Intelligence, Arcana, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival

trait.name: Alchemist
trait.text:
Often found cooped-up experimenting or scavenging for ingredients, the Alchemist is a student of the metaphysical essence of things, and is as curious as they are resourceful.

Playing an Alchemist:
This class grants you features to create a low defense, high damage and utility martial blaster.

Action: Utilize
Bonus Action (Set-Up): Catalyze
Movement: Far from enemies, but within throw range.
Reaction: Defensive features, such as Mind Over Matter.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 1 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Becoming An Alchemist As A Level 1 Character
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Alchemist, you begin play with 8 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

Core Alchemist Traits:
	• Primary Ability: Intelligence
	• Hit Point Die: D8 per Alchemist Level
	• Saving Throw Proficiencies: Constitution, Intelligence
	• Skill Proficiencies: Choose 3: Arcana, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Sleight of Hand, Survival
	• Weapon Proficiencies: Improvised and Simple weapons
	• Tool Proficiencies: Alchemist's Supplies
	• Armor Training: Light armor

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background (choose A or B):
	• (A) Alchemist's Fire, 5 GP of raw materials, Light Crossbow, 20 Bolts, Case, Padded Armor, 5 Flasks, Alchemist's Supplies, and an Explorer's Pack, and 5 GP
	• (B) 150 GP

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 1 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Becoming An Alchemist As A Multiclass Character
feature.text:
Core Alchemist Traits:
	• Hit Point Die: D8 per Alchemist level
	• Skill Proficiencies: one from Arcana, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Sleight of Hand, or Survival
	• Tool Proficiencies: Alchemist Supplies
	• Armor Training: Light armor

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 1 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 1: Alchemy
feature.text:
Your practice of alchemical research has trained you to use and create devastating concoctions.

	Formulae: Formulae are the recipes to Craft Alchemical Items with Alchemist's Supplies. You know the Formulae listed below, as well as two other Alchemical Items of your choice.

Acid
Alchemist's Fire
Antitoxin
Candle
Component Pouch
Oil
Perfume
Potion of Healing

	Learning Formulae: Whenever you gain an Alchemist Level, you learn the Formula for another Alchemical Item of your choice. If you find Formulae during your adventures, you can add them to the Formulae you know. You can also research a Potion or Alchemical Item to learn its Formula. Either way takes 2 hours of time spent with a set of Alchemist's Supplies. If the Item has a rarity of Common, the time required is doubled, and doubles again for each rank above Common.

	Craft Discount: You only need to provide 5 GP worth of raw materials to Craft any item worth 50 GP or less that you know how to Craft with Alchemist's Supplies, and can Craft these items in 1 day, rather than their purchase price divided by 5.

	Item Attacks: Whenever you attack with Alchemical Items, you can use your Intelligence modifier for the DC instead of using Dexterity. Further, the range you can throw them is doubled and being within 5 feet of the target does not impose Disadvantage on the D20 Test.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 1 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 1: Catalyze
feature.text:
On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a Bonus Action: Study or Utilize to use an Item that normally calls for an Action.
	Whenever you take the Utilize Action while holding Alchemist's Supplies in-hand, you can create any of the items you can Craft with them, ignoring the Time requirement. Items created this way only last for 1 minute, then lose their potency.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 1 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 2: Methodical
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

	Experimentalist. Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in those skills.

	Fast Hands. You can draw or store two items during your Free Interaction, rather than one.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 1 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Alchemist Subclass
feature.text:
You gain an Alchemist Subclass of your choice, detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Alchemist levels.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Alchemist levels 8, 12, and 16.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 5: Eureka
feature.text:
You can use the Bonus Action granted by Catalyze to Craft a Potion with a rarity of Common that you know the Formula for, which otherwise follows the same rules for Catalyze.
	Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a Long Rest. The rarity increases as you gain levels in this class, starting at 9th level (Uncommon) and again at 13th level (Rare).

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 5: Extra Attack
feature.text:
You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Subclass Feature
feature.text:
You gain a feature from your Alchemist Subclass.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 7: Mix
feature.text:
While you have two Alchemical Items or Potions in hand and neither is the same item, you can use the Bonus Action granted by Catalyze to swiftly, and safely, combine them. When used, both effects occur simultaneously. Attempting to use this feature with an Item previously combined by this feature results in both items losing their potency and being destroyed.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 8: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 9: Eureka (Uncommon)
feature.text:
The rarity of the Potion you can create with your Eureka feature increases to Uncommon.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 9: Mercurial Flux
feature.text:
Items you Craft with Catalyze now last for 1 hour before losing their potency.
	Further, you can replace the raw materials to Craft Alchemical Items you know the Formula for with valuables (such as GP) of a value equal to or greater than the cost of the raw materials.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Subclass Feature
feature.text:
You gain a feature from your Alchemist Subclass.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 11: Volatile Potency
feature.text:
When a damage or healing roll is made with an Alchemical Item or Potion you Craft, you can roll 1d6 and add the result to the damage or healing of the item. This increases to 2d6 when you reach 17th level.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 12: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 13: Eureka (Rare)
feature.text:
The rarity of the Potion you can create with your Eureka feature increases to Rare.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 13: Mind Over Matter
feature.text:
When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you fails an ability check or a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to add a bonus to the roll, potentially causing it to succeed. The bonus equals your Intelligence modifier.
	You can take this Reaction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Subclass Feature
feature.text:
You gain a feature from your Alchemist Subclass.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 15: Philosopher's Stone
feature.text:
Your studies have revealed to you the mystic Formula for the legendary Philosopher's Stone, which you can create over the course of 7 days. If you create a new one, any of your previous Philosopher's Stones are destroyed and return to nothing. Your Philosopher's Stone grants you the following benefits.

	• You are Immune to Magical Contagions and Curses, and cannot be aged by natural or magical means.

	• Once per hour, you can use the Utilize Action to Craft an item worth 50 GP or less without materials.

	• You can allow it to replace any of the material components called for by a spell, which consumes the Philosopher's Stone in the casting.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 16: Ability Score Improvement
feature.text:
You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 17: Volatile Potency Enhancement
feature.text:
The damage and healing bonus from your Volatile Potency feature increases to 2d6.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 18: Lightning in a Bottle
feature.text:
Once every 7 days, you can create a Potion with your Eureka feature with a rarity of Very Rare.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 19: Epic Boon
feature.text:
You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 20: Big Bang
feature.text:
When you roll for Initiative, you can use the Utilize and Attack action once (no Action required).

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 2 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Alchemist Subclass: Animator
feature.text:
Crafter of Life

An Animator repurposes living matter to create living creatures that serve them. They are creators of constructs, often found with the animator serving as an assistant in their research.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 3 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Homunculus Companion (Animator)
feature.text:
You can conduct a Ritual over the course of an hour, shaping a mixture of 25 GP worth of clay, ash, mandrake root, and blood to gain the service of an Alchemical Homunculus.
	Your Alchemical Homunculus is a faithful companion, and it dies if you die. You determine its appearance. See this creature's game statistics in the Alchemical Homunculus stat block.
	In combat, it shares your Initiative count, but takes its turn immediately after yours. It is Friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your telepathic commands (no Action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the Dodge action and uses its move to avoid danger.
	If you are Incapacitated, it can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.
	You can't have more than one Homunculus from this feature at a time. If you attempt to create another, the creation fails.

Alchemical Homunculus:
Tiny Construct, Shares Your Alignment
AC 12 + your Intelligence modifier
HP 5 plus 5 times your Alchemist Level (it has a number of Hit Point Dice [d4s] equal to your Alchemist Level)
Speed 30 ft.
Str 14 (+2), Dex 14 (+2), Con 15 (+2), Int 10 (+0), Wis 12 (+1), Cha 10 (+0)
Immunities Poison; Exhaustion, Poisoned
Senses Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 10
Languages Understands the languages you know; telepathy 30 ft.

Traits:
Evasion. If the homunculus is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, the homunculus instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it has the Incapacitated condition.

Actions:
Bite. Melee Attack Roll: +2 plus your Intelligence modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: 1 Piercing damage, and the target is Poisoned for 1 minute. If the attack roll exceeds the target's Constitution score by 5 or more, the target falls Unconscious until it takes damage or another creature uses an Action to shake it awake.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 3 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Zoetic Theory (Animator)
feature.text:
You can give your Homunculus materials of a value of at least 5 GP to absorb into its body during a Short or Long Rest. For each component used, the Alchemical Homunculus gains a benefit.

	Adder's Stomach. It gains a Spit Acid attack, a ranged weapon with a range of 30 feet that deals 1d6 + your Intelligence modifier Acid damage.

	Eagle's Eye. It gains proficiency with Perception checks and has Advantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks.

	Fur of Bat. While it doesn't have the Deafened condition, it has 30 feet of Blindsight.

	Leech. Its Bite attack damage increases to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier and, when it hits a creature that is not a Construct or Undead, it can spend and roll one of its Hit Dice to regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled.

	Spiderwebs. It gains a Climb Speed equal to its Walking Speed and can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 3 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Anima Profane (Animator)
feature.text:
You gain the ability to cast the Animate Dead spell, but only as a Ritual. The Skeleton or Zombie created through this Ritual has the following changes:

	• It is a Construct rather than an Undead.

	• Its Hit Point Maximum is increased by an amount equal to your Alchemist level.

	• It gains the Telepathic Bond feature of your Alchemical Homunculus.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 4 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Life Stitcher (Animator)
feature.text:
Your Zoetic Theory is enhanced.

	Adder's Stomach. Its Spit Acid damage increases to 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier.

	Eagle's Eye. It has Expertise in Perception checks while it doesn't have the Blinded condition.

	Fur of Bat. It does not provoke Opportunity Attacks while using its Fly Speed.

	Leech. Its Bite attack damage increases to 2d4 + your Intelligence modifier.

	Spiderwebs. Its Climb Speed increases by 10 feet.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 4 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Contemptible Chimera (Animator)
feature.text:
If your Homunculus and a Construct created with Anima Profane are within 5 feet of each other, you can use an Action to command them to merge, creating a Flesh Golem that you control, with the following changes:

	• It gains the Homunculus' Fly, Bite, Telepathic Bond, and any Traits and Actions through Zoetic Theory.

	• Its Hit Point Maximum is increased by an amount equal to your Alchemist level.

	• The Flesh Golem dies immediately if you die or create a new Construct from your Alchemist features.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 4 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Alchemist Subclass: Apothecary
feature.text:
Practitioner of Natural Medicine

While laughter might be the best medicine, it never cured Filth Fever. Apothecaries are medical practitioners, creating potent potions to cure what ails.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 4 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Holistic Medicine (Apothecary)
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

	Natural Medicine. You gain proficiency in the Medicine, Nature, or Survival skill (your choice), and you have advantage on any ability check you make to stabilize a creature with 0 Hit Points and to forage.

	Doctor's Tonic. You learn the Formula for Healing Draught or one Alchemical Item of your choice if you already know it.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 4 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Spagyric Theory (Apothecary)
feature.text:
When you create an item that restores Hit Points, you can infuse the item with at least 5 GP of any of the following materials to enhance it.

	Honeycomb. The consumer gains a bonus on Wisdom (Animal Handling) and Charisma checks made against Beasts equal to your Intelligence modifier for 1 hour.

	Powdered Gems. If the consumer has the Poisoned condition from an effect that a successful saving throw would end, it can immediately attempt the saving throw (no Action required).

	Powdered Silver. The consumer gains a d4 bonus to the next saving throw they make within the next minute.

	Troll's Blood. The consumer regains 1 Hit Point at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute, or until they take Acid or Fire damage (whichever comes first).

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 4 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Sweet Succor (Apothecary)
feature.text:
When a creature consumes an Alchemical Item or Potion you administer or Craft that restores Hit Points, the item's first healing roll gains a bonus equal to your Intelligence modifier.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 4 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Panacea (Apothecary)
feature.text:
Your Spagyric Theory is enhanced.

	Honeycomb. The item causes subtle changes in the consumer's scent. Animals are put at ease by the scent, granting the consumer a bonus on Wisdom (Animal Handling) and Charisma checks made against beasts equal to your Intelligence modifier for 1 hour and advantage on these checks.

	Powdered Gems. If the consumer is afflicted by any condition that a successful saving throw would end, it can immediately attempt the saving throw when the item restores its Hit Points (no Action required).

	Powdered Silver. The next time the consumer makes a saving throw within the next minute, they can roll a 2d4 and add the result rolled to the saving throw.

	Troll's Blood. The consumer regains 2 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute, and their severed body members (fingers, legs, tails, and so on) are restored after 2 minutes if the severed part is held to the stump.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 4 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Miracle Elixir (Apothecary)
feature.text:
When you create a Healing Draught or Potion of Healing of any type, you can infuse it with 300 GP worth of diamond dust. If you administer the draught to a creature that has died within the last hour, the creature returns to life with 1 Hit Point. Doing so can't return to life a creature that has died of old age, nor can it restore any missing body parts.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Alchemist Subclass: Crystallographer
feature.text:
Maker of Matter

Crystallography is the study of crystalline structures and the creation of matter from chemical compounds.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Crystalizer (Crystallographer)
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

	Jeweled Alchemy. You gain proficiency with Jeweler's Tools and learn the Formula for Frigid Azote, or another Alchemical Item if you already know it.

	Paralyzer. Whenever a creature makes an ability check or saving throw to end an effect caused by one of your Alchemical Items that reduced its speed, the creature must roll 1d4 and subtract the number rolled from the d20 roll.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Vitreus Theory (Crystallographer)
feature.text:
When you create an item that reduces Speed or that creates an object or structure (such as an Instant Wall), you can infuse the item with at least 5 GP of any of the following materials to enhance it.

	Banded Agate. The form of any structure created by using the item expands by 5 feet in one direction of your choice, provided the space it would enter is unoccupied.

	Carbon. Any object or structure created by using the item is hardened, giving it an AC equal to your Alchemy save DC and additional Hit Points equal to your Alchemist level.

	Cicada. For 1 minute, the target must make a Constitution saving throw at the start of each of its turns. On a failure, the creature must spend 2 feet of speed for every 1 foot it attempts to use a Walk or Climb speed. On a success, this effect ends.

	Obsidian. Each time the creature makes an ability check or saving throw against the Alchemical item or comes into contact for the first time on its turn with an object or structure created by the item, it takes 1d6 Piercing damage.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Sterner Stuff (Crystallographer)
feature.text:
You can use your Eureka feature to create a nonmagical crystal or gem of your choice. You can create this item using valuables (such as gold pieces) of a value equal to half the value of the item. The value of the item can't be more than 50 times your alchemist level, and disappears after a number of hours equal to your proficiency bonus.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Matter Maker (Crystallographer)
feature.text:
Your Vitreous Theory is enhanced.

	Banded Agate. The form expands by 10 feet instead.

	Carbon. Any object or structure created is Immune to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage other than from magic or Adamantine weapons.

	Cicada. The item also affects a creature's Fly and Swim speeds.

	Obsidian. The Piercing damage increases to 2d6.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Prima Materia (Crystallographer)
feature.text:
Any item you create with Sterner Stuff no longer disappears, and you can use Eureka to Craft a Spark of Creation and only need to provide 500 GP to do so.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Alchemist Subclass: Fulminare
feature.text:
Philosophers of Destruction

The process of creation must have its opposite, and Fulminares are the specialists of chaos and combustion.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Student of Destruction (Fulminare)
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

	Combuster's Vessels. You gain proficiency with Potter's Tools and you learn the Formula for Thunderstone, or another Alchemical Item if you already know it.

	Exploding Damage. Whenever you roll the highest value on any of the damage dice of an Alchemical Item, it deals one extra die of damage.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Phlogiston Theory (Fulminare)
feature.text:
When you create an item that deals damage, you can infuse the item with at least 5 GP of any of the following materials to enhance it.

	Nut Shells. The item sends a seismic shock, causing the ground within 10 feet of the area the item was thrown to become Difficult Terrain.

	Quartz. When a creature takes damage from the item, it becomes Dazed until the end of the turn. While Dazed, the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw before it makes an attack, or the attack misses. On a success, the target is no longer Dazed.

	Saltpeter. If it only targets a single creature, you can instead target a point within the same range. All creatures within 10 feet of the point are targeted by it.

	Powdered Arcane Focus. When it deals damage, roll a d6 and consult the following table to determine its Damage Type.

Powdered Arcane Focus:
d6 | Damage Type
1 | Cold
2 | Lightning
3 | Necrotic
4 | Psychic
5 | Radiant
6 | Force

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 5 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Hit the Deck (Fulminare)
feature.text:
When you are forced to make a Dexterity saving throw against an effect you can see and hear, you can use your Reaction to move up to half your Speed immediately before the effect occurs, potentially moving out of the area of danger.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 6 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Chemical Warfare (Fulminare)
feature.text:
Your Phlogiston Theory is enhanced.

	Nut Shells. The area of the effect increases to 15 feet and deals double damage to objects and structures.

	Quartz. The creature has Disadvantage on the Constitution saving throw to end the Dazed condition.

	Saltpeter. The area of the effect increases to 15 feet.

	Powdered Arcane Focus. When you roll on the table, roll 3d6 and choose one of the dice to use for the result instead.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 6 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Spontaneous Combustion (Fulminare)
feature.text:
Your Exploding Damage benefit of Student of Destruction is enhanced in the following way.

	Exploding Damage. Whenever you roll the highest value on any of the damage dice of an Alchemical Item, you can roll those dice an additional time and add the number rolled to the damage until that die doesn't roll its highest value.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 6 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Alchemist Subclass: Salbenist
feature.text:
Anointed Warriors of Oil

The title of Salbenist (literally "oil-user") is used by alchemists who wield blades coated in alchemical oil.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 6 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Oleic Arms (Salbenist)
feature.text:
You have the following benefits.

	Martial Training. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons that lack the Heavy or Two-Handed properties and training with Medium armor.

	Burning Blades. You learn the Formula for Bladefire Oil, or another Alchemical Item if you already know it.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 6 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Anointed Blade (Salbenist)
feature.text:
You can perform a Ritual over the course of 1 hour with a weapon you are proficient with and coat it with an oil. The oil is absorbed into the weapon, anointing it and granting you the following benefits until you perform this Ritual again.

	• Whenever you attack with the weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity; and you can use its Mastery Property.

	• As part of making an attack with it, you can will the oil absorbed into it to coat it. Doing so does not consume the oil, and the weapon remains coated until you dismiss it, it leaves your hand, or until you coat it with another oil.

	• Whenever you make a damage roll with it and roll the highest value on one of the damage dice, you can roll that die one additional time and add the number rolled to the damage.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 6 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: All-Consuming Flame (Salbenist)
feature.text:
Whenever you take damage of the same type dealt by the oil anointing your weapon, you can use a Reaction to reduce the damage you take to 0. If you do, you regain a number of Hit Points equal to the total damage reduced. If these Hit Points would exceed your Hit Point maximum, you can choose to instead gain the remainder as Temporary Hit Points.
	You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1), and you cannot do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 6 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Hallowed Warrior (Salbenist)
feature.text:
When you will the oil absorbed into your Anointed Blade to coat it, you can choose another Weapon Mastery Property. The weapon gains this other Weapon Mastery Property until you dismiss it, it leaves your hand, or until you coat it with another oil.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 7 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Soul of Cinder (Salbenist)
feature.text:
Whenever you make a damage roll for damage dealt with your Anointed Blade and roll the highest value on any of the dice, the attack's damage ignores Resistance and Immunity.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 7 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Alchemist Subclass: Toxicologist
feature.text:
Insidious Poisoners and Pathologists

A reviled trade in most societies, Toxicologists are alchemists that specialize in disease and poison.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 7 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Adulterated Alchemy (Toxicologist)
feature.text:
You gain the following benefits.

	Poisoner. You gain proficiency with the Poisoner's Kit and treat Poisons you create as Alchemical Items for the purposes of your Alchemist class features.

	Substance Savant. You have Advantage on ability checks to handle, harvest, or identify Poisons, and diagnose Magical Contagions.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 7 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 3: Fel Theory (Toxicologist)
feature.text:
When you Craft an item that inflicts the Poisoned condition or deals Poison or Necrotic damage, you can infuse it with at least 5 GP of any of the following materials to enhance it.

	Desecrated Water. Poison damage dealt by it becomes Necrotic damage.

	Eye of Newt. While the target is poisoned in this way, the target takes 1d6 Poison damage the first time it is hit with an attack each turn.

	Powdered Lead. The Poison becomes a powder that takes effect when inhaled.

	Valerian Root. Whenever the target Poisoned this way makes a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, it must subtract a d4 from the number rolled.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 7 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 6: Mithridatism (Toxicologist)
feature.text:
You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition on yourself, and you have Resistance to Poison damage.
	If another feature, item, or spell gives you Resistance to Poison damage, you can choose instead to gain one of the following benefits, which lasts for the duration listed in the effect (you choose when the effect takes place).

	• You are Immune to Poison damage.

	• You have Resistance to either Acid or Necrotic damage (choose one).

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 7 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 10: Malediction (Toxicologist)
feature.text:
Your Fel Theory is enhanced.

	Desecrated Water. Damage dealt by the item ignores Resistance to Necrotic damage.

	Eye of Newt. The damage increases to 2d6 Poison.

	Powdered Lead. The inhaler has a d4 penalty to the saving throw forced by the Poison.

	Valerian Root. The penalty increases to 2d4.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 7 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Level 14: Demon Core (Toxicologist)
feature.text:
Poisons you create have the following benefits.

	• They ignore Resistance to Poison damage.

	• Creatures with Immunity to Poison damage instead take half damage from the item instead of none.

	• They ignore Immunity to the Poisoned condition, with these creatures instead making the saving throw with Advantage.

Source:	The Alchemist Class p. 7 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Blood Hunter (Alt. LaserLlama) [5.5e]
fields.proficiency: Constitution, Charisma, Acrobatics, Arcana, Athletics, History, Insight, Nature, Investigation, Religion, Survival

feature.name: Starting Blood Hunter
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Blood Hunter, you begin play with 12 + your Constitution modifier hit points.

You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.

	• Armor: light armor, medium armor, shields
	• Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons
	• Tools: Alchemist's supplies
	• Skills: Choose 2 from Athletics, Acrobatics, Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Religion, Survival

You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

	• (a) a martial weapon or (b) two simple weapons
	• (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) hand crossbow and 20 bolts
	• (a) studded leather armor or (b) scale mail armor
	• alchemist's supplies and an explorer's pack

If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 5d4x10 gp to buy your equipment.

Source:	LaserLlama's Alternate Blood Hunter v2.1.2 p. 1 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Multiclass Blood Hunter
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose blood hunter as one of your classes.

Ability Score Minimum:
As a multiclass character, you must have at least the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a blood hunter.

	• Strength or Dexterity 13
	• Constitution 13

Proficiencies Gained:
When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of your new class's starting proficiencies, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a blood hunter.

	• Armor: light armor, medium armor, shields
	• Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons
	• Tools: alchemical supplies

Blood Hunter Multiclassing with Warlock:
If your blood hunter is part of the Order of Witch Knights and also has warlock levels, add one-third of your blood hunter levels (rounded down) to your warlock level and consult the warlock progression table in the Player's Handbook for total spell slots, cantrips known, and spell slot level.

You should consider aligning your Otherworldly Patron feature between both classes, but your DM might allow you to have two different patrons at their discretion.

Source:	LaserLlama's Alternate Blood Hunter v2.1.2 p. 1 (Homebrew)

feature.name: Multiclass Features
feature.text:
When you gain a new level in a class, you get its features for that level. You don't, however, receive the class's starting equipment, and a few features have additional rules when you're multiclassing: Channel Divinity, Extra Attack, Unarmored Defense, and Spellcasting.

Channel Divinity:
If you already have the Channel Divinity feature and gain a level in a class that also grants the feature, you gain the Channel Divinity effects granted by that class, but getting the feature again doesn't give you an additional use of it. You gain additional uses only when you reach a class level that explicitly grants them to you. For example, if you are a cleric 6/paladin 4, you can use Channel Divinity twice between rests because you are high enough level in the cleric class to have more uses. Whenever you use the feature, you can choose any of the Channel Divinity effects available to you from your two classes.

Extra Attack:
If you gain the Extra Attack class feature from more than one class, the features don't add together. You can't make more than two attacks with this feature unless it says you do (as the fighter's version of Extra Attack does).
	Similarly, the warlock's eldritch invocation Thirsting Blade doesn't give you additional attacks if you also have Extra Attack.

Unarmored Defense:
If you already have the Unarmored Defense feature, you can't gain it again from another class.

Spellcasting:
Your capacity for spellcasting depends partly on your combined levels in all your spellcasting classes and partly on your individual levels in those classes. Once you have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, use the rules below. If you multiclass but have the Spellcasting feature from only one class, you follow the rules as described in that class.

Spells Known and Prepared:
You determine what spells you know and can prepare for each class individually, as if you were a single-classed member of that class. If you are a ranger 4/wizard 3, for example, you know three 1 st-level ranger spells based on your levels in the ranger class. As a 3rd-level wizard, you know three wizard cantrips, and your spellbook contains ten wizard spells, two of which (the two you gained when you reached 3rd level as a wizard) can be 2nd-level spells. If your Intelligence is 16, you can prepare six wizard spells from your spellbook.
	Each spell you know and prepare is associated with one of your classes, and you use the spell casting ability of that class when you cast the spell. Similarly, a spellcasting focus, such as a holy symbol, can be used only for the spells from the class associated with that focus.
	If a cantrip of yours increases in power at higher levels, the increase is based on your character level, not your level in a particular class.

Spell Slots:
You determine your available spell slots by adding together all your levels in the bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, and wizard classes, half your levels (rounded down) in the paladin and ranger classes, and a third of your fighter or rogue levels (rounded down) if you have the Eldritch Knight or the Arcane Trickster feature.
